general.name: Chihuahua
general.shortDescription: The Chihuahua is a small, lively companion dog that barks often and bonds closely.
general.longDescription:
A Chihuahua stands 7 inches tall and weighs 5 pounds, with expressive eyes and a distinctive apple head. It belongs to the Companion group and has a smooth, straight single coat that comes in many colours and patterns. Grooming takes very little work, shedding is light and it hardly drools.
At home, a Chihuahua is lively, affectionate and playful with its family and likes spending time on a lap. It is cautious around strangers and gets on moderately well with other dogs. Because it barks readily and stays alert to what is going on around it, it makes a reliable watchdog. It isn't suited to children, as its small frame doesn't cope well with rough play.
This breed adapts well to city homes, though it needs more daily exercise than its size suggests. Steady activity and moderate mental stimulation help use up its energy. Training takes some consistency so it doesn't become too dominant. A Chihuahua has a lifespan of 15 years, so taking one on is a long commitment.

general.name: Siberian Husky
general.shortDescription: The Siberian Husky is a friendly, playful sled dog that needs plenty of daily exercise.
general.longDescription:
Originally bred to pull light sled loads over snow, the Siberian Husky is a nimble Working dog built for endurance. It stands 20 inches tall, weighs 50 pounds and has a lifespan of 13 years. Its almond-shaped eyes can be brown, blue or a mismatched pair.
The breed has a thick, straight, rough double coat that stays naturally clean with little dog odour, and it rarely drools. Grooming needs are light, though it sheds heavily, especially as the seasons change. Because it has very high energy and strong needs for mental stimulation, it belongs in an active household with time for vigorous daily exercise. Training takes moderate effort, and it adapts fairly well to different living situations.
A Siberian Husky is faithful, playful and unusually sociable. It gets along well with children, other dogs and strangers alike, which makes it a poor watchdog. Expect plenty of noise too, as this is a very vocal breed.

general.name: Yorkshire Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Yorkshire Terrier is a loving, vigilant companion dog with a long silky coat.
general.longDescription:
Originally bred to catch rats in mines and mills, the Yorkshire Terrier is now a Companion breed standing 8 inches tall and weighing 7 pounds. Its straight, glossy, silky single coat can grow to floor length and is often steel blue and golden tan. It sheds very little and rarely drools, though that long coat demands frequent grooming.
The Yorkshire Terrier keeps its terrier character: it is brave, tenacious and sometimes bossy. It is very affectionate and playful with its family, friendly towards strangers and good with children, while getting along moderately well with other dogs. Strong protective instincts and a tendency to bark make it an alert watchdog.
Because it adapts easily and learns quickly, it settles well into city living. It still needs plenty of daily exercise and mental stimulation to stay occupied, and it has a lifespan of 13 years.

general.name: French Bulldog
general.shortDescription: The French Bulldog is a quiet, playful companion dog with distinctive large bat ears.
general.longDescription:
The French Bulldog is a small, compact, muscular Companion dog recognised by its large bat ears. It stands 12 inches tall and weighs 25 pounds. Relative to other breeds, its lifespan is on the shorter side at 10 years.
Its short, smooth, straight single coat needs very little grooming, which keeps routine coat care simple. It sheds moderately and drools a moderate amount, which is worth knowing before you bring one home.
In temperament, the French Bulldog is happy, even-tempered and very playful. It is affectionate with its family, good with children and sociable with other dogs as well as strangers. Because it rarely barks and adapts easily to different living spaces, it fits well into flats and city homes.
This is an intelligent breed that is fairly easy to train and enjoys play along with moderate mental stimulation. It needs moderate daily exercise to stay content. The breed stays alert and has moderate watchdog instincts, so it notices what is going on around the home without barking constantly.

general.name: German Shepherd
general.shortDescription: The German Shepherd is a brave, confident herding dog that learns quickly.
general.longDescription:
The German Shepherd is an agile, muscular Herding breed known for its bravery, confidence and intelligence. It stands 25 inches tall and weighs 70 pounds, with smooth curves and a free, easy trot. Because it learns quickly and works reliably, it is used in herding, service work, police duties and military tasks.
Training a German Shepherd is straightforward, as it is eager to learn and picks up new tasks quickly. That intelligence comes with real daily demands, though. The breed needs vigorous physical exercise and plenty of mental stimulation every day. As long as those needs are met, it adapts easily to different homes and living environments.
At home, the German Shepherd is loyal, gentle, playful and very affectionate with its family, and it does well with children. It is moderately sociable with other dogs, while tending to stay aloof towards strangers. Combined with its courage and strong protective instincts, that reserve makes it a reliable guardian. Barking stays at a moderate level.
Its medium-length, straight, rough double coat sheds heavily, so owners should expect plenty of loose hair around the house. Routine grooming needs are light, and drooling is low. With a lifespan of 13 years, the German Shepherd suits an active owner who has the time to keep an attentive working dog occupied.

general.name: Labrador Retriever
general.shortDescription: The Labrador Retriever is an energetic, friendly Sporting dog that trains easily.
general.longDescription:
The Labrador Retriever is a sturdy, medium-sized Sporting dog that stands 25 inches tall and weighs around 70 pounds. Its short, smooth, straight double coat comes in yellow, black and chocolate. You'll also notice a gentle expression and a thick, tapering tail often called an otter tail.
At home, Labrador Retrievers are loving, playful and very adaptable. They get on well with children, other dogs and strangers, while staying moderately alert and barking an average amount. They are lively dogs with very high exercise needs, so activities like swimming and fetch suit them well. They also need plenty of mental stimulation, though training itself is straightforward.
Plan for heavy shedding from that double coat, even though it needs little regular grooming. Drooling is low. With a lifespan of 12 years, the Labrador Retriever fits best in an active household that has time for daily exercise, enjoys training and doesn't mind dealing with loose hair.

general.name: Dachshund
general.shortDescription: The Dachshund is a curious, vocal Hound with a long back, short legs and a bold personality.
general.longDescription:
The Dachshund is a small, bold Hound with a long back, short legs and an alert expression. It stands 7 inches tall, weighs 20 pounds and has a long lifespan of 15 years. The breed comes in standard and miniature sizes, with a fairly short, smooth, straight single coat in many colours and patterns. Shedding, grooming and drooling are all low.
Dachshunds are curious, lively and very affectionate with their families. They are playful, adaptable and sociable with other dogs and strangers, while getting along moderately well with children. They have moderate needs for exercise and mental stimulation. Even though they're always keen for an outing, they aren't built for strenuous activities like long-distance running or leaping.
This is a brave, watchful dog with strong protective instincts. It barks loudly and very often, using its voice to alert the household. Dachshunds are clever and independent, and while they can be a little stubborn, training is still fairly easy overall. They suit owners who want an affectionate, lively companion and don't mind plenty of noise.

general.name: Golden Retriever
general.shortDescription: The Golden Retriever is an intelligent, faithful Sporting dog from Scotland with a quiet, friendly nature.
general.longDescription:
The Golden Retriever is a medium-sized Sporting dog that originated in Scotland. It stands 25 inches tall and weighs around 65 pounds, with a broad head, friendly eyes and a smooth, powerful gait. Its medium-length double coat is wavy, silky and gold, with a feathery tail.
This is an intelligent, hardworking breed used in hunting and fieldwork. Golden Retrievers are versatile enough to take on other demanding jobs as well, including guiding blind people and search-and-rescue work.
At home, they are faithful, adaptable and very affectionate. They get on well with children, other dogs and strangers, and they rarely bark. Their protective instincts are moderate, though they stay outgoing and trusting in new situations. Training is straightforward, so they settle well into different lifestyles.
Exercise needs are moderate, so regular daily activity is enough for them. Mental stimulation is a bigger priority. They enjoy swimming, fetch and games that use their retriever instincts, and many keep a playful, puppyish streak well into adulthood.
Their silky double coat needs only occasional brushing, and drooling is low. Shedding is heavy, though, so expect plenty of loose hair at home. The average lifespan is 10 years, which is on the shorter side compared with other breeds.

general.name: Beagle
general.shortDescription: The Beagle is a curious, vocal Hound bred to hunt in packs and enjoy company.
general.longDescription:
The Beagle is a sturdy, solid Hound that stands 15 inches tall and weighs around 25 pounds. It has a broad head with large brown or hazel eyes and long, low-set ears. Its short, smooth, straight single coat comes in colours like red and white, lemon and tricolour.
Bred to hunt in packs, Beagles enjoy company and are very sociable with other dogs. They are also very child-friendly and adapt well to most homes. Family affection and friendliness towards strangers are both moderate, and their protective instincts are low.
This is a curious, happy and playful breed with high needs for both exercise and mental stimulation. They need plenty of playtime and daily activity to stay content. Expect a vocal dog too, as Beagles bark frequently, and training takes moderate patience and effort.
Day-to-day coat care is straightforward. Grooming needs are low, shedding is moderate and drooling is minimal. With a lifespan of around 13 years, the Beagle fits well in an active household that wants a lively, easygoing Hound and doesn't mind some noise.

general.name: Bulldog
general.shortDescription: The Bulldog is a relaxed, friendly Companion dog with a muscular, low-slung build.
general.longDescription:
The Bulldog is a brave, relaxed Companion dog with a solid, muscular, low-slung build. It stands 15 inches tall and weighs around 45 pounds. For all its serious, dignified bearing, it is a friendly, loyal breed.
You can recognise one straight away by its loose head skin, furrowed brow, small ears, pushed-in nose and undershot jaw with hanging chops. It walks with a rolling gait. The short, smooth, straight single coat is glossy and comes in many colours and patterns.
At home, Bulldogs are affectionate with their families and friendly towards strangers. They do moderately well with children and other dogs, and their protective instincts sit in the middle. Adaptability is average too, though they can live in either town or country homes. Barking stays low.
Exercise and mental stimulation needs are moderate. A Bulldog enjoys brisk walks as much as curling up in your lap. Because of their short snouts, they need a cool environment during hot weather to avoid breathing difficulties.
Being easygoing and docile doesn't mean they are lazy. Bulldogs are quite playful, and they need regular activity and a balanced diet to maintain their health. Training is fairly easy.
Grooming needs, shedding and drooling are all moderate. The breed's lifespan of 9 years is short compared with other dogs. For owners who can keep a dog cool in warm weather and stick to regular walks, the Bulldog is a calm, affectionate companion.

general.name: Miniature Poodle
general.shortDescription: The Miniature Poodle is a lively, clever companion dog with a curly coat that sheds little.
general.longDescription:
The Miniature Poodle is a small companion dog, standing 13 inches tall and weighing about 13 pounds. It has a single, curly coat with a rough texture that grows long, and it rarely drools. With a lifespan of 15 years, it lives longer than many other breeds. Underneath its dignified look is an athletic dog built for activity.
At home, the Miniature Poodle is affectionate, playful and very friendly with children. It greets strangers warmly too, though it is only moderately sociable with other dogs. It stays reasonably alert around the house and barks often, so expect a vocal dog.
Because this breed learns quickly, training usually goes smoothly. It picks up commands and tricks easily, and it needs plenty of daily mental stimulation to stay happy. Despite its small frame, it requires regular exercise too. It adapts well to different households once those demands are met.
Shedding is low, which cuts down on loose fur, but the coat still takes work. You'll need to groom it often to keep its long curls tidy. If you have time for daily exercise, training and regular grooming, the Miniature Poodle is a lively companion.

general.name: Australian Shepherd
general.shortDescription: Developed in California as a herding dog, the Australian Shepherd is smart, agile and energetic.
general.longDescription:
The Australian Shepherd was developed in California from European stock and has long been linked with cowboys. It is a medium dog, standing 20 inches tall and weighing 55 pounds, with a lifespan of 14 years. Its wavy, rough double coat is medium in length and can show blue or red merle patterns. It sheds moderately, needs little grooming and rarely drools.
This agile, rugged herder has a sharp gaze and a strong urge to round up birds, dogs and even children. It is playful and very friendly with children, while staying more measured in its affection at home and its interest in strangers or other dogs. It barks a fair amount and keeps a steady eye on its surroundings.
Training is straightforward because the breed learns fast, and it does well in obedience and agility sports. The real commitment is its daily workload. It needs heavy exercise and plenty of mental work, so a sedentary home won't suit it. Active owners who give it a job get a hardworking partner.

general.name: Great Dane
general.shortDescription: Standing 30 inches tall, the Great Dane is a reliable, affectionate guardian with strong protective instincts.
general.longDescription:
Known as the Apollo of Dogs, the Great Dane is a powerful breed that stands 30 inches tall and weighs around 145 pounds. Its short, smooth, straight single coat comes in several colours and patterns, including the black and white patchwork called harlequin. The coat sheds moderately and needs very little grooming, though this breed drools heavily.
At home, the Great Dane is reliable, tolerant and very affectionate with its family. It is playful and adaptable, while its size and strong protective instincts often deter intruders. It gets along reasonably well with children, strangers and other dogs, barks a fair amount and takes steady work to train.
Owning a Great Dane means planning for its space, exercise and health needs. This breed requires plenty of daily activity and mental stimulation. Its lifespan of 9 years is short compared with other breeds, which is worth weighing up before you commit.

general.name: German Shorthaired Pointer
general.shortDescription: Built for long days outdoors, the German Shorthaired Pointer is an athletic, friendly and obedient sporting dog.
general.longDescription:
The German Shorthaired Pointer, often called the GSP, is a medium sporting dog standing 25 inches tall and weighing around 60 pounds. It has dark, expressive eyes and a short, smooth, straight single coat in solid liver or liver and white patterns. Coat care is light because it needs minimal grooming, though it sheds moderately and drools a little. Its lifespan is 10 years, which is on the shorter side.
At home, this breed forms strong bonds and is very affectionate and friendly with children. It is playful, adaptable and sociable with both strangers and other dogs. Strong protective instincts make it a loyal watchdog, while its barking stays moderate.
Training usually goes smoothly because the German Shorthaired Pointer is obedient, eager to please and responds well to positive methods. Its biggest demand is daily activity. Both its exercise and mental stimulation needs are very high, backed by power, speed, agility and endurance. Running, swimming, organised dog sports and long days in the field or at the lake give it the work it needs to stay settled at home.

general.name: Shetland Sheepdog
general.shortDescription: Known as the Sheltie, the Shetland Sheepdog is a lively, affectionate and vocal Scottish herder.
general.longDescription:
The Shetland Sheepdog, often called the Sheltie, comes from Scotland's Shetland Islands. This small, agile herding dog stands 15 inches tall, weighs 20 pounds and lives around 13 years. Similar in look to larger Collies, it has a long, rough, straight coat with a dense undercoat in black, blue merle or sable with white markings. It rarely drools, sheds moderately and needs regular grooming.
At home, the Sheltie is happy, sensitive and deeply affectionate, and it picks up quickly on its family's mood. It is very playful, adapts easily and gets along well with children and other dogs. Around strangers, it is usually reserved. Strong protective instincts make it an alert watchdog, and it barks a great deal, so expect plenty of noise.
Because this breed learns so fast, training is straightforward, and many Shelties do well in obedience, agility and herding trials. It needs plenty of daily exercise and mental stimulation to stay settled. If you don't mind a vocal dog and routine coat care, the Shetland Sheepdog is a lively, devoted companion that likes being part of family life.

general.name: Standard Poodle
general.shortDescription: Athletic and easy to train, the curly-coated Standard Poodle needs daily exercise and frequent grooming.
general.longDescription:
The Standard Poodle belongs to the Companion group, stands about 15 inches tall and weighs around 55 pounds. It is a dignified, athletic dog with a long, rough curly coat and a lifespan of around 15 years.
This breed has a single coat that sheds very little, and Standard Poodles rarely drool. The catch is upkeep, because that curly coat needs frequent grooming to keep it in good condition.
At home, Standard Poodles are very affectionate and playful, and they do well with children. They are also very friendly towards strangers, though their sociability with other dogs is more moderate.
They have strong protective instincts and bark fairly often, so expect a watchful, vocal dog. Even so, they settle into most kinds of homes as long as their daily routine gives them enough to do.
Exercise needs are high for this athletic breed, and mental stimulation needs are even higher. Because they are intelligent and easy to train, Standard Poodles do well in obedience, agility, canine sports and service roles.
They suit people who enjoy teaching their dog new things and can keep up with frequent grooming and active days. With enough company and mental work, a Standard Poodle settles into family life well.

general.name: Shih Tzu
general.shortDescription: At 13 pounds, the silky-coated Shih Tzu adapts easily to apartment living and loves family company.
general.longDescription:
Often called the Lion Dog, the Shih Tzu is a small, sturdy member of the Companion group. It stands about 10 inches tall, weighs around 13 pounds and has a typical lifespan of 15 years. Its long, straight, silky double coat sheds very little and the breed rarely drools, though keeping that coat tidy takes frequent grooming.
Shih Tzus are happy, loving dogs that stay close to their families. They are very good with children and very sociable with other dogs, and moderately friendly with strangers. Protective instincts and barking are both moderate. Because they adapt very easily, they suit apartments and homes without large gardens, and they are content curled up beside you or soaking up attention.
Daily care outside grooming is manageable. A Shih Tzu has moderate exercise, play and mental stimulation needs, so regular everyday activity is usually enough to keep one content. The breed is fairly easy to train too. If you don't mind putting in time on coat care, you get a loving, adaptable housemate that fits comfortably into most households.

general.name: Rottweiler
general.shortDescription: Rottweilers are quiet, muscular Guardian dogs that protect their homes closely and stay affectionate with family.
general.longDescription:
The Rottweiler belongs to the Guardian group and traces its working heritage back to the mastiffs of the Roman legions. It is a large, muscular dog with thickly muscled hindquarters and a steady trot, standing about 25 inches tall and weighing around 105 pounds. Its short, smooth black coat has rust markings, and the breed lives for around 10 years.
Within its family, a Rottweiler is faithful, affectionate and playful, often forgetting its size to climb onto a lap. With strangers it tends to be self-assured and somewhat aloof, and it is moderately sociable with children and other dogs. Rottweilers are quiet dogs that rarely bark, though their protective instincts are very strong. Well-bred Rottweilers are steady and brave rather than needlessly aggressive.
Early training and socialisation are important to guide those protective instincts in the right direction. Rottweilers are easy to train, adaptable and have moderate exercise needs, but they require plenty of mental stimulation. Their single coat needs very little grooming, though you can expect moderate shedding and some drooling.

general.name: Staffordshire Bull Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Staffordshire Bull Terrier is a compact 30-pound dog, brave on watch and gentle with children.
general.longDescription:
The Staffordshire Bull Terrier, widely known as the Staffie, packs a muscular Terrier build into a compact 15-inch, 30-pound frame. You can recognise the breed by its short, broad head and pronounced cheek muscles, along with a short, smooth single coat that comes in a variety of colours. Most live for around 13 years.
Originally bred for courage and tenacity, the breed has left its brawling past behind through responsible breeding and is now a gentle, affectionate family dog. Staffies are especially patient with children and generally friendly towards strangers. They are still brave and strongly protective, so they make alert watchdogs and bark a moderate amount.
They adapt very easily to different homes, provided they get plenty of daily exercise and mental stimulation. Because they are intelligent, hardworking and easy to train, they pick things up quickly. Early socialisation is important, as their sociability with other dogs is moderate and they benefit from clear guidance on good manners.
Upkeep on their straight coat is light, with fairly low shedding and only occasional grooming. They do drool a moderate amount. For active owners who have time for regular exercise and early socialisation, the Staffordshire Bull Terrier is a playful, loyal housemate.

general.name: Belgian Malinois
general.shortDescription: Hardworking Belgian Malinois excel in police, military and obedience work when given daily exercise and training.
general.longDescription:
The Belgian Malinois is a confident, alert member of the Herding group, standing about 25 inches tall and weighing around 60 pounds. It has a typical lifespan of 15 years. Its short, smooth, straight single coat ranges from rich fawn to mahogany, with black ears, a black mask and dark chocolate-coloured eyes.
Hardworking and intelligent, this breed is very easy to train and eager to have a job. Belgian Malinois work in police and military roles, and they also take part in competitive obedience and agility. Their exercise and mental stimulation needs are both high. If they go without regular activity and engagement, behavioural issues can follow.
Strong protective instincts make the Belgian Malinois a reliable watchdog, and it barks a moderate amount. Around the house it is moderately affectionate and playful, and it adjusts reasonably well to different living setups. With children, strangers and other dogs, it tends to be neither overly outgoing nor overly wary. It suits active households that want a focused working partner.
Coat care is straightforward. The breed rarely drools, sheds a moderate amount and only needs light grooming. The real demand is your time, because a Malinois needs consistent training, daily exercise and steady mental challenges to stay settled at home.

general.name: Samoyed
general.shortDescription: The Samoyed is a friendly, vocal working dog from Siberia with a long, thick white double coat.
general.longDescription:
The Samoyed is a Working group dog from Siberia, originally bred for hard work in extreme cold. Adults stand about 20 inches tall, weigh around 50 pounds and live about 13 years. Their long, straight, silky double coat is all white. The upturned corners of their mouth give them a smiling expression, limit drooling and stop icicles forming on their face.
Around people, the Samoyed is affectionate, adaptable and playful. These dogs get on very well with families, children and strangers, and they do best with plenty of attention. With other dogs, they are moderately sociable, while at home they have strong protective instincts. Expect a noisy companion too, because they bark often.
Because they have high energy and high mental stimulation needs, they require plenty of daily exercise and varied activity. Training is fairly straightforward, though their clever, sometimes mischievous streak means they need consistent structure.
That dense white coat sheds a moderate amount and needs moderate grooming to stay in good shape. Active owners who don't mind a lot of barking get a loyal, loving dog.

general.name: Pembroke Welsh Corgi
general.shortDescription: The Pembroke Welsh Corgi is a small, muscular herding dog with strong protective instincts and high energy.
general.longDescription:
Built for hard work on short, powerful legs, the Pembroke Welsh Corgi is a small Herding group dog with a muscular body and deep chest. It stands about 10 inches tall, weighs around 30 pounds and typically lives about 13 years. The short, straight, rough double coat comes in red, sable, fawn or black and tan, with or without white markings.
These dogs are playful and very affectionate with their families without being overly needy, and they adapt well to different homes. They get on well with strangers and other dogs, though they are only moderately good with children. With sharp senses, strong protective instincts and a big bark, they make vigilant watchdogs and can be noisy.
Despite their small size, Pembroke Welsh Corgis are agile and need plenty of daily exercise, interactive play and mental stimulation. Bright and sensitive, they are fairly easy to train. Grooming needs are light and they hardly drool, though they shed heavily, so expect a lot of hair around the house.

general.name: Newfoundland
general.shortDescription: The Newfoundland is a large, quiet working dog that is tolerant and patient with children.
general.longDescription:
At about 25 inches tall and around 125 pounds, the Newfoundland is a powerfully built Working group dog with a thick, medium-length, rough, wavy double coat. That coat protects them in harsh climates and comes in grey, brown, black or the black-and-white Landseer pattern. Their lifespan is around 10 years, which is on the shorter side compared with other breeds.
Despite its size, the Newfoundland is sweet-tempered, loving and tolerant. These dogs form close bonds with their families and are patient and watchful with children, which earned them the nickname nanny dog. They are just as sociable with other dogs and friendly towards strangers. Even at 125 pounds, they adapt well to a range of living situations.
They have strong protective instincts and make watchful guardians, while staying calm and welcoming with people they meet. Barking is rare, so this is a very quiet breed around the house. Their needs for exercise, play and mental stimulation are all moderate. They enjoy interactive games and take a moderate amount of work to train, responding best to gentle, positive reinforcement.
The main practical trade-off is heavy drooling, which is a constant part of daily life with this breed. Their coat sheds a moderate amount, though grooming demands themselves are fairly light. If you can handle the size and the drool, the Newfoundland is a steady, faithful and loving dog.

general.name: Doberman Pinscher
general.shortDescription: The Doberman Pinscher is a sleek, vigilant guardian dog with very high energy.
general.longDescription:
The Doberman Pinscher is a sleek, compact Guardian group dog with a muscular build and a short, straight, smooth single coat. Coats come in black, blue, red or fawn, always with rust markings. Standing about 25 inches tall and weighing around 80 pounds, these dogs live roughly 10 years, a shorter lifespan than many breeds. Grooming needs are minimal and they drool very little, though they still shed heavily.
Brave and highly vigilant, the Doberman Pinscher has strong protective instincts and takes guarding seriously. At home, these dogs are faithful, playful and very affectionate with their families and children. They adapt well to different households and are generally friendly with strangers, though they are only moderately sociable with other dogs. Barking is moderate rather than constant.
Energy is the main commitment with this breed. They have very high exercise needs and high mental stimulation needs, so they do best with plenty of daily activity and engaging work. They are also bright and very easy to train, which helps active owners put all that energy to good use.

general.name: Bichon Frise
general.shortDescription: The Bichon Frise is a small, lively companion dog with a long, curly white coat.
general.longDescription:
A small, sturdy dog in the Companion group, the Bichon Frise stands about 10 inches tall, weighs around 15 pounds and has a long lifespan of about 15 years. Rounded hair on the head frames their large dark eyes, black nose and black lips. Their long, curly, rough white double coat sheds very little and they hardly drool, but keeping it in shape means very frequent grooming.
Curious, happy and playful, the Bichon Frise gets on well with almost everyone. They are very affectionate with families and children, sociable with other dogs and friendly towards strangers. Because their protective instincts are low, they are much more likely to greet a visitor than guard the house, though they bark a moderate amount. Confident and adaptable, they suit city living well.
Even at 15 pounds, these are lively dogs with high exercise demands, so they require plenty of daily activity and play alongside moderate mental stimulation. They are fairly easy to train and enjoy performing for their owners.

general.name: Maltese
general.shortDescription: The Maltese is a small, affectionate companion dog with a long, silky white coat.
general.longDescription:
Sometimes called 'Ye Ancient Dogge of Malta', the Maltese has kept people company since ancient times. A member of the Companion group, this small dog stands 8 inches tall and weighs 7 pounds. Beneath its long white coat of straight, silky hair sits a compact body with a smooth gait, along with big dark eyes and a black nose.
Maltese dogs are happy, loving and closely attached to their families. They adapt well to different homes and don't drool. Around children, strangers and other dogs, they're moderately friendly, and their playfulness sits in the middle as well. They're also hardy, alert watchdogs with a fearless streak, and they enjoy taking on agility courses.
Their single, floor-length white coat sheds very little. The trade-off is grooming, which needs frequent work to keep the silky hair in good condition. Daily exercise and mental stimulation needs are moderate. Training sits in the middle for difficulty, and they bark a moderate amount.
With a lifespan of 14 years, a Maltese is a long-lived companion. It's a good match for households that want an affectionate, adaptable small dog and have the time to keep up with its coat.

general.name: Miniature Schnauzer
general.shortDescription: The Miniature Schnauzer is a friendly, easily trained terrier with a wiry coat and bushy eyebrows.
general.longDescription:
Bred from the larger Standard Schnauzer, the Miniature Schnauzer is the smallest of the three Schnauzer breeds. It sits in the Terrier group, standing 13 inches tall and weighing 15 pounds. Originally used as an all-round farm dog and ratter, it is tough and fearless without being aggressive. Miniature Schnauzers are generally healthy and have a lifespan of 14 years.
Bushy eyebrows and a beard give this breed a human-like expression. Its rough, wiry double coat is medium in length and comes in salt and pepper, black and silver or solid black. It sheds a moderate amount and needs frequent grooming, while drooling stays low.
Miniature Schnauzers adapt easily to apartments or larger homes with land. They're very affectionate with their families and great with children, though only moderately sociable with strangers and other dogs. Intelligent and obedient, they're easy to train. They need moderate exercise alongside plenty of play and mental stimulation.
Plan for plenty of noise. Miniature Schnauzers bark frequently and have strong protective instincts, so they make alert watchdogs as well as lively house dogs.

general.name: West Highland White Terrier
general.shortDescription: The West Highland White Terrier is a playful, faithful small working terrier.
general.longDescription:
Often called the Westie, the West Highland White Terrier has been around for over 300 years. A member of the Terrier group, it stands 10 inches tall, weighs 18 pounds and has a lifespan of 15 years. It has a compact, sturdy body, dark eyes and a carrot-shaped tail. Its straight, medium-length double coat is all white and hard to the touch.
Bred to hunt rats and other underground rodents, this small terrier is tough and self-reliant. That working background gives it plenty of courage and an active, alert nature. For coat care, expect moderate shedding and moderate grooming, and it doesn't drool.
Westies are faithful and happy, with a very playful streak. They have high exercise needs and moderate mental stimulation needs, so daily activity matters. They're deeply affectionate with their families, great with children and friendly towards strangers, though more moderate with other dogs. They also adapt well to either an apartment or a house with a yard.
Their independent streak puts training in the middle for difficulty, so you'll need time and patience even though they're smart. Westies are also highly vigilant and bark a great deal, so be ready for a noisy, protective terrier.

general.name: Cocker Spaniel
general.shortDescription: Originally a hunting companion, the Cocker Spaniel is a sociable, affectionate dog with long ears.
general.longDescription:
The Cocker Spaniel belongs to the Sporting group and has a history as a hunting companion, though it settles easily into family life. Compact and sturdy, it stands 15 inches tall, weighs 25 pounds and has a lifespan of 12 years. Big, expressive eyes and long, silky ears give it a sweet expression. Its long double coat is wavy and silky, and it comes in a range of colours and patterns.
That long coat takes regular upkeep. Cocker Spaniels shed a moderate amount and need frequent grooming to keep their fur in good condition, though drooling stays low. Because they have high exercise needs, they do best with daily brisk walks alongside moderate play and mental stimulation. They're intelligent and fairly easy to train.
At home, Cocker Spaniels are happy and loving with their families. They're very good with children, get on very well with other dogs and are friendly towards strangers too. They adapt easily to different households. Barking and protective instincts both sit in the middle, so expect a dog that is moderately alert and moderately vocal.

general.name: Pug
general.shortDescription: The Pug is a playful, quiet companion dog with a wrinkled brow and a smooth, short coat.
general.longDescription:
The Pug belongs to the Companion group and has a history as a mischievous companion to Chinese emperors and the mascot of Holland's royal House of Orange. Standing 12 inches tall and weighing 15 pounds, it is a small, solid dog with a compact frame.
The breed's Latin motto, 'multum in parvo', means 'a lot in a little', which fits its substantial presence in a small body. Pugs come in three colours: all black, or silver or apricot-fawn with a black face mask. A large round head, bright eyes and wrinkled brows give them human-like expressions that shift from curiosity to surprise and happiness.
Pugs are very affectionate and thrive on human company, so they suit families, singles and seniors alike. They adapt easily to the city or the countryside. Very playful by nature, they're great with children, very friendly with strangers and sociable with other dogs and pets.
They need moderate exercise to stay healthy, along with moderate mental stimulation and regular playtime. Training is fairly easy. Their short, smooth single coat lies straight and takes little grooming, and they don't drool. The main chore is heavy shedding, which leaves a lot of hair behind. Pugs rarely bark and have moderate protective instincts.
With proper care and attention, a Pug has a lifespan of 15 years. It's a good fit for households wanting a quiet, affectionate house dog with minimal grooming needs, provided you're ready to deal with heavy shedding.

general.name: Boston Terrier
general.shortDescription: Nicknamed 'The American Gentleman' for its tuxedo coat, the Boston Terrier is playful and affectionate.
general.longDescription:
Nicknamed 'The American Gentleman' for its neat tuxedo markings, the Boston Terrier is a compact, sturdy companion dog with a square head, short muzzle and big, round eyes. Its short, straight, smooth single coat comes in white paired with black, brindle or seal, which is a dark brown.
This small, agile breed stands around 10 inches tall and weighs about 20 pounds, with a well-balanced build. Shedding is light and drooling is minimal, so keeping the coat tidy takes little more than an occasional brush.
Boston Terriers are playful, affectionate dogs with a lively sense of humour and a hint of mischief. They get along very well with children and strangers, and they are usually sociable around other dogs too. They rarely bark without reason, though they stay reasonably alert to what is going on around them.
Despite their small frame, they have plenty of energy and need brisk daily walks and active trips to the park. They are intelligent and fairly easy to train, with ordinary needs for mental games. Given enough exercise, they settle reasonably well into city homes and enjoy outings to outdoor cafes. Most Boston Terriers live around 12 years.

general.name: Bernese Mountain Dog
general.shortDescription: Bred for Swiss farm work, the Bernese Mountain Dog is a gentle, heavy-shedding family companion.
general.longDescription:
Built for hard work on the farms and pastures of Switzerland, the Bernese Mountain Dog handles cold weather easily. Its straight, rough, medium-length double coat is tricoloured in jet black, clear white and rust. At roughly 25 inches tall and 90 pounds, this is a big, strong working dog, and owners should expect heavy shedding, regular brushing and a fair bit of drool.
At home, Bernese Mountain Dogs are calm, brave and deeply affectionate. They love being close to their families and often form a particular attachment to one person. They are friendly and gentle with children, sociable with other dogs and generally welcoming towards strangers too. They stay alert to their surroundings without being constant barkers.
Outside, that relaxed indoor manner gives way to real energy, so they need plenty of daily exercise and enjoy a playful romp with their owners. They are eager to please and fairly easy to train, happy with ordinary training and play to keep their minds busy. Adaptable and steady, they fit well into active households, though their lifespan is short at around 9 years.

general.name: Pomeranian
general.shortDescription: At around 5 pounds, the Pomeranian packs a bold, vocal watchdog into a long coat.
general.longDescription:
Pomeranians are curious, lively little dogs with a brave streak that makes them quick to act as watchdogs. They are very protective of their home and bark often, alerting you to anything unusual. With their own families they are deeply affectionate and enjoy a bit of play, while around children, unfamiliar people and other dogs they tend to be polite rather than overly outgoing.
Long kept by royals and commoners alike, this tiny breed stands about 7 inches tall and weighs roughly 5 pounds. A foxy face with bright eyes sits framed by a long, straight, rough double coat that comes in nearly two dozen colours, most often orange or red. They shed lightly and barely drool, though that full coat needs regular brushing to stay in good shape.
Short outdoor walks and indoor play are enough to keep them happy, and they adapt well to both city and suburban homes. They are bright dogs that enjoy learning tricks and games. Training is middling in difficulty, so steady practice gets the best results. Most Pomeranians live a long life of around 15 years.

general.name: Weimaraner
general.shortDescription: Germany's silvery-grey Weimaraner is an athletic, easily trained hunting dog that thrives on heavy exercise.
general.longDescription:
With its sleek, silvery-grey coat, long velvety ears and amber or blue-grey eyes, the Weimaraner earned the nickname 'Grey Ghost' in its native Germany. This large, streamlined sporting breed reaches around 25 inches tall and weighs about 75 pounds. Its short, smooth, straight single coat sheds a fair amount, though drooling is light and occasional brushing is enough to keep it clean.
Bred for hunting, Weimaraners have very high demands for both daily exercise and mental work. They are obedient and very easy to train, taking readily to obedience work and dog sports. They adapt well to different households, provided they get the heavy physical activity and engagement they need to stay happy and healthy.
Once exercised, they show a gentle, deeply affectionate side and stay close to their families. They are playful, brave and great with children. Very strong protective instincts make them vigilant watchdogs, barking when something warrants it. They take a measured approach to strangers and other dogs, warming up in their own time. Most live around 12 years.

general.name: English Springer Spaniel
general.shortDescription: Happy, obedient and full of stamina, the English Springer Spaniel loves long days outdoors.
general.longDescription:
English Springer Spaniels are muscular bird dogs built for long days in the field, backed by strong stamina and a cheerful work ethic. They are happy, obedient and eager to please, which makes them very easy to train.
This medium-sized breed stands about 20 inches tall and weighs roughly 45 pounds, with long ears and a kind, trusting expression. Its wavy, silky, medium-length double coat comes in a range of colours and patterns. Grooming is light, though you can expect a fair amount of shedding and drool.
They are intelligent, playful dogs that welcome strangers and get on well with other dogs, while getting along reasonably well with children.
With high needs for both exercise and mental work, they enjoy long walks, swimming, chasing and fetching. Once those needs are met, they are polite and adaptable in different kinds of homes.
Many owners know them for switching easily between a calm house dog on weekdays and a dependable hunting partner at weekends. They are deeply affectionate, crave company and can become distressed if neglected.
They stay reasonably alert and bark now and then when something happens. With an average lifespan of about 13 years, they suit active households that can include them in daily life.

general.name: Dalmatian
general.shortDescription: The Dalmatian is an athletic, spotted working dog originally used to guard coaches.
general.longDescription:
Standing 20 inches tall and weighing 60 pounds, the Dalmatian is a medium-sized dog in the Working group. Its short, smooth, straight coat carries black or liver spots over a muscular frame built for endurance. The breed once worked as a coach dog, guarding horse-drawn rigs for nobles, gypsies and firefighters.
That background shows in a strong protective instinct, so Dalmatians make alert watchdogs. They are very affectionate at home, playful and friendly with strangers. They adapt well to different routines and do reasonably well with children and other dogs. Barking is moderate.
They need plenty of exercise and mental stimulation, so they suit runners, hikers and active households. Dalmatians are intelligent and fairly easy to train. Their short single coat needs little grooming, though they shed heavily. Drooling is light, and a Dalmatian typically lives around 12 years.

general.name: King Charles Spaniel
general.shortDescription: The King Charles Spaniel is a small, affectionate companion dog suited to families.
general.longDescription:
The King Charles Spaniel belongs to the Companion group, pairing a toy breed's focus on people with sporting spaniel athleticism. At 13 inches tall and 15 pounds, it is a small dog with large, round eyes and a calm expression. Its medium-length single coat is silky and wavy.
Sociability is this breed's strongest point. King Charles Spaniels are very affectionate with their families, great with children and happy around other dogs. Most are friendly with strangers too. They are moderately adaptable and moderately playful, glad to chase squirrels outside or settle next to you on the sofa. Watchfulness and barking both sit around the middle.
Day-to-day care is straightforward. They need moderate daily exercise and mental stimulation, and their even temper makes training fairly easy. Grooming, shedding and drooling are all low, so upkeep stays manageable. With a lifespan of 14 years, the King Charles Spaniel lives longer than many breeds and suits households looking for a dignified, loving companion.

general.name: Border Collie
general.shortDescription: The Border Collie is an energetic, intelligent herding dog that needs plenty of daily work.
general.longDescription:
Part of the Herding group, the Border Collie is a muscular, nimble dog standing 20 inches tall and weighing 45 pounds. It has a lifespan of 14 years and suits owners with the time and energy to keep a driven dog occupied.
Border Collies have intense, almond-shaped eyes and the fixed stare known as the herding eye. Their rough, wavy double coat is medium in length and comes in various colours and patterns. Shedding and grooming are moderate, and they don't drool.
They are very easy to train and do well in herding, agility and obedience. At home, they are very affectionate, playful and adaptable, happy to cuddle after a busy day. They are friendly with strangers and moderate with children and other dogs, though they can be noisy.
Exercise and mental stimulation needs both sit at the top of the scale. Protective instincts are moderate, while energy stays high throughout the day. Active families willing to provide daily exercise and mental engagement will find the Border Collie a lively, loving dog.

general.name: Boxer
general.shortDescription: The Boxer is a lively, muscular working dog, protective at home and gentle with children.
general.longDescription:
The Boxer is a muscular, agile dog in the Working group, standing 25 inches tall and weighing 65 pounds. Its short, smooth single coat is straight and comes in fawn or brindle with white markings. Dark brown eyes and a wrinkled forehead give the breed an alert, curious expression.
Playful and lively, Boxers need plenty of daily exercise and mental stimulation. They suit active families that can keep up with their athletic energy, as adaptability is moderate rather than high.
Strong protective instincts make Boxers alert, attentive watchdogs. At home, they are affectionate with their families and stand out for being patient and gentle with children. Most are friendly towards strangers as well.
Because they are intelligent and eager to please, Boxers are fairly easy to train. Early socialisation helps them get on well with other animals and strangers, especially since sociability with other dogs is moderate. Barking and drooling are both moderate, while shedding and grooming stay low.
A Boxer has a lifespan of 10 years, shorter than many breeds. The low coat upkeep helps balance their high activity needs. For an active household that doesn't mind some drool and wants a playful, loyal dog around children, a Boxer fits well.

general.name: Standard Schnauzer
general.shortDescription: The Standard Schnauzer is a brave, intelligent German farm dog and protective companion.
general.longDescription:
Originally a farm dog from Germany, the Standard Schnauzer sits in the Working group, larger than the Miniature and smaller than the Giant. It stands 20 inches tall, weighs 40 pounds and has a sturdy, square-built frame. Its rough, wiry, tight-fitting double coat is medium in length and comes in black or pepper and salt. Arched eyebrows and bristly whiskers on a long head give it a distinct look.
At home, Standard Schnauzers are very affectionate, playful and adaptable, and they are great with children. They are brave, highly vigilant watchdogs that protect their families, while staying more measured around strangers and other dogs. Barking is moderate, though they love chasing squirrels in the garden.
These intelligent dogs have sharp senses and need plenty of mental stimulation alongside moderate daily exercise. Training is easy with a firm, gentle approach. They shed very little, need moderate grooming and drool an average amount. With a lifespan of 15 years, the Standard Schnauzer is a long-lived, lively companion.

general.name: Akita
general.shortDescription: The Akita is a large, faithful Japanese guardian that stays cautious around strangers.
general.longDescription:
The Akita is a large Guardian breed from Japan, standing about 25 inches tall and weighing around 100 pounds. It has a broad head, upright ears, dark eyes and a tail that curls over its back. Its straight, rough double coat is medium in length and comes in several colours, including white.
At home, an Akita is brave, dignified and faithful to its household, showing moderate affection and playfulness. It barely drools and doesn't bark much, keeping a quiet, clean manner indoors. Around strangers it tends to be cautious, and it has strong protective instincts that keep it alert to anything unusual.
Getting along with other dogs is rarely easy, because Akitas aren't sociable with them and are naturally wary of other animals. Early socialisation helps, and training takes moderate patience and consistency. This is an active dog that needs plenty of daily exercise alongside regular mental work. Expect moderate shedding and regular brushing to keep the coat in shape.
Akitas live around 12 years. They have moderate adaptability and get on reasonably well with children. In Japan, the breed is regarded as a symbol of good health, happiness and long life.

general.name: Russell Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Russell Terrier is a small, curious English terrier with high energy.
general.longDescription:
Bred in England for fox hunting by the Sporting Parson, the Russell Terrier is a compact dog in the Terrier group, standing about 10 inches tall and weighing around 12 pounds. It has a rectangular build, dark almond-shaped eyes, mobile V-shaped ears and an easy, confident stride. Its short, smooth, wiry coat has no undercoat and is mostly white with tan or black markings.
For such a small dog, it has a loud voice and a watchful streak, barking frequently to flag anything out of the ordinary. At the same time, it is very affectionate with its family, keen on play and very friendly towards both strangers and other dogs. It gets on reasonably well with children and adapts easily to different living setups.
Exercise and mental stimulation are the biggest commitments, because both sit at the highest level. Short walks won't satisfy a tireless hunting breed, so it needs plenty of space to explore, play and stay busy. Training takes moderate effort. Grooming is straightforward, because it doesn't drool, sheds a moderate amount and only needs occasional brushing. Russell Terriers live around 13 years.

general.name: Dogue de Bordeaux
general.shortDescription: The Dogue de Bordeaux is a muscular, loving French guardian with strong protective instincts and a short lifespan.
general.longDescription:
Also known as the Mastiff of Bordeaux, the Dogue de Bordeaux is a French Guardian breed whose history reaches back to before France became a nation. It stands around 25 inches tall and weighs about 105 pounds, with a heavy, muscular build. Its huge head, deeply furrowed brow and expressive eyes give it an unmistakable look, paired with a short, smooth, straight fawn coat that has no undercoat.
At home, the Dogue de Bordeaux is brave, faithful and very affectionate with its family. Because its protective instincts are very strong, early socialisation and training are important to stop it becoming overly dominant, though the breed is fairly easy to train. It has moderate playfulness and barking levels, and it sits in the middle when it comes to getting along with children, strangers and other dogs.
The breed adapts well to different living environments provided it gets moderate daily exercise and plenty of mental stimulation. Living with one comes with two messy realities: it drools heavily and sheds a lot. Grooming itself takes very little work because of the short coat. Prospective owners should also be prepared for a short lifespan of around 7 years.

general.name: Miniature Pinscher
general.shortDescription: The Miniature Pinscher is a small, brave, playful companion with loud watchdog instincts.
general.longDescription:
The Miniature Pinscher is a small Companion breed, standing about 11 inches tall and weighing around 9 pounds. It has a brave, dignified bearing and a big-dog personality packed into a tiny frame.
Its compact, wedge-shaped body moves with a high-stepping hackney gait, much like a trotting hackney horse. The coat is short, straight, smooth and shiny with no undercoat, coming in solid red, chocolate-and-rust or black-and-rust. Dark, slightly oval eyes and high-set ears complete the look.
Don't expect a quiet pace just because of the size. It has very high needs for both exercise and mental stimulation, so it needs plenty to do every day. Training takes moderate effort. Protective instincts are strong and barking is frequent, so it acts as an alert, noisy watchdog.
With its own family, the Miniature Pinscher is very affectionate and playful. It generally gets on well with other dogs and adapts easily to different homes. Around children and strangers it is reasonably sociable without being overly outgoing.
Miniature Pinschers have a long lifespan of around 15 years. Coat upkeep is minimal, because they don't drool and rarely need grooming, though they do shed a moderate amount. Between the energy and the barking, they still take real daily commitment.

general.name: Toller
general.shortDescription: The Toller is an energetic, intelligent sporting dog, easy to train and very affectionate with children.
general.longDescription:
Also known by its full name, the Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever, the Toller is a medium-sized Sporting dog standing about 20 inches tall and weighing around 45 pounds. Its wavy, silky double coat is medium in length and ranges from golden red to dark copper, often with white markings. Almond-shaped eyes give it an alert, eager expression.
With its own family, a Toller is loving, very affectionate and always up for play. It is very good with children and generally friendly with other dogs. Around strangers, however, it tends to be cautious. Protective instincts are moderate, and it doesn't bark much.
Bred as a hunting dog, the Toller is happiest when it has a job to do. It needs heavy daily exercise alongside high levels of mental stimulation. Games of fetch, hiking, camping and swimming are all good outlets for its tireless energy.
Training is one of the easiest parts of owning one. Tollers are intelligent, eager to please and very easy to train, so they suit both new and experienced owners who can keep up with the exercise. They also adapt well to different living environments once their daily physical and mental needs are met.
Practical coat care is fairly light. A Toller doesn't drool much, sheds a moderate amount and only needs occasional grooming to keep its silky coat in good condition. The breed typically lives around 13 years.

general.name: Bullmastiff
general.shortDescription: The Bullmastiff is a brave, quiet Guardian bred in England from Bulldogs and Mastiffs to hold poachers.
general.longDescription:
The Bullmastiff began in England as a cross between Bulldogs and Mastiffs, bred to pursue and hold poachers. This large, muscular Guardian stands around 25 inches tall and weighs about 115 pounds. It has a wide head, deep muzzle, dark eyes and V-shaped ears set high on the skull.
Its straight, smooth single coat is short and comes in fawn, red or brindle. Grooming takes very little effort, though you can expect moderate shedding and moderate drooling. Prospective owners should also plan for a short lifespan of around 8 years.
Bullmastiffs are faithful, brave and affectionate with their families, and they bark very little. Their protective instincts are strong, so they stay alert around people they don't know. They get on reasonably well with children, strangers and other dogs, and they have a moderately playful side.
Plan on giving this breed plenty of daily exercise and regular mental work. Bullmastiffs learn fairly easily, which helps when teaching manners to a dog this heavy. Early training and socialisation matter, and they adapt reasonably well to different living setups once their needs are met.

general.name: Giant Schnauzer
general.shortDescription: The Giant Schnauzer is a watchful, obedient Guardian with high energy and a wiry double coat.
general.longDescription:
Bred to scale up the Standard Schnauzer into a bigger, stronger working dog, the Giant Schnauzer is a solidly built Guardian. Adults stand around 25 inches tall and weigh about 70 pounds.
The medium-length double coat is wiry and rough, and it comes in solid black or pepper and salt. A bristly beard and full eyebrows frame the face and give the breed a keen, alert look.
Keeping that coat in good shape takes frequent grooming, and Giant Schnauzers shed a moderate amount. Drooling is low, so they don't leave much mess around the house.
With their own families, they are very affectionate, faithful and playful. They are also highly vigilant guardians that bark a moderate amount. Around children, strangers and other dogs, they tend to be moderately sociable rather than automatically outgoing.
Daily activity is the biggest commitment with a Giant Schnauzer. They need a great deal of daily exercise along with plenty of mental work. Because they are obedient and easy to train, they adapt well when owners give them regular tasks and routines.
With a typical lifespan of 14 years, this is a long commitment for active owners who want a watchful, capable working partner beside them.

general.name: Airedale Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Airedale Terrier is a brave, intelligent Terrier with low shedding and strong protective instincts.
general.longDescription:
Known by the nickname King of Terriers, the Airedale Terrier is a sturdy Terrier standing on long, strong legs. Adults measure around 25 inches tall and weigh about 60 pounds, with an average lifespan of 13 years. A long head with dark eyes, folded ears, a beard and a moustache gives them a keen, alert look.
Their short-to-medium coat is a single layer of rough, wiry hair, tan with black markings. Airedale Terriers shed very little and don't drool, though the coat still needs regular grooming to keep it tidy.
Brave, intelligent and friendly, Airedale Terriers are moderately affectionate and playful at home, and they get along reasonably well with children, strangers and other dogs. Their protective instincts are high, so they stay watchful over the home and bark a moderate amount.
Capable as hunters, sporting dogs and companions, Airedale Terriers have moderate exercise and mental stimulation needs. They adapt reasonably well to different routines, and training takes steady, consistent effort. Their bold, determined nature fits owners who want an alert, willing dog for sports and family activities.

general.name: English Cocker Spaniel
general.shortDescription: The English Cocker Spaniel is a lively, sociable Sporting dog bred to flush and retrieve gamebirds.
general.longDescription:
Compact and evenly built, the English Cocker Spaniel is a lively Sporting dog bred to flush and retrieve gamebirds. Adults stand around 15 inches tall and weigh about 30 pounds, moving easily between field work and home life.
Dark eyes and thick ears that sit close to the head give the breed a friendly, approachable look. Their long, wavy, silky double coat comes in a wide variety of colours and patterns.
At home, English Cocker Spaniels are happy, vigilant and very affectionate with their families. They are very sociable with children and other dogs, and generally friendly towards strangers. They are moderately playful, fairly protective and bark a moderate amount.
Eager to please and fairly easy to train, they adapt well to different homes and routines. Their daily exercise needs are moderate, though they need plenty of mental stimulation to stay settled and engaged.
Regular grooming keeps the silky double coat tidy, and owners should expect moderate shedding alongside low drooling. With an average lifespan of 13 years, this is a friendly, attentive companion for households ready to keep up with its lively habits.

general.name: Mastiff
general.shortDescription: The Mastiff is a quiet, dignified Guardian weighing about 170 pounds, protective yet gentle with families.
general.longDescription:
The Mastiff is a heavily built, muscular Guardian standing around 30 inches tall and weighing about 170 pounds. A wide head, wrinkled brow and black mask give it a calm, watchful expression. Its short, straight, rough double coat comes in fawn, apricot or brindle. Grooming takes very little work, though shedding is moderate and drooling is heavy. Potential owners should also expect a short lifespan of around 8 years.
Even at that size, Mastiffs are dignified, friendly and patient companions. They are very affectionate with their families and very good with children. They rarely bark, yet their protective instincts are strong. Around strangers and other dogs they are moderately sociable, with a moderately playful streak.
Early socialisation and gentle, consistent training matter when raising a dog this large and protective. Training takes moderate effort, and daily exercise and mental stimulation needs are both moderate. Mastiffs adapt well to family homes that are ready for their size and their drool.

general.name: English Setter
general.shortDescription: The English Setter is a friendly, relaxed Sporting dog with a wavy speckled coat.
general.longDescription:
The English Setter is a Sporting breed and a hunter, standing about 25 inches tall and weighing around 60 pounds. It has an oval head, dark brown eyes and a silky, wavy double coat of medium length. Its speckled markings, called belton, come in liver, lemon and orange. Expect moderate shedding, regular grooming and some drooling.
Sometimes called the gentleman of the dog world, the English Setter is relaxed, happy and very affectionate with its family. It gets on well with children, other dogs and strangers, and it adapts easily to different homes. It has a playful side, barks a moderate amount and keeps a fair watch over the house.
Exercise needs are moderate, so daily walks and active play suit it well. It needs more mental stimulation than physical work, so regular training and activities keep it occupied. Most owners find English Setters fairly easy to train. They live about 12 years on average and make sociable, well-mannered companions for homes wanting an affectionate dog.

general.name: Shiba Inu
general.shortDescription: Originally a Japanese hunter, the Shiba Inu is a vigilant, independent Companion dog.
general.longDescription:
The Shiba Inu is an old Japanese breed, originally bred for hunting. This small, sturdy Companion dog stands about 15 inches tall and weighs around 20 pounds, with a muscular build and a foxlike look. Its short, straight double coat feels rough and comes in red, red sesame or black and tan, marked with white.
Shiba Inus are bold, confident and highly vigilant, which makes them attentive watchdogs. With their families they're very affectionate, balancing a playful side with a dignified manner. Around strangers, children and other dogs, they're moderately sociable and often cautious at first.
Training takes patience, because their independence makes them challenging to teach. They need moderate daily exercise, regular playtime and plenty of mental stimulation to stay occupied. They adapt reasonably well to urban or rural homes, and they bark a moderate amount.
Grooming needs are low and they barely drool, though shedding is moderate. Shiba Inus live around 15 years, a relatively long lifespan for a dog, and they suit owners who want a lively, watchful companion with a strong will.

general.name: Toy Poodle
general.shortDescription: Tiny at 5 pounds, the Toy Poodle is a bright, confident Companion dog.
general.longDescription:
Standing about 9 inches tall and weighing around 5 pounds, the Toy Poodle is a tiny, agile Companion breed with plenty of confidence. It has a long, curly single coat with a rough texture and a relatively long lifespan of 15 years. Shedding is very low and it barely drools, though the coat needs frequent grooming.
Toy Poodles are very affectionate, playful and friendly with children and strangers. Around other dogs, they're moderately sociable. They have a fair level of protective instinct, and they tend to bark quite a bit.
This is an intelligent, eager breed that's very easy to train, with a real knack for obedience and agility. Even at this size, it needs plenty of exercise and very high mental stimulation. It adapts well to city flats or country homes when kept active.
The Toy Poodle suits families or individuals who want a companionable, sharp small dog and have time for regular grooming, training and daily exercise.

general.name: American Eskimo
general.shortDescription: The American Eskimo is a faithful, adaptable Companion dog with a dense white double coat.
general.longDescription:
The American Eskimo is an agile Companion breed that comes in standard, miniature and toy sizes, averaging around 15 inches tall and 20 pounds. It has a dense white double coat of medium length, straight and rough, with a lion-like ruff and a plumed tail carried over the back. Black eye rims, nose and lips frame a smiling face, and the breed barely drools.
Faithful, intelligent and very affectionate, the American Eskimo is great with children and very friendly towards strangers. It's moderately playful and moderately sociable with other dogs, with average alertness and barking. Eager to please and fairly easy to train, it adapts well to most homes.
Daily exercise needs are high, while mental stimulation, shedding and grooming are moderate. Because it thrives on interaction, neglect can lead to behavioural issues. Expect a lifespan of around 15 years, so this breed belongs in an active household with plenty of time to spend together.

general.name: Brittany
general.shortDescription: Energetic, playful and easy to train, the Brittany is a Sporting gundog built for active outdoor homes.
general.longDescription:
The Brittany is an energetic, agile Sporting gundog built for work in the field. Standing about 20 inches tall and weighing around 35 pounds, it's a little smaller than a setter and leggier than a spaniel.
Its short, wavy double coat has a rough texture and bold patterns, usually white with vivid orange or liver markings. Coat care is straightforward, with moderate grooming and moderate shedding, and the breed barely drools.
Exercise is the biggest commitment with a Brittany. This is a very high-energy dog that needs vigorous daily activity alongside plenty of mental stimulation. Dog sports such as obedience, agility, flyball and dock diving are all good outlets for its enthusiasm.
At home, Brittanys are happy, playful and moderately affectionate. They're friendly with children and get on well with other dogs, while staying moderately open with strangers. Protective instincts and barking are both moderate, so they're reasonably alert without constant noise. They're intelligent and very easy to train, doing best with a consistent, engaging routine.
Adaptability is moderate, because a Brittany fits best into an active, outdoorsy household. These dogs typically live about 13 years and make bright, spirited partners for people who spend plenty of time outside.

general.name: Cardigan Welsh Corgi
general.shortDescription: The Cardigan Welsh Corgi is a loyal, vocal herding dog originally bred to move cattle.
general.longDescription:
Bred to herd cattle, the Cardigan Welsh Corgi sits low on short legs with a deep chest and a sturdy body. At 12 inches tall and 30 pounds, it is a strong, compact dog with a lifespan of 14 years. Unlike its Pembroke cousin, the Cardigan has a tail. Its straight, rough double coat is medium in length and comes in several colours, including blue-merle.
At home, this Herding breed is affectionate, playful and faithful. It gets on well with children and is friendly with strangers, though proper socialisation helps with other dogs and pets. Expect plenty of noise. Cardigans have a big bark for their size and make alert watchdogs, so they aren't quiet companions.
Those short legs still belong to an agile worker that needs a lot of daily exercise and mental stimulation. They're intelligent and fairly easy to train, and they adapt reasonably well to different homes once their energy is spent. Drooling is minimal and grooming needs are light, though they shed a moderate amount.

general.name: Belgian Tervuren
general.shortDescription: The Belgian Tervuren is a vigilant, brave herding dog that learns fast and needs regular work.
general.longDescription:
Alert and muscular, the Belgian Tervuren is a medium-sized Herding breed built for agile work. It stands 25 inches tall and weighs 60 pounds, with males generally larger than females, and has a lifespan of 13 years. The head is carried high above a straight, rough double coat of medium length, with a thicker collarette around the neck that is more pronounced in males.
Vigilant and brave, the Tervuren has strong protective instincts and can be possessive of its people. It is moderately affectionate and playful with family, and reasonably tolerant of children, strangers and other dogs. Barking and adaptability are both moderate. Alongside its watchful nature, the breed often shows a mischievous sense of humour.
This breed needs plenty of daily exercise and mental stimulation, so it suits an active household that gives it regular tasks. Intelligent and very easy to train, Tervurens do well in herding and obedience work. Coat care is simpler than it looks, because they barely drool, need only occasional grooming and shed a moderate amount.

general.name: Bloodhound
general.shortDescription: The Bloodhound is a large, friendly scent hound that drools heavily and follows its nose.
general.longDescription:
Often called the Sleuth Hound, the Bloodhound is a large Hound bred to follow scents across wide terrain on powerful legs. Its nose drives almost everything it does. Fully grown, it measures 25 inches tall and weighs 95 pounds, with a relatively short lifespan of 10 years.
You can spot the breed immediately by its long, wrinkled face, loose skin and large drooping ears. Warm, deep-set eyes give it a solemn expression. Its short, smooth, straight single coat comes in black and tan, liver and tan or red.
Away from a trail, the Bloodhound is docile, friendly and affectionate with its family. It gets on reasonably well with children, strangers and other dogs, and it isn't particularly protective. Expect plenty of noise, because Bloodhounds are very vocal. Their independent, curious nature can also pull them into mischief when they catch an interesting smell.
They need moderate exercise and mental stimulation, with long walks and time to explore scents. Adaptability is moderate. Even though they're sensitive and independent, they are fairly easy to train once you have their attention. Grooming needs are light and shedding is moderate, but heavy drooling is a daily fixture with this breed.

general.name: Anatolian Shepherd
general.shortDescription: The Anatolian Shepherd is an independent flock guardian with strong protective instincts.
general.longDescription:
With roots going back 6,000 years to the Bronze Age, the Anatolian Shepherd is a big Working breed built to guard flocks across harsh terrain. It weighs 115 pounds and stands 30 inches tall, yet stays nimble on a muscular frame. Lifespan is 12 years, and the short, straight, smooth coat is a single layer.
Relaxed and faithful, the Anatolian Shepherd watches over whatever it considers its flock, from livestock to children, smaller dogs or the family cat. It's highly vigilant and territorial, and it stays reserved rather than openly affectionate with its own family. Strangers are met with real caution. Around the home it's moderately playful, barks a fair amount and gets on reasonably well with children and other dogs.
Training is challenging because Anatolians are independent, intelligent and dominant. They need steady, firm leadership from owners who can manage a demanding dog. Exercise, mental stimulation and adaptability are all moderate, so they don't need nonstop activity to settle. Upkeep is easier than the size suggests: they barely drool, need only occasional grooming and shed a moderate amount.

general.name: German Wirehaired Pointer
general.shortDescription: The German Wirehaired Pointer is a loving, lively gundog built for outdoor work.
general.longDescription:
Built for rough ground and bad weather, the German Wirehaired Pointer is a sturdy Sporting gundog slightly larger than its close relative, the German Shorthaired Pointer. It weighs 60 pounds, stands 25 inches tall and has a long lifespan of 15 years. Its rough, wiry double coat of medium length shields it from thorny underbrush, and a shaggy beard and eyebrows frame its face.
At home, this breed is very affectionate, playful and often amusing. It's friendly with strangers and adapts well to new routines. It gets on reasonably well with children and other dogs, stays watchful with moderate protective instincts and barks a fair amount. It likes being close to its family.
Plan for plenty of outdoor time. With very high energy and strong mental stimulation needs, the German Wirehaired Pointer is built to work through bushes all day and won't be happy lounging indoors. It's bright, eager and easy to train, even if an independent streak shows up occasionally. Upkeep is straightforward, with low shedding, occasional grooming and light drooling.

general.name: Belgian Sheepdog
general.shortDescription: The Belgian Sheepdog is an intelligent, vigilant herding dog with a black double coat and high energy.
general.longDescription:
The Belgian Sheepdog is a muscular dog in the Herding group, standing 25 inches tall and weighing 60 pounds. It has dark, questioning eyes and an abundant, medium-length black double coat that is straight and rough, with a collarette around the neck and breeches on the hindquarters. Most live for around 13 years.
Reliable and easy to train, this breed thrives on hard work and takes well to dog sports and active tasks. It needs plenty of daily exercise and mental stimulation to stay content, and it is sensitive enough to dislike being neglected or left out of family life. Strong protective instincts make it a vigilant watchdog around the home.
It enjoys human companionship and brings a proud, playful presence to everyday life. For all that thick black coat, grooming stays fairly light, though you should still expect moderate shedding through the year.

general.name: Gordon Setter
general.shortDescription: The Gordon Setter is a confident, loving bird dog from Scotland.
general.longDescription:
The Gordon Setter is a Sporting group bird dog with roots in Scottish aristocracy, bred to work Scotland's rugged ground in harsh weather. Sometimes called the black avenger of the Highlands, it stands 25 inches tall, weighs 65 pounds and lives for around 13 years.
Its medium-length double coat is silky, wavy and black with tan markings, and longer hair grows on the ears, chest, belly, legs and tail. Tan spots sit above bright brown eyes that give the face a wise, willing expression.
This is an athletic outdoor dog that needs heavy daily exercise and plenty of mental work, so it suits active households that spend plenty of time outdoors. Training is straightforward because the Gordon Setter learns quickly. At home, it is brave, confident and very affectionate with its family, with a watchful, protective streak.
Once it has had enough outdoor activity, it is just as content settling by the fireside and adapts well to different living setups. Even with the longer hair on its ears, chest and legs, grooming needs stay fairly light and shedding is moderate. One thing to plan for is drooling, which tends to be heavy in this breed.

general.name: Italian Greyhound
general.shortDescription: The Italian Greyhound is a slender, very affectionate companion dog shaped like a small Greyhound.
general.longDescription:
Often called an IG, the Italian Greyhound is a Companion group breed shaped like a miniature Greyhound. At 15 inches tall and 10 pounds, it has a slim, curved frame and long, fine-boned legs.
