Its short, smooth, straight coat has no undercoat, so this dog needs extra warmth in cold weather. Lifespan is long compared with other breeds, at around 15 years.
Happy and companionable, Italian Greyhounds are observant, playful and very affectionate, and they thrive on close human contact, often curling up in a lap or sharing a bed. They are very friendly with strangers and other dogs, and get along reasonably well with children. Outside, watch for anything moving quickly, because they keep the Greyhound urge to chase.
They settle easily into different kinds of homes and are happy with moderate daily exercise and mental engagement. Training tends to be fairly straightforward. Coat care is minimal too, because the short, smooth fur needs very little grooming, though it still sheds a moderate amount through the year.

general.name: Border Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Border Terrier is a brave, loving small terrier with a rough coat and otter-shaped head.
general.longDescription:
The Border Terrier is a sturdy small dog in the Terrier group, standing 14 inches tall and weighing 14 pounds. Its head has a distinct otter shape, and its legs are fairly long for a small terrier. The short, rough wire coat has no undercoat and comes in grizzle and tan, blue and tan, wheaten or red. Most live for around 14 years, which is a long lifespan for a dog.
Brave, happy and affectionate with its family, this breed is especially good with children and friendly towards strangers. It is playful and good-natured at home, though it is only moderately sociable with other dogs. Border Terriers are tough enough for work in the fields, and those hunting instincts can show up around smaller animals. They adapt well to city life as long as they get out regularly.
A moderate amount of daily exercise and mental stimulation keeps them content, whether in the garden or out on walks, and training is fairly easy. Looking after that wiry coat doesn't take much work either, because shedding is light and grooming is only needed occasionally.

general.name: Flat-Coated Retriever
general.shortDescription: The Flat-Coated Retriever is a playful, outgoing sporting dog built for heavy outdoor exercise.
general.longDescription:
The Flat-Coated Retriever is a lean dog in the Sporting group, standing 25 inches tall and weighing 65 pounds. It has a long head with a smart, kindly expression and a medium-length single coat that is smooth, wavy and lies flat in either black or liver. Its lifespan averages around 9 years, which is short compared with other breeds.
People often call this breed the Peter Pan of the Sporting group because it seems young at heart, with a constantly wagging tail and a playful, slightly mischievous streak. It is very affectionate with its family, great with children and outgoing with both strangers and other dogs. It also adapts very well, settling into different kinds of homes with ease.
That smooth coat is straightforward to look after, needing only light grooming alongside moderate shedding. What really takes time is keeping this breed busy. Flat-Coated Retrievers have huge reserves of energy and need plenty of outdoor exercise and mental work, whether retrieving ducks in the field or taking part in dog shows. Fortunately, they are willing to please and very easy to train.

general.name: Chinese Crested
general.shortDescription: The Chinese Crested is a small, lively companion dog found in hairless and coated varieties.
general.longDescription:
Most people recognise the Chinese Crested by its hairless variety, which has spotted pink skin, a spiky crest on its head, furry feet and a feathery tail. The breed also comes in a coated variety called the powderpuff, which has soft, silky hair. Both types share the same fine-boned build and graceful movement, standing about 12 inches tall and weighing around 10 pounds.
As a Companion breed, the Chinese Crested stays closely tuned in to the people it lives with. It is loving and forms strong bonds with its family, and it is friendly towards strangers as well. Vigilant and lively, it likes being part of everyday household life.
Day to day, Chinese Cresteds adapt well to different living situations. They are fairly easy to train, and their attentive nature helps them settle comfortably into life with their owners.
The breed barely sheds and doesn't drool. Grooming demands are light overall, though the two varieties differ: the hairless type needs very little coat upkeep, while the powderpuff's silky coat needs more frequent brushing. Chinese Cresteds also live longer than many breeds, with a typical lifespan of around 15 years.

general.name: Portuguese Water Dog
general.shortDescription: The Portuguese Water Dog is a lively, affectionate Working dog bred to help fishermen.
general.longDescription:
A Portuguese Water Dog wants a job to do. Originally bred as an all-round helper for fishermen, this sturdy Working breed stands about 20 inches tall, weighs around 45 pounds and lives for roughly 12 years. It is very easy to train and needs plenty of daily exercise and mental challenges.
Around the house, the breed is very affectionate and playful, with a brave, protective side when it comes to its family. It is great with children and usually friendly with both strangers and other dogs. Although it adapts easily to different homes, it suits active owners who can match its high energy.
Coat care is the other commitment to plan for. The Portuguese Water Dog has a long, rough, curly single coat that suits water work. It sheds little, so it leaves less fur around the house, and it doesn't drool much. Even so, that curly coat needs frequent grooming.

general.name: Greyhound
general.shortDescription: The Greyhound is a tall, dignified Hound built for speed and affectionate at home.
general.longDescription:
Every line of a Greyhound is built for running. Standing around 30 inches tall and weighing about 65 pounds, this large Hound has a lean, aerodynamic frame with a deep chest that sweeps into a tightly tucked waist. That inverted S silhouette has caught the eye of artists, poets and royalty for millennia, and it reflects the speed and grace of a natural sprinter.
For all its athleticism, the Greyhound is a gentle, dignified dog with an independent character. It is affectionate with its family and adapts well to different living situations. Running is still what it loves most, so owners should expect high exercise needs and plan regular time for it to run. Most Greyhounds are also sociable with other dogs.
Coat care is straightforward. The Greyhound has a short, smooth, straight coat with no undercoat, so it rarely needs grooming. It sheds only a small amount and doesn't drool, which keeps daily upkeep light. Greyhounds typically live for around 12 years. They suit people who appreciate a tall, athletic companion that gives warmth to its family while keeping a measure of autonomy.

general.name: Old English Sheepdog
general.shortDescription: The Old English Sheepdog is an intelligent, shaggy Herding dog that is affectionate and patient with children.
general.longDescription:
Behind the shaggy hair hanging over its eyes, the Old English Sheepdog is a mellow, agreeable family dog. It is very affectionate with its household, patient with children and playful around the home. That gentle side goes with steady courage. A sensible watchdog with a loud, ringing bark, it keeps a protective eye on the people it loves.
This Herding breed packs plenty of muscle into a compact frame. Standing about 20 inches tall and weighing around 80 pounds, it moves with a bear-like gait that reflects both agility and strength. Intelligent and adaptable, it is fairly easy to train, though it needs plenty of mental stimulation alongside regular activity to stay happy.
The biggest commitment for owners is the coat. The Old English Sheepdog grows a long, thick double coat with rough, wavy hair that requires frequent grooming to keep it healthy and looking its best. Anyone bringing one home should be ready for high-maintenance upkeep. The breed also has a shorter lifespan than many dogs, living for around 10 years.

general.name: St. Bernard
general.shortDescription: The St. Bernard is a giant, affectionate Working breed from the Swiss Alps, patient with children.
general.longDescription:
At about 30 inches tall and 145 pounds, the St. Bernard is a massive, heavily muscled dog. Originally from the Swiss Alps, this imposing Working breed is quiet around the house and rarely barks. Even at this size, it adapts well to different living conditions.
With its family, the St. Bernard is happy, curious, companionable and very affectionate. It is known for its patience with children, which makes it a gentle presence in family homes. At the same time, its protective instincts are very strong, so it keeps a careful watch over the people it lives with.
There are two practical trade-offs to consider before choosing the breed. The St. Bernard is a heavy drooler, and it has a short lifespan of around 9 years. Coat care itself is straightforward: its short, smooth, wavy double coat needs little grooming, less than its size might suggest.

general.name: Papillon
general.shortDescription: The Papillon takes its name from its butterfly ears and brings lively, vigilant company.
general.longDescription:
The Papillon takes its name from the French word for butterfly. It belongs to the Companion group and stands around 10 inches tall, weighing about 8 pounds. Despite its small size, it is a hardy breed that typically lives for 15 years.
Its large ears are shaped like butterfly wings and usually stand upright, though the Phalene variety has drooped ears. The straight, silky coat is medium length and usually has a white base with other colour combinations.
Upkeep is light: the single coat only needs occasional brushing, shedding is moderate and this breed does not drool. Papillons are very adaptable and settle well into both city and country homes across different climates.
Around people, this is a happy, very affectionate dog. Papillons are great with children, playful during family activities and welcoming towards strangers. With other dogs, they are moderately sociable.
They are vigilant and protective for their size. Papillons notice unusual activity around the home quickly and will alert their owners, so expect a noisy dog that barks often.
Papillons are easy to train, learn tricks quickly and do well in agility competitions. Their exercise needs are high and their need for mental stimulation is very high, so they suit active households that can give them daily exercise, play and training.

general.name: Whippet
general.shortDescription: Fast on a sprint and relaxed indoors, the Whippet is a quiet Hound.
general.longDescription:
Often nicknamed the 'Poor Man's Racehorse', the Whippet is a fast, slender Hound that looks like a smaller Greyhound. At around 20 inches tall and 35 pounds, it has a deep chest, trim waist, long arched neck and a streamlined 'inverted S' body shape. Expect a lifespan of around 14 years.
Happy, relaxed and very affectionate, Whippets are great with children and very sociable with other dogs, while staying fairly friendly with strangers. They are playful and love to chase, needing bursts of hard exercise and plenty of mental stimulation before settling into long stretches of lounging. Once those needs are met, they do well in flats or houses with fenced gardens, though training takes moderate effort.
Grooming is barely a chore with their short, smooth coat, which rarely needs brushing. They shed lightly and do not drool. Because Whippets seldom bark and stay quiet indoors, they suit city living well.

general.name: American Bulldog
general.shortDescription: Immigrants brought the muscular, faithful American Bulldog to 1800s farms for tough working jobs.
general.longDescription:
Immigrants brought the American Bulldog to the United States in the 1800s, where small farmers and ranchers relied on its strength, bravery and loyalty to guard property, herd livestock and catch feral pigs. A muscular dog in the Working group, it grows to about 23 inches tall and 80 pounds, with a relatively short lifespan of 10 years.
Faithful and confident, the American Bulldog tends to be reserved with its family and cautious around strangers. It is moderately friendly with children and other dogs. This is a calm breed that is not especially playful, alert or adaptable, and it barks only occasionally.
Everyday upkeep is light. Its short, smooth coat needs very little grooming and sheds lightly, and drooling is not an issue. Exercise and mental stimulation needs are both low, while training is fairly straightforward. That suits owners looking for a quiet, loyal Working dog without heavy daily demands.

general.name: Rhodesian Ridgeback
general.shortDescription: A ridge of backward-growing hair sets the dignified, loving Rhodesian Ridgeback apart from other Hounds.
general.longDescription:
You can spot a Rhodesian Ridgeback by the ridge of hair growing backwards along its back. Sometimes called the 'Renaissance hound', this athletic Hound was originally used in Africa to track and bay lions. Built for speed and strength, adults reach about 25 inches tall and 80 pounds, though their 10-year lifespan is relatively short.
The smooth wheaten coat is short and straight, paired with a black nose or a less common brown one. Expect moderate shedding, light grooming and a little drooling. At home, Rhodesian Ridgebacks are dignified, relaxed and very affectionate. They are great with children and highly protective, while staying reasonably friendly with strangers and other dogs, and they bark only occasionally.
Because they are independent and have a strong prey drive, they need firm, fair guidance from an early age. Even so, training is fairly straightforward overall. They adapt well to different environments, enjoy a fair bit of play and need moderate daily exercise alongside plenty of mental stimulation.

general.name: AmStaff
general.shortDescription: Muscular AmStaffs pair a springy, confident gait with an intelligent, friendly nature and strong protective instincts.
general.longDescription:
The AmStaff, short for American Staffordshire Terrier, is a confident, intelligent dog in the Terrier group. Stocky and muscular at about 18 inches tall and 60 pounds, it has a broad head, defined jaw, pronounced cheekbones and dark, round eyes set wide apart. Courageous and loyal, it typically lives for 15 years.
On the move, the AmStaff has an agile, springy gait. Its glossy coat comes in many colours and patterns and asks very little of its owners: shedding is light, drooling is not a problem and grooming is seldom needed.
Often called 'personality dogs', AmStaffs are very affectionate with their families and friendly towards strangers. They do reasonably well with children and other dogs, and bark a moderate amount. Keenly aware of their surroundings, they are highly protective and make alert watchdogs. They adapt fairly well and need moderate exercise, play and mental stimulation. Training is moderately challenging, though some AmStaffs work in showbiz and other activities.
If you plan to bring an AmStaff home, look for a responsible breeder so you start with a healthy, well-socialised dog.

general.name: Scottish Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Scottish Terrier is a small, confident terrier with short legs and a wiry coat.
general.longDescription:
The Scottish Terrier, often called the Scottie, stands 10 inches tall, weighs 20 pounds and has a lifespan of 12 years. Its persistent terrier character and dignified manner earned it the nickname 'the Diehard'. It is a confident, independent dog that prefers to do things on its own terms.
A Scottie is easy to spot by its sturdy body, short legs and the longer hair on its beard, legs and lower body. Its rough, wiry topcoat sits over a soft, dense undercoat in black, wheaten yellow or brindle. Upright ears, an erect tail and piercing eyes give it an alert look.
This British terrier is highly vigilant and quick to bark, so it works well as a watchdog. It is polite enough with strangers and children, though it saves its warmest side for its own family. Strong hunting instincts make it a risk around cats and other small animals, and it doesn't always get on well with other dogs.
At home, the Scottish Terrier is deeply affectionate and has a playful, lively side. It settles well into different households when it gets brisk walks and plenty of mental stimulation to keep it occupied.
Shedding stays low, though the medium-length wire coat needs regular grooming to stay tidy. Training takes moderate patience because of that independent streak, so steady, consistent routines work best.

general.name: Wire Fox Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Wire Fox Terrier is an energetic, friendly British terrier with a rough, mostly white coat.
general.longDescription:
The Wire Fox Terrier was originally used in British foxhunts and still carries plenty of that alert, confident energy. It has a sturdy frame, stands 15 inches tall, weighs 17 pounds and has a long average lifespan of 14 years.
Its rough, wiry double coat is mostly white, and its dark, round eyes sit under V-shaped ears that fold forward. Shedding stays low, though the medium-length coat needs regular grooming to keep it tidy.
With people, the Wire Fox Terrier is affectionate, lively and openly friendly. It gets on very well with children and welcomes strangers easily, while its sociability with other dogs is more moderate.
It is a vigilant dog with strong protective instincts and a habit of barking often. You'll always know when someone is at the door, though the noise can be a factor in close quarters.
This is an athletic, playful and amusing breed with high needs for both exercise and mental stimulation. It does best in an active home where it has regular games, walks and activities to keep busy.
Wire Fox Terriers adapt well to different routines and pick up training fairly easily. Even so, their independent terrier streak and strong prey drive can still be a challenge outdoors, so steady practice helps.

general.name: Vizsla
general.shortDescription: The Vizsla is a lean, affectionate Hungarian sporting dog with a short, smooth golden-rust coat.
general.longDescription:
The Vizsla is a Hungarian sporting gundog built to work all day in the field. It stands 23 inches tall, weighs 55 pounds and has an average lifespan of 13 years. Light on its feet with a lean build, it has long, silky ears and a short, smooth, straight golden-rust coat with no undercoat. That single coat needs very little grooming, though shedding is moderate.
At home, the Vizsla is deeply affectionate, very playful and keen to stay right beside its people. It forms close bonds with its owners and dislikes being left alone for long stretches. It gets on very well with children, is sociable with other dogs and greets strangers warmly. Both its protective instincts and its barking sit at a moderate level.
Plan for very high daily exercise and mental stimulation. With its stamina and lively nature, a Vizsla makes a keen partner for running or cycling and takes well to dog sports. Its gentle look indoors turns into sharp focus once it starts working. Because it is very adaptable and easy to train, it suits active households with the time to keep it busy.

general.name: Pekingese
general.shortDescription: The Pekingese is a small, dignified companion dog from China with a rolling gait and lion-like mane.
general.longDescription:
The Pekingese is a compact companion dog from ancient China, where it was kept by the ruling classes and emperors. It stands 8 inches tall, weighs 12 pounds and has a lifespan of 13 years. It carries itself with a dignified manner and moves with a rolling gait.
Its long, straight, silky double coat grows thickest around the neck and shoulders to form a ruff known as a lion's mane. Coat colours range through shades of red, from golden to deep mahogany. A broad, short muzzle and large, dark eyes give the head a clear, expressive look.
Pekingese are faithful and very affectionate with their families, and they form close bonds with their favourite people. They also keep a confident, independent streak and enjoy regular play.
Alert and protective by nature, they make attentive watchdogs while remaining very quiet. They adapt well to most routines, and training difficulty is moderate, though an opinionated Pekingese will test your patience at times.
Around children, other dogs and strangers, the breed sits in the middle range. It tolerates children best when handled gently and dislikes rough play. Moderate exercise and mental stimulation needs, alongside a low barking tendency, suit flat living well.
Drooling isn't an issue, but shedding is moderate and the long coat needs regular grooming to stay in good condition. For owners who respect its dignified pace, the Pekingese settles comfortably into life as a devoted companion.

general.name: Great Pyrenees
general.shortDescription: The Great Pyrenees is a calm, strong mountain guardian bred to protect sheep from predators.
general.longDescription:
The Great Pyrenees is a working dog originally bred to guard sheep from predators on snowy mountains. It is a large, powerful breed that stands 30 inches tall, weighs 95 pounds and has a relatively short lifespan of 10 years. Its straight, rough, weatherproof double coat is pure white or marked with shades of grey, tan, reddish-brown or badger.
Around the house, it is relaxed, intelligent, tolerant and deeply affectionate with its family. Even so, its protective instincts remain very strong, and a calm Great Pyrenees can move with surprising speed if it spots a threat. It sits in the middle range for playfulness, barking and sociability with children, strangers and other dogs.
It adapts reasonably well to different homes and does best with steady, everyday exercise and mental stimulation. Training takes some patience, and you should expect a fair amount of drooling alongside moderate, seasonal shedding. Because its medium-length coat only needs light grooming, routine coat care is simpler than its size suggests.

general.name: Alaskan Malamute
general.shortDescription: The Alaskan Malamute is a large arctic sled dog from the Working group with a rough, weatherproof double coat.
general.longDescription:
Bred as an arctic sled dog, the Alaskan Malamute is a solidly built spitz in the Working group. It stands 25 inches tall, weighs about 80 pounds and lives roughly 12 years. Strong shoulders, a deep chest, upright ears and a thickly furred tail carried over the back define its frame, along with brown, almond-shaped eyes.
At home, the Alaskan Malamute is faithful, happy and fond of resting beside its family after a busy day. It gets on moderately well with children, other dogs and strangers, while keeping alert, protective instincts. Because Malamutes are pack dogs, start firm, kind training in puppyhood so they don't try to take charge. Most learn easily once clear habits are set.
This breed needs plenty of daily exercise and steady mental work. Its rough, straight double coat of medium length stands up to cold weather, sheds moderately and needs regular brushing. Alaskan Malamutes rarely drool, and they settle in well once they get enough exercise.

general.name: Havanese
general.shortDescription: Native to Cuba, the Havanese is a small, playful dog with a long, silky double coat.
general.longDescription:
Native to Cuba, the Havanese is a small dog in the Companion group that likes being close to people. It stands about 10 inches tall and weighs around 10 pounds, with a sturdy, compact frame, expressive eyes and a springy walk.
Its tail curls over its back, and its straight, silky double coat grows long in a wide range of colours. You can leave the coat long, cord it like a Puli or clip it short to make brushing simpler. Shedding is light, drooling is almost non-existent and regular grooming keeps the hair in good order.
Havanese are intelligent, fairly easy to train and full of playful, clownish habits that keep people amused. Moderate daily exercise and regular mental games are usually enough to keep them settled.
They adapt easily to city living or any other home where they get plenty of human attention. Moderately alert by nature, a Havanese will warn you when something unusual happens. They also bark fairly often, so expect a vocal little watchdog.
A Havanese is very affectionate with its family and gets along easily with children, strangers and other dogs. It bonds closely with everyone in the household. With a long lifespan of around 15 years, this lively breed stays a sociable part of family life for a long time.

general.name: Chinese Shar-Pei
general.shortDescription: The Chinese Shar-Pei is an independent, faithful Working dog with loose folds of skin.
general.longDescription:
Originating in ancient China, the Chinese Shar-Pei is a medium-sized dog in the Working group. It stands around 20 inches tall, weighs about 55 pounds and has a shorter lifespan of roughly 10 years. Heavy folds of loose skin cover its head, neck and shoulders, alongside a broad, hippopotamus-like muzzle, a blue-black tongue, small sunken eyes and tiny triangular ears.
Independent, faithful and usually relaxed around the house, the Chinese Shar-Pei forms a strong bond with its family. It has firm protective instincts and meets a threat with determination, which makes it a reliable guardian. Calm and loyal with its own people, it takes a more measured approach to children, strangers and other dogs.
Because this intelligent breed has a mind of its own, early training and socialisation help prevent dominance issues. Training takes steady effort and consistency. Once settled, the Chinese Shar-Pei adapts well to different living spaces and gets by on moderate daily exercise and mental work.
Its short, straight, smooth single coat needs very little grooming, though it does shed a fair bit. You can also expect moderate drooling and an average amount of barking.

general.name: Afghan Hound
general.shortDescription: The Afghan Hound is a dignified, independent dog with a long, silky coat and high exercise needs.
general.longDescription:
Originally from mountainous regions, the Afghan Hound is a medium-sized dog in the Hound group. It stands about 25 inches tall, weighs around 55 pounds and has a relatively long lifespan of roughly 15 years. Its straight, silky single coat grows very long and once shielded it from harsh climates.
Independent and dignified, the Afghan Hound can seem aloof at times, though it shows deep loyalty and a tender, playful side with its family. It is often reserved around people it doesn't know well and prefers to keep its own counsel. Training is very challenging, so this breed usually suits experienced owners who appreciate an independent dog.
Plan on plenty of daily exercise along with regular mental stimulation to keep an Afghan Hound content. That long coat sheds very little and the dog barely drools, which helps around the house. Even so, keeping the silky hair in good condition calls for frequent grooming.

general.name: Basset Hound
general.shortDescription: The Basset Hound is a low-slung, relaxed dog with long ears and a tolerant nature.
general.longDescription:
A low-slung member of the Hound group, the Basset Hound stands 15 inches tall yet weighs around 55 pounds, with a typical lifespan of about 13 years. Built for stamina rather than speed, it moves with a steady, easy stride and has a strong sense of smell. A big, domed head, creased brow, sad-looking eyes and long, soft ears give it a look that is hard to miss.
At home, the Basset Hound is mild, agreeable and tolerant, showing its loyalty through steady companionship. It is very good with children and other dogs, and stays fairly relaxed around strangers. Because a Basset Hound can be stubborn, training takes reasonable patience and steady practice.
Daily exercise needs are modest, though regular mental work helps keep it occupied. Be ready for frequent, loud barking and heavy drooling, as both are part of life with a Basset. Its short, straight, smooth single coat sheds lightly, yet it still needs routine grooming to stay in good shape.

general.name: Australian Cattle Dog
general.shortDescription: The Australian Cattle Dog is a hardworking, clever herding breed with very high energy.
general.longDescription:
The Australian Cattle Dog, also called the Blue Heeler, Red Heeler or Queensland Heeler, is a compact, muscular herding breed closely related to the wild Dingo. It stands about 20 inches tall, weighs around 45 pounds and lives about 15 years. Puppies are born with a white coat that turns blue-grey or red, often marked with mottling or speckling.
This is a faithful, agile and persistent dog that is clever enough to outsmart its owner at times. It picks up training fairly easily, which helps when working livestock or heading out as a running partner. At home, it stays alert and protective. It isn't overly clingy with its family, and it gets along reasonably well with children, strangers and other dogs.
This is a tirelessly energetic dog that needs heavy daily exercise and plenty of mental work. It suits an active owner who can keep it busy with work, sport or long runs. Without enough to do, it gets bored quickly and can get into mischief.
Its short, smooth, straight double coat needs very little grooming, though you can expect regular shedding. It barely drools and rarely barks. It has a playful streak when invited and settles reasonably well into daily life as long as its body and mind stay busy.

general.name: Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier is a friendly, active Irish terrier with a wavy, silky coat.
general.longDescription:
The Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier comes from Ireland and has a sturdy, square build. It stands about 18 inches tall, weighs around 35 pounds and lives about 13 years. Longer hair falls over its eyes, paired with a goatee. This is a happy, faithful dog that is very affectionate with its family and very friendly with children.
Its medium-length single coat is silky and wavy, in shades from pale beige to gold. It sheds very little and doesn't drool much, though the coat mats easily and needs frequent grooming to stay tidy. Expect an active dog that needs plenty of daily exercise along with regular mental stimulation.
Around the house, it stays alert and protective without being overly noisy, and it has a playful side. It gets along reasonably well with strangers and other dogs. Because it can be a bit stubborn, training takes steady patience rather than a quick hand, though it responds well to consistent work. It adapts fairly well to different living environments.

general.name: Lhasa Apso
general.shortDescription: The Lhasa Apso is a small, confident Himalayan companion with a very long, silky coat.
general.longDescription:
The Lhasa Apso comes from the Himalayan region, where the breed has existed for over 1,000 years. It is a small, sturdy dog standing about 10 inches tall and weighing around 15 pounds. Its straight, silky single coat grows very long and drapes down both sides of its body, while dark, oval eyes peek through the hair on its face.
Lhasa Apsos worked as sentinels in palaces and monasteries, and that background still shows. They are confident, intelligent and strongly protective, and they'll speak up when something catches their attention without barking constantly. With their own families, they are very affectionate and loyal. Around strangers, children and other dogs, they tend to be polite rather than overly eager.
The Lhasa Apso settles easily into different homes and adapts very well to new routines. It needs regular daily walks and enough mental stimulation to keep a bright mind busy, and it has a playful, entertaining side at home. Training takes steady patience, as its bright, self-assured personality means it isn't always eager to follow orders.
Keeping that long coat tidy takes regular brushing, though the breed sheds very little and rarely drools. With a lifespan of about 14 years, a Lhasa Apso is a long-term companion that brings a watchful eye and close devotion to the household.

general.name: Chesapeake Bay Retriever
general.shortDescription: The Chesapeake Bay Retriever is a watchful, loving sporting dog with a rough, wavy, waterproof coat.
general.longDescription:
The Chesapeake Bay Retriever, often called the Chessie, is a strong sporting breed standing about 25 inches tall and weighing around 70 pounds. It lives about 12 years. Its medium-length, wavy coat is rough, oily and waterproof, in chocolate brown, sedge or deadgrass, paired with yellow-amber eyes.
Used as a hunting dog for duck retrieval in the Mid-Atlantic, the Chessie has high energy and high mental stimulation needs. It has a tenacious, independent streak, yet it is very easy to train. Those qualities make it a capable worker and watchdog.
At home, it is loving with its family and adapts well to different living environments. It stays vigilant and protective, lets out a warning bark when needed and has a lively, playful side. Around children, strangers and other dogs, it tends to be measured rather than instantly warm.
That single coat sheds noticeably and needs regular brushing to keep it in good shape, though the breed doesn't drool much. Keep up with its need for daily activity and mental work, and it settles well between the field and family life.

general.name: Pointer
general.shortDescription: The Pointer is an athletic, faithful sporting dog used to point game birds.
general.longDescription:
The Pointer is an athletic sporting breed used for centuries to point game birds. It stands about 25 inches tall, weighs around 60 pounds and lives about 15 years. Fast and agile, it makes a good partner for runners and active families. Its short, smooth, straight single coat comes in solid and patterned colours. It sheds regularly, needs little grooming and doesn't drool much.
The Pointer has sharp instincts and is very easy to train, with a hardworking but relaxed nature. It adapts well to both rural and urban settings. With its family, it is faithful and very affectionate, and it gets along very well with other dogs. It welcomes strangers easily and does reasonably well with children.
It is alert enough to let you know when someone is at the door without being overly noisy or territorial. Playful and energetic, the Pointer needs plenty of daily exercise and mental stimulation to stay settled indoors. Give it space to run and regular work to focus on, and its calm, sociable side comes through at home.

general.name: Collie
general.shortDescription: The Collie is an affectionate, vocal herding dog that learns quickly and suits family life.
general.longDescription:
The Collie is a member of the Herding group with a background working sheep. A typical Collie stands around 25 inches tall, weighs about 65 pounds and lives for roughly 13 years. They are agile dogs with a dignified, faithful character.
The breed comes in two coat varieties: the rough Collie with its straight, medium-length coat and the shorter smooth Collie. Both varieties appear in sable and white, tricolour, blue merle and white.
Collies have a wedge-shaped head, mobile ears and expressive almond eyes. At home they are affectionate, loyal and notably gentle with children. That steady nature fits family life well.
They need moderate daily exercise and mental stimulation, and they adapt well to different living setups. Because they are intelligent and eager to please, training is fairly easy, particularly when you stick to gentle methods.
Expect moderate shedding and regular brushing, with very little drooling. Noise is the main catch. Collies bark a great deal and stay moderately alert to their surroundings, and they tend to be measured with strangers and other dogs.
Playful and fond of company, a Collie suits an active family that wants a responsive, devoted dog and doesn't mind a lot of barking.

general.name: Bull Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Bull Terrier is a muscular, energetic terrier with an egg-shaped head and playful nature.
general.longDescription:
The Bull Terrier is a sturdy, big-boned member of the Terrier group. Standing around 20 inches tall and weighing about 60 pounds, it is a muscular, balanced dog with an agile, jaunty stride and a lifespan of around 13 years. Bull Terriers are happy, playful and devoted, though they can be mischievous and stubborn.
The breed's clearest feature is its long, egg-shaped head, paired with erect pointed ears and small triangular eyes. Its short, straight, smooth coat comes in white or any other colour, often with brindle striping. Grooming needs are light and they don't drool, though shedding is moderate.
Bull Terriers need plenty of daily exercise and mental stimulation, so they fit best in active homes where they spend lots of time with their owners. Training takes moderate effort and calls for a firm, loving approach. Because they aren't sociable with other dogs, early socialisation with both dogs and people is important.
Around people, they are affectionate with family and usually friendly towards strangers, with a moderate tolerance for children. Adaptability, barking and protective instincts all sit in the middle range. When their needs for activity, training and company are met, they are comical, loyal housemates.

general.name: Irish Wolfhound
general.shortDescription: The Irish Wolfhound is a large, quiet, dignified hound originally used to hunt wolves.
general.longDescription:
The Irish Wolfhound belongs to the Hound group and was once used to hunt wolves. This is a very large breed at around 30 inches tall and 115 pounds, with a muscular, Greyhound-like build made for speed. Its rough, wiry, medium-length coat comes in white, grey, brindle, red, black and fawn. Its average lifespan is short at around 7 years.
At home, Irish Wolfhounds are relaxed, dignified and very affectionate with their family. They tend to be sociable with other dogs, moderately good with children and moderately friendly towards strangers. Barking is rare, so they are quiet housemates, but their protective instincts are high. Brave and watchful, they stay closely tuned to what happens around them.
The wiry coat needs only occasional grooming, shedding is moderate and drooling stays low. Activity needs are steady rather than extreme, so they do well with regular daily exercise and enough to keep their minds busy. Training takes a patient, consistent approach. Even with a calm disposition, owning a dog of this size is a major commitment, best suited to people ready for a big, watchful hound.

general.name: Irish Setter
general.shortDescription: The Irish Setter is a friendly, energetic sporting dog with a wavy, silky mahogany coat.
general.longDescription:
The Irish Setter is a gundog from the Sporting group with over 200 years as both a hunting partner and family pet. They reach around 25 inches in height, weigh about 65 pounds and often live to 14 years. Long, sinewy legs give them speed and agility, and their medium-length, wavy, silky coat comes in mahogany or chestnut.
Irish Setters are loving, outgoing dogs that are happy around almost everyone. They are very affectionate with their families, great with children and sociable with both strangers and other dogs. Playful and always keen on a game of fetch, they adapt well to different homes, while barking and protective instincts stay moderate.
Energy is the biggest commitment. Irish Setters have very high exercise needs and want plenty of mental stimulation to stay settled. Because they are rugged, bold and eager to please, training is fairly easy with patient, positive methods. Their silky coat needs regular brushing, shedding is moderate and they drool very little.

general.name: Cane Corso
general.shortDescription: The Cane Corso is a loyal, vigilant guardian with Roman roots.
general.longDescription:
The Cane Corso belongs to the Guardian group, with a history going back to ancient Rome. At roughly 25 inches tall and 50 pounds, it is a muscular, agile dog with a lifespan of around 10 years. Its short, straight, smooth coat needs minimal grooming and sheds lightly, though drooling is moderate.
With its family, the Cane Corso is dignified, intelligent and loving, showing strong affection to the people it knows. Because it pairs eagerness to please with a confident, assertive temperament, early socialisation and steady training are essential. Training itself is fairly straightforward. Protective instincts are very high, so it stays calm, vigilant and closely alert.
Plan for plenty of daily exercise, as the Cane Corso has high activity needs and enjoys regular mental engagement. Around strangers it tends to be reserved and discerning. It usually gets on reasonably well with children and other dogs, and it adjusts to different living setups without much trouble. Barking is occasional rather than constant. Given consistent guidance and daily activity, the Cane Corso is a steady, devoted companion.

general.name: Chow Chow
general.shortDescription: The Chow Chow is a quiet, watchful Chinese guardian with a thick mane and a blue-black tongue.
general.longDescription:
The Chow Chow is an all-purpose Guardian breed from ancient China with a muscular, deep-chested build. Full-grown dogs stand 20 inches tall, weigh 60 pounds and have a fairly short lifespan of 10 years. You can spot one quickly by its blue-black tongue, stiff-legged walk and deep-set almond eyes that give the face a serious scowl.
A thick, straight, rough double coat forms a heavy mane around the head and shoulders. Coats come in red, black, blue, cinnamon and cream. People often compare Chow Chows to cats because they keep themselves clean and have little doggy odour, though they do shed and drool moderately and need regular brushing.
At home, a Chow Chow is loyal and affectionate with its family, yet aloof with strangers and often unsociable with other dogs. Strong protective instincts make it a very watchful breed, though it is quiet and rarely barks.
Exercise, training and mental stimulation needs are all moderate, and it adapts reasonably well to city living. With steady socialisation, this intelligent, dignified dog becomes a reliable companion that can live comfortably with children and enjoy moderate playtime.

general.name: Cairn Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Cairn Terrier is a lively, watchful Scottish earthdog bred to root out small prey.
general.longDescription:
The Cairn Terrier started out in Scotland as a working earthdog, hunting foxes and other small prey among rocky ground. Measuring 10 inches tall and weighing 14 pounds, it packs a tough, compact frame that suits both outdoor games and quiet time on a lap. Its medium-length double coat has a rough, wiry top layer over a soft undercoat. Coat care is light, it sheds only modestly and it doesn't drool.
At home, a Cairn Terrier is happy, playful and very affectionate with its family, wanting close contact with the people it lives with. It settles into most family routines and handles visitors, kids and other dogs reasonably well. Strong watchful instincts mean it barks often, so expect a vocal companion.
Curious and clever, this Terrier loves exploring the garden and brings plenty of lively energy to daily life. With a lifespan of 15 years, it does well on moderate exercise and regular mental stimulation. Training takes moderate effort because of its independent thinking, though it stays loyal and engaged with owners who spend plenty of time with it.

general.name: Basenji
general.shortDescription: The Basenji is a clean, independent African hound that communicates with a yodel-like sound.
general.longDescription:
Often called Africa's barkless dog, the Basenji is a graceful, agile Hound with a dignified manner. It stands 15 inches tall, weighs 25 pounds and lives around 14 years. A short, smooth, straight single coat, a tightly curled tail and a wrinkled forehead give it an expressive, almost humanlike look. Instead of barking, it makes a sound somewhere between a chortle and a yodel.
Basenjis are clean, fastidious dogs that groom themselves like cats. They don't drool, shed fairly lightly and rarely need brushing, so coat care takes very little effort. That same cat-like independence carries into daily life and makes training challenging, even though the breed is intelligent.
Daily life with a Basenji calls for plenty of exercise and mental stimulation to match its high energy and agile build. Socially, it sits comfortably in the middle, showing steady affection at home and an even temperament with people and other dogs. It suits active owners who can meet those exercise demands and enjoy a quiet, independent dog with a strong mind of its own.

general.name: Irish Water Spaniel
general.shortDescription: The Irish Water Spaniel is a playful, hardworking Sporting dog known for its curly, waterproof coat.
general.longDescription:
The Irish Water Spaniel is an agile, athletic Sporting dog built for hard work both in the field and in the water. It stands 23 inches tall and weighs 55 pounds. Its rough, liver-coloured single coat grows in tight curls across the body, with longer, looser curls on top of the head and a rat tail. That waterproof coat makes it a strong swimmer, and it sheds very little while drooling only lightly.
At home, this brave, happy breed is deeply affectionate with its family and full of playful energy. It adapts easily to different households and stays very quiet, rarely barking. While it can be a little more reserved with unfamiliar people and dogs than with its own family, it makes a warm, lively companion around the house and outdoors.
Training is one of the easiest parts of living with this hardworking dog, so it suits both novice and experienced owners. Because it needs plenty of mental stimulation, it does best with regular activity and tasks alongside moderate daily exercise. Its curly coat needs moderate grooming to stay in shape, and the breed typically lives around 13 years.

general.name: Polish Lowland Sheepdog
general.shortDescription: The Polish Lowland Sheepdog is a confident, adaptable herding dog with a long, shaggy double coat.
general.longDescription:
Known in Poland as the PON, short for Polski Owczarek Nizinny, the Polish Lowland Sheepdog is a confident, lively Herding breed with a sturdy, muscular build. It stands 20 inches tall, weighs 40 pounds and lives around 13 years. It has a very long, wavy, rough double coat over a soft, dense undercoat, with shaggy hair that often partially covers the eyes.
That heavy coat sheds fairly lightly and the breed drools little, though keeping the long hair in order takes frequent grooming. It is highly adaptable and settles easily into both country and city homes. Strong protective instincts make it an alert watchdog, and it barks often when something catches its notice.
With its own family, a Polish Lowland Sheepdog is devoted, playful and very affectionate, and it keeps the reliable nature of a working herding dog. Outside its immediate household, it stays reasonably friendly without being overly forward.
This intelligent breed needs plenty of mental stimulation alongside moderate daily exercise to keep its sharp mind busy. It can be a bit stubborn at times, yet it is fairly easy to train and responds well to consistent, positive reinforcement.

general.name: Norwich Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Norwich Terrier is a small, vigilant English terrier bred to catch rats.
general.longDescription:
The Norwich Terrier comes from Norwich in England, where it worked as an earthdog hunting rats. It stands 10 inches tall and weighs around 12 pounds, with a stocky body and a rough, wiry double coat that only needs occasional grooming and sheds a moderate amount. Its pointed, upright ears set it apart from its close relative, the Norfolk Terrier.
That ratting background still shows in a tough, fearless streak. Norwich Terriers are curious and vigilant, quick to notice anything unusual around the house. They work well as watchdogs and bark quite often, so expect a fairly vocal dog.
They have high energy for such a small dog and need plenty of daily exercise alongside mental stimulation. Games of fetch and active play suit them well. Once they have had a proper run, they are just as happy to curl up on a lap.
Around people, the Norwich Terrier is faithful, playful and very affectionate. It is good with children, friendly with strangers and generally gets along fine with other dogs. The breed adapts well to both city and country living and typically lives for around 14 years.
Training takes patience because these terriers are clever and can be stubborn. Short, positive sessions tend to get the best results and keep their minds busy. Owners who make time for daily activity and games get a sturdy, lively housemate in return.

general.name: German Pinscher
general.shortDescription: The German Pinscher is a muscular, lively working dog that learns very quickly.
general.longDescription:
The German Pinscher began life as a rat catcher and became the prototype for several other pinscher breeds. Standing about 20 inches tall and weighing around 35 pounds, it has a muscular, streamlined body, dark eyes and a long, wedge-shaped head. Its short, smooth coat comes in red, black or blue with red markings, needs very little grooming and sheds moderately.
Now classed in the Working group, this brave, athletic dog moves with a strong, easy stride and takes well to varied tasks. It is intelligent, very easy to train and picks things up quickly. Most German Pinschers live around 13 years.
At home, a German Pinscher is playful and very affectionate with its own family. Strong protective instincts make it a watchful guardian, and it can be reserved around people it does not know. It usually gets along with children and other dogs, and adapts reasonably well to different living setups.
The real commitment is energy rather than coat care. This breed has a high drive to stay busy and needs vigorous daily exercise alongside regular mental challenges. Active owners who enjoy training will find a lively, responsive partner, while quieter households will struggle to wear it out.

general.name: Ibizan Hound
general.shortDescription: The Ibizan Hound is a leggy, polite Spanish rabbit hunter that sprints fast and leaps high.
general.longDescription:
The Ibizan Hound comes from the Balearic Islands of Spain, where it hunted rabbits by sprinting and leaping. Standing about 25 inches tall and weighing around 50 pounds, it has a lean, deer-like build, a long head and large, upright ears often compared to ancient Egyptian art. Its short, smooth wire coat is red, white or a mix of both, paired with amber or caramel eyes and rosy skin on the nose, lips and eye rims.
Indoors, the breed is relaxed, polite and very affectionate with its family. It is especially sociable with other dogs, enjoys play and adapts well to different environments. Grooming takes almost no effort because the coat sheds lightly and needs very little brushing. Most Ibizan Hounds live for about 13 years.
Where this hound asks a lot of its owner is exercise and mental work. It needs heavy daily activity, room to run freely and plenty of stimulation to stay settled, along with patient training. Without that outlet, its energy is hard to manage, so it belongs in an active home with space.

general.name: Presa Canario
general.shortDescription: The Presa Canario is a large, independent guardian with strong protective instincts and calm confidence.
general.longDescription:
The Presa Canario is a large molossoid dog standing around 25 inches tall and weighing about 95 pounds, with an average lifespan of around 10 years. It has a solid, well-proportioned body, a rectangular outline and a black mask on the face. Its short, smooth coat needs very little grooming, though owners should expect heavy drooling.
Historically used to herd cattle, the breed now sits in the Guardian group and brings very strong protective instincts to the job. It tends to stay calm and watchful, holding a firm stance when alert. Its low, deep bark easily warns off intruders.
This is an independent, self-assured dog with little interest in play. Even within its own household, it is fairly reserved in showing affection. It stays wary of strangers and is not suited to homes with children or other dogs.
Daily exercise needs are fairly low, paired with a moderate need for mental stimulation. Because the breed does not adapt easily to changes in routine or surroundings, it does best in a steady, predictable home.
Training takes steady work because a Presa Canario can be stubborn and needs a confident, experienced handler. This is a serious guardian for someone who understands independent dogs and wants a calm, watchful presence.

general.name: Saluki
general.shortDescription: The Saluki is a slim, swift hound prized by kings for thousands of years.
general.longDescription:
For thousands of years, the Saluki was kept by kings as a hunting hound. Standing around 25 inches tall and weighing about 55 pounds, it has a slim but sturdy build, long legs and easy athletic balance. Built for speed, this hound is a swift sprinter that loves a chase. Its large, oval eyes give the face a warm expression, and its short, smooth coat comes in many colours and patterns with minimal grooming and light shedding.
At home, a Saluki is gentle, dignified and very affectionate with its family, yet clearly independent. It handles different climates and environments reasonably well and typically lives for around 14 years. Protective instincts are very low, so nobody gets a Saluki to guard the house.
Living with one means accepting that independent streak and bringing patience and understanding to training. A Saluki needs plenty of physical exercise along with very high mental stimulation to stay content. It is not a breed that thrives on strict obedience, and it does best with owners who appreciate an athletic, self-directed hound.

general.name: Boerboel
general.shortDescription: The Boerboel is a 175-pound South African guardian with a calm temperament and strong protective instincts.
general.longDescription:
The Boerboel was bred in South Africa to guard remote homesteads against dangerous predators. Descended from ancient mastiff-type dogs, it stands around 25 inches tall and weighs about 175 pounds, with a lifespan of roughly 10 years. It has a broad, blocky head, strong jaws and a muscular build, yet moves with more agility than many other mastiffs.
With its family, the Boerboel is relaxed and very affectionate, and it usually gets along well with children. It has strong protective instincts and takes guarding seriously. Combined with its size and strength, that makes it a poor fit for first-time dog owners.
Boerboels are intelligent and fairly easy to train, though they can grow overly dominant without early training and socialisation. They need regular mental work and plenty of interaction with their owners. Most are fairly neutral around strangers, and they are not very sociable with other dogs.
Coat care is simple. The short, smooth single coat lies straight and needs little grooming, though it sheds moderately. Boerboels also drool a fair amount.
Exercise needs, playfulness and barking are all moderate, and the breed adapts reasonably well to different homes. For an experienced owner prepared to put in the early work, a Boerboel is a loyal and confident guardian.

general.name: Bearded Collie
general.shortDescription: Bred in Scotland, the Bearded Collie is a lively herding dog with a long, shaggy coat.
general.longDescription:
Known as the Beardie, the Bearded Collie is a medium-sized herding dog from Scotland. It stands about 20 inches tall, weighs around 50 pounds and lives roughly 13 years. Its long, silky single coat falls in shaggy waves, and its expression often looks dreamy and distant. That coat sheds moderately and needs frequent grooming, though Beardies hardly drool.
Beardies are affectionate, playful and very good with children and other dogs, and most are friendly with strangers. They adapt well to different households as long as they get plenty of outdoor exercise. Expect noise, because this is a vocal breed that barks often.
Intelligent and independent, a Bearded Collie can be wilful, so training takes patience and variety to keep it from getting bored. Give it regular mental work alongside daily exercise, and it is a lively, amusing companion for an active home.

general.name: Puli
general.shortDescription: Agile and faithful, the Puli is a compact herding dog with a long, corded coat.
general.longDescription:
The Puli is a compact, agile herding dog standing about 15 inches tall and weighing roughly 30 pounds. Its long, rough double coat forms naturally into dense, woolly, weatherproof cords. Pulik shed very little and barely drool, though looking after those cords takes a lot of grooming.
Bred to work closely with people, the Puli is light-footed enough to be nicknamed the acrobat of the dog world. It is easy to train because it learns fast and likes to please. Physical exercise needs are moderate, yet its need for mental stimulation is very high, so it needs regular training or mental work to stay occupied.
Pulik are faithful and very affectionate with their families, and they adapt well to different living environments. They have strong protective instincts, while barking and playfulness are both average. With children, other dogs and strangers, they are moderately sociable, though they can be a little reserved around people they don't know.
With a lifespan of about 13 years, the Puli is a loyal, playful companion for an owner ready to match its sharp mind and high grooming needs.

general.name: Lakeland Terrier
general.shortDescription: From England's Lake District, the Lakeland Terrier is a brave, confident small dog with a wiry coat.
general.longDescription:
The Lakeland Terrier comes from England's Lake District, where farmers originally kept it to work in packs protecting livestock from foxes. It stands about 15 inches tall, weighs around 17 pounds and lives roughly 14 years. Despite its compact size, it has a sturdy, square build on long legs in the British terrier mould, and it walks with a cocky swagger.
You can recognise a Lakeland Terrier by its rectangular head, folded V-shaped ears and the mischievous look in its eyes. Its short, rough wire double coat comes in several colours and often has a saddle mark across the back. Grooming and shedding are both low, and the breed hardly drools.
Around the house, Lakelands are playful, confident and very affectionate with their families, and they adapt well to different homes and routines. Sociability with children, other dogs and strangers is moderate, as are their barking and protective instincts.
A Lakeland Terrier needs moderate daily exercise alongside plenty of mental stimulation to keep its sharp mind occupied. Training takes a moderate amount of patience and consistency. Brave and friendly, it carries the confidence of a much larger dog in a 17-pound frame.

general.name: Smooth Fox Terrier
general.shortDescription: A playful, independent dog bred for British foxhunts, the Smooth Fox Terrier has a short, smooth coat.
general.longDescription:
Originally bred for traditional foxhunts in Britain, the Smooth Fox Terrier is often called the gentleman of the terrier world. It stands around 15 inches tall, weighs about 17 pounds and lives roughly 14 years. It has a V-shaped head and a short, straight, smooth single coat that lies dense and flat, mostly white with black, tan or black-and-tan markings. Grooming needs are low and it hardly drools, though the coat sheds moderately.
In the home, Smooth Fox Terriers are very affectionate with their families and have strong protective instincts. They are also very vocal, so frequent barking is part of living with one. Around children, other dogs and strangers they are moderately sociable, balancing a friendly nature with a clear independent streak.
This is a playful, energetic terrier that needs plenty of daily physical exercise alongside moderate mental stimulation. It adapts well to different living environments as long as it gets enough activity and interaction. Training takes moderate effort because its independent nature asks for steady patience. Give it enough to do and you get a lively, entertaining companion.

general.name: Mexican hairless dog
general.shortDescription: The Mexican hairless dog is an active, affectionate companion with minimal grooming needs.
general.longDescription:
Also called the Xoloitzcuintli (pronounced show-low-eats-QUEENT-lee), the Mexican hairless dog goes back over 3,000 years, when the Aztecs treated it as a sacred dog of the gods. Today it is a Companion breed that typically stands 15 inches tall, weighs 35 pounds and lives around 15 years, though it comes in toy, miniature and standard sizes.
There are two coat types. The hairless variety has smooth, tough skin, while the coated type has short, flat hair. Colours include black, grey-black, red, liver and bronze. Under that sleek frame is a strong, rugged dog, and its forehead often wrinkles when it's concentrating.
At home, the Mexican hairless dog is relaxed, faithful and very affectionate with its family. It makes an alert watchdog with a moderate barking habit and adapts well to different homes. Around children, strangers and other dogs, it's moderately sociable, with a playful streak.
With smooth skin or a short, flat coat, grooming is minimal. The breed barely sheds and doesn't drool. It still needs plenty of daily exercise and mental stimulation, though, and it's fairly easy to train.

general.name: Welsh Springer Spaniel
general.shortDescription: The Welsh Springer Spaniel is an active red and white Sporting breed, warm with family and cautious around strangers.
general.longDescription:
The Welsh Springer Spaniel is a medium-sized bird dog from the Sporting group that works well in the field and settles happily at home. Standing 18 inches tall and weighing 45 pounds, it sits between a Cocker Spaniel and an English Springer, with a lifespan of 14 years. Its medium-length, wavy, silky double coat comes in red and white. Waterproof, weatherproof and thornproof, that coat handles different climates and rough terrain well.
At home, a Welshie is happy, relaxed and very affectionate with its family. It's great with children, gets along well with other dogs and adapts easily to different households. Around strangers, though, it's very reserved and cautious, so it won't rush up to greet everyone it meets. It has a playful side and will bark to alert you, without being noisy or overly watchful.
This is an active breed that needs plenty of daily exercise and mental stimulation to stay happy, so it suits households that enjoy time outdoors. Training is usually straightforward because the Welsh Springer Spaniel learns very easily. Grooming takes relatively little effort for a medium-length double coat, though you can expect moderate shedding and light drooling.

general.name: Borzoi
general.shortDescription: The Borzoi is a quiet, independent sighthound with a silky coat and strong prey drive.
general.longDescription:
Once known as the Russian Wolfhound, the Borzoi is a large sighthound from the Hound group, bred to be swift and tough enough to chase and pin fierce quarry. It stands around 25 inches tall, weighs about 80 pounds and lives roughly 12 years. Its medium-length, silky, curly single coat needs relatively little grooming, though it sheds moderately. Drooling isn't an issue.
Indoors, the Borzoi is quiet, dignified and calm. It's faithful and loving in a gentle way, preferring a peaceful home to rough play. It generally gets on well enough with children, strangers and other dogs without being overly eager, and it settles into a steady routine.
Outdoors, that strong prey drive comes out, so it needs ample fenced space to run safely. This breed also needs plenty of daily exercise and mental stimulation. Training is often challenging because the Borzoi has a cat-like independence, so it takes patience and consistency.

general.name: Greater Swiss Mountain Dog
general.shortDescription: The Greater Swiss Mountain Dog is a friendly, vigilant Working dog with a tricolour coat.
general.longDescription:
The Greater Swiss Mountain Dog is a large, strong Working breed with a short, smooth, straight coat in black, red and white tricolour. It typically stands 25 inches tall, weighs 115 pounds and lives around 10 years, which is on the shorter side for dogs.
Historically, Swissies worked as dependable herders, drafters and all-round pasture dogs. Even with that heavy build and strength, they are agile enough to move flocks across mountainous terrain, and they still carry the drive of a working dog.
Around people, the Greater Swiss Mountain Dog is faithful, reliable and very affectionate. It gets along well with children and is very friendly towards strangers, yet it still has strong protective instincts and stays alert. It has a playful side too, while its sociability with other dogs, adaptability and barking are all moderate.
The short single coat takes little grooming, though you can expect moderate shedding and moderate drooling. To stay content, this breed needs plenty of daily exercise and mental stimulation, and it's fairly easy to train.

general.name: Briard
general.shortDescription: The Briard is a quiet, confident Herding dog with a long coat that needs frequent grooming.
general.longDescription:
The Briard is a confident, intelligent and faithful dog from the Herding group. People often describe the breed as a heart wrapped in fur, and it brings a watchful presence to a home while staying very quiet.
Standing around 25 inches tall and weighing about 80 pounds, the Briard has a muscular frame and a nimble gait for its size. Its long, wavy, rough double coat comes in grey, tawny or black. The hair parts naturally down the middle above expressive eyebrows and a full beard, and the face has a frank, questioning look.
Bred to manage large flocks, the Briard still carries strong protective instincts. It's particularly watchful around children, whom it tends to treat as part of its flock. It shows steady, measured affection at home and gets along reasonably well with children, strangers and other dogs without being overly outgoing.
That long double coat sheds very little, and the breed only drools lightly. Keeping all that hair tidy takes frequent, regular grooming, though.
Day to day, the Briard needs a moderate amount of exercise and mental stimulation. It adapts reasonably well to different routines and mixes a playful streak with a calmer side.
The Briard typically lives around 12 years. Training sits in the middle for difficulty, though a strong work drive and spirited energy can be overwhelming for first-time owners.

general.name: Dutch Shepherd
general.shortDescription: The Dutch Shepherd is a lively, watchful herding dog bred for farm work and long active days.
general.longDescription:
Bred for herding and general farm work, the Dutch Shepherd is a muscular medium dog that stands around 25 inches tall and weighs about 60 pounds. It has the build to run and work through the day, which is why many now do obedience, dog sports and search and rescue. Most live around 13 years.
At home, this breed is very affectionate with its family, playful and strongly protective. It stays alert without barking much, and it adapts well to different routines. Around children, strangers and other dogs it is moderately sociable. It can have an independent, stubborn streak now and then, though its intelligence makes it easy to train.
The biggest commitment is energy. Exercise and mental stimulation needs are both at the top of the scale, so a Dutch Shepherd suits active owners who have time for long outings and regular work to keep its mind busy. Its short, straight, rough double coat sheds moderately and needs little grooming, and drooling is low.

general.name: Wirehaired Pointing Griffon
general.shortDescription: The Wirehaired Pointing Griffon is a friendly, obedient gundog with a wiry coat built for fieldwork.
general.longDescription:
The Wirehaired Pointing Griffon is a medium sporting dog bred for hunting and fieldwork. It stands around 20 inches tall and weighs about 50 pounds. Its rough, medium-length wire double coat sheds moderately and needs fairly little grooming, though the breed does drool a moderate amount.
The preferred coat colour is steel grey with brown markings. A prominent moustache and bushy eyebrows sit over round, eager eyes. The harsh texture is practical for working in the field.
At home, the Wirehaired Pointing Griffon is very affectionate, playful and faithful. It is great with children and welcoming towards strangers, while sociability with other dogs sits closer to the middle. It adapts easily between fieldwork and family life, with moderate barking and moderate protective instincts.
Training comes easily to this obedient, quick-witted dog, which helps because both its exercise and mental stimulation needs are very high. It needs steady daily activity and real tasks to stay settled. For active families and hunters who can keep up with that pace, the Wirehaired Pointing Griffon is a loyal, spirited companion with a long typical lifespan of around 14 years.

general.name: Petit Basset Griffon
general.shortDescription: The Petit Basset Griffon is a happy, shaggy French hound bred for rabbit hunting with a loud voice.
general.longDescription:
The Petit Basset Griffon is a small, sturdy French hound with a happy, lively temperament. It stands about 15 inches tall and weighs around 35 pounds, with a long, rough, wavy double coat that gives it a shaggy look. Despite all that hair, it sheds lightly, needs little grooming and rarely drools.
Developed in the Vendée region of France to hunt rabbits, the breed is low to the ground with a proudly held head and a sabre tail. It also has a loud bark and uses it often, which matters if you have close neighbours.
Socially, this hound is an extrovert. It gets on very well with children and other dogs, and it is affectionate with family and friendly with strangers. Playful by nature, it is also alert and fairly protective, so it tends to notice and announce anything unusual around the house.
The Petit Basset Griffon adapts well to both rural and urban homes, as long as it gets regular exercise and mental stimulation to keep its busy mind occupied. Training takes moderate patience. Most live around 15 years, so active households get many years with a lively companion.

general.name: Lagotto Romagnolo
general.shortDescription: The Lagotto Romagnolo is a loving, relaxed Italian truffle dog with a curly coat that barely sheds.
general.longDescription:
The Lagotto Romagnolo comes from Italy, where it was bred to hunt truffles. It is a small sporting dog with a rough, curly, medium-length double coat that resembles human hair more than typical fur.
Adults stand around 18 inches tall and weigh about 30 pounds. A beard, whiskers and heavy eyebrows can make the dog look like a stuffed toy, yet underneath is a sturdy worker with a sharp sense of smell built for rooting out truffles.
At home, the Lagotto Romagnolo is deeply affectionate with its family and generally relaxed. It stays observant of its surroundings with moderate protective instincts, and its adaptable nature helps it settle comfortably into different living setups.
Because the breed is intelligent and eager to please, training is fairly straightforward. Indoors, it is relatively quiet, rarely drools and needs modest grooming, while shedding is minimal.
This is a playful dog that gets on very well with other dogs and is friendly towards strangers, though its patience with children is more moderate. Even with its relaxed side indoors, it still has high exercise and mental stimulation needs and enjoys games that put its nose to work.
The Lagotto Romagnolo typically lives around 15 years. For owners who can provide daily outings and plenty of mental work, it is a devoted and lively companion.

general.name: Treeing Walker Coonhound
general.shortDescription: The Treeing Walker Coonhound is a brave, intelligent hunting hound built for speed and heavy exercise.
general.longDescription:
The Treeing Walker Coonhound is a brave, intelligent and polite hunting dog that stands about 25 inches tall and weighs around 60 pounds.
Built to cover long distances at speed, it has a streamlined body, long muscular legs and strong hindquarters. That athletic frame makes it a quick, agile runner in the field.
Indoors, this hound is sweet, gentle and very affectionate with its family. It is playful, adapts well to different homes and gets on very well with children and other dogs. Training comes easily, though friendliness with strangers is more moderate.
Exercise and mental stimulation needs are both at the highest level, so this dog needs long, active outings and regular work to stay content. Expect plenty of noise too, as barking frequency is high.
Coat care is about as simple as it gets. Its short, smooth, straight single coat requires almost no grooming, though it sheds moderately and the breed drools a moderate amount. Protective instincts sit in the middle, and typical lifespan is around 13 years.
For active households that can give it real miles outdoors and don't mind a loud hound, the Treeing Walker Coonhound is a steady, loyal companion both in the field and at home.

general.name: Tibetan Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Tibetan Terrier is a watchful, loving companion with a long wavy coat and snowshoe feet.
general.longDescription:
Large, flat feet shaped like snowshoes are the first clue to where the Tibetan Terrier comes from. They evolved to help the dog cross the snowy, mountainous terrain of Tibet, where the breed was linked to Buddhist monasteries and became known as the Holy Dog of Tibet.
Standing 15 inches tall and weighing 25 pounds, the Tibetan Terrier is a small to medium companion dog with a lifespan of 15 years. It has a long, rough, wavy topcoat over a woolly undercoat, so expect regular grooming. It doesn't drool much either.
Around the house, these dogs are loving, faithful and closely bonded to their families. They are observant and vigilant, with strong protective instincts that make them dependable watchdogs. They also adapt well to different living environments, settling in wherever their people live.
Plan to put time into keeping a Tibetan Terrier busy. It needs plenty of daily activity and ample mental stimulation to stay occupied, so it fits best with owners who enjoy having an active, watchful dog involved in their day.

general.name: Irish Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Irish Terrier is a brave, dignified red terrier that loves children but doesn't like other dogs.
general.longDescription:
People nicknamed the Irish Terrier the Daredevil of the Emerald Isle for a reason. It is fearless at work, yet dignified, tender and deeply affectionate with its own people at home. This compact terrier stands 18 inches tall, weighs 25 pounds and has a lifespan of 15 years, pairing a sturdy, graceful build with a fiery red coat.
Inside the home, an Irish Terrier is devoted to its family and great with children. Its protective instincts are very strong, so it keeps a vigilant eye on the household, and it adapts well to different living environments. The main caveat is other dogs. Irish Terriers aren't sociable with them, so don't expect one to enjoy mixing with other dogs.
Where you will spend time is keeping an Irish Terrier mentally busy. It is an intelligent dog that needs plenty of mental stimulation to stay engaged and lively. Physical upkeep is much simpler: the rough, wiry double coat sheds lightly, rarely needs grooming and comes with no drooling.

general.name: Standard Manchester Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Standard Manchester Terrier is a sleek, lively black and tan terrier that learns quickly.
general.longDescription:
A long, wedge-shaped head with tan spots above watchful eyes makes the Standard Manchester Terrier easy to recognise. Its short, straight, smooth coat mixes jet black with rich mahogany tan over a sleek, racy body. Standing 15 inches tall and weighing 17 pounds, the breed pairs the streamlined build of a coursing hound with the fearless instincts of a terrier.
The breed comes from Manchester, England, and still adapts comfortably to both city and country living. At home, a Standard Manchester Terrier is deeply affectionate with its family and gets on well with children. It is also playful, alert and protective, keeping a close eye on what goes on around the house.
Training is usually straightforward, because these dogs are intelligent and eager to please. They do need an active routine with plenty of exercise and play to match their lively, athletic nature. They can also be quite vocal, so expect a fair bit of barking.
Coat upkeep is simple. The short single coat sheds lightly and needs little grooming, and the breed doesn't drool. With a typical lifespan of 15 years, the Standard Manchester Terrier is a long-lived, spirited companion for active households.

general.name: Finnish Spitz
general.shortDescription: The Finnish Spitz is a vocal, energetic companion from Finland with a foxy face and golden-red coat.
general.longDescription:
If you want a quiet house, the Finnish Spitz will test your patience. In its native Finland, the breed earned the nickname Barking Bird Dog for the way it tracks and indicates game with its voice. At home, it keeps that habit, communicating with enthusiastic barking and expressive yodels.
Often called a Finkie or Finn, this companion dog stands 18 inches tall, weighs 25 pounds and has a lifespan of 15 years. It has a foxy face, prick ears, a curving plumed tail and a dense, rough, straight double coat in golden-red. Despite its compact size, it is a fearless, lively presence.
Around the family, the Finnish Spitz is sensitive, friendly and deeply affectionate. It is great with children and sociable with other dogs. While it can be wary of strangers, it is not shy, which makes it a vigilant alert dog.
Plan your week around keeping this dog moving. The Finnish Spitz needs a great deal of exercise along with plenty of mental stimulation to stay engaged. Provided it gets enough activity, it adapts well to different living situations.
Coat care takes less work than the thick double coat might suggest, as it needs little grooming and drooling stays low. If you can live with the noise and keep up with its energy, the Finnish Spitz is a lively, attentive companion.

general.name: American Foxhound
general.shortDescription: The American Foxhound is a relaxed, independent hound with speed, endurance and a very loud voice.
general.longDescription:
At home, the American Foxhound is easy company. It has large, soft eyes, a gentle expression and a relaxed, loving demeanour. The breed is great with children and very sociable with other dogs, and it can even get on well with cats.
Its history is tied to Revolutionary heroes and the grand estates of Virginia. Standing 25 inches tall and weighing 65 pounds, with a lifespan of 12 years, this sleek, rangy hound is known for speed and endurance. Long, finely boned legs and a slightly arched loin set it apart from its English cousin.
