Meeting this hound's daily needs takes commitment. American Foxhounds require substantial exercise to prevent depression and destructive behaviours. Once they pick up a scent, their strong prey drive makes them single-minded, so they need careful management. They are also very vocal, with a loud, melodious bawling that neighbours may not welcome.
Coat care is the easy part: the short, straight, smooth single coat rarely needs grooming, and the breed doesn't drool. The harder work is obedience, because these independent dogs can make training and housebreaking challenging, particularly for novice owners.

general.name: Neapolitan Mastiff
general.shortDescription: The Neapolitan Mastiff is a big, wrinkled Guardian dog used as a quiet protector since ancient Rome.
general.longDescription:
The Neapolitan Mastiff belongs to the Guardian group and has worked as a guard dog since ancient Rome. Standing around 30 inches tall and weighing about 130 pounds, it is a big, heavy dog covered in deep wrinkles, with a dignified bearing. Compared with other breeds, its lifespan is short at about 8 years.
Vigilance is its strongest trait. This dog watches its surroundings closely yet rarely barks. At home it is faithful and calm, settling quietly with its family rather than looking for constant play. With proper socialisation, it gets along reasonably well with children, other dogs and strangers, though it stays watchful.
Coat care is straightforward, as the short, smooth, straight single coat needs little grooming and sheds moderately. Drooling is the bigger daily consideration, because the Neapolitan Mastiff is a heavy drooler. Living with one also takes owners prepared for the practical demands of its size.
Daily exercise needs are low, so this isn't a breed built for long runs, though it still benefits from regular mental work to stay occupied. Training takes steady effort and patience, but the dog's intelligence and desire to please help it come along well.

general.name: Bedlington Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Bedlington Terrier is an active, sheep-like Terrier first bred in an English mining shire.
general.longDescription:
Named after the English mining shire where it was first bred, the Bedlington Terrier is easy to recognise by its sheep-like build. Standing about 15 inches tall and weighing around 20 pounds, it has a fleecy, pear-shaped head, tasselled ears, an arched back and a curved, scimitar-shaped tail. Its light, springy movement points to sighthound ancestry, likely from Whippets.
This is an athletic Terrier that needs plenty of daily exercise and active play. Once it has burned off its energy, it settles happily beside its owners indoors and likes being at the centre of family attention. Bedlington Terriers are cheerful, faithful housemates and alert watchdogs with strong protective instincts, and they live a long life of about 14 years.
The medium-length, rough, curly single coat sheds very little, and the breed does not drool. Keeping that crisp coat in shape still takes regular grooming, so owners should expect routine upkeep rather than a wash-and-go dog.

general.name: Parson Russell Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Parson Russell Terrier is a small, clever Terrier with high energy and strong affection.
general.longDescription:
Often shortened to PRT, the Parson Russell Terrier is a small, bold Terrier built for an active life. Standing about 14 inches tall and weighing around 15 pounds, this clever, lively dog packs a big personality into a compact frame. It lives about 15 years and adapts well to different homes as long as its owners keep up with its pace.
Exercise is the biggest daily commitment. Parson Russell Terriers have very high energy and need plenty of movement, from running beside horses to playing hard in the garden. They also need lots of mental stimulation to stay occupied, and because they are playful and quick to learn, training is fairly easy.
Coat care is light compared with the exercise routine. The mostly white, short, smooth, wavy double coat sheds lightly and needs little grooming, and the breed does not drool.
At home, Parson Russell Terriers are very affectionate with their families and get along readily with other dogs. They are reasonably friendly with children and strangers, and they stay alert enough to notice what goes on around them without barking non-stop.

general.name: Spinone Italiano
general.shortDescription: The Spinone Italiano is an affectionate, tolerant Sporting dog bred in Italy for steady field stamina.
general.longDescription:
The Spinone Italiano is a Sporting breed from ancient Italy, developed as a versatile hunting dog with strength and endurance in the field. Standing around 25 inches tall and weighing about 60 pounds, it has a square, solid, muscular frame built for steady stamina rather than speed, and a lifespan of about 10 years.
Its dense, rough, medium-length wire coat has no undercoat and keeps a natural, unclipped look in a range of colours and patterns. Shaggy eyebrows and a tufted beard frame its expressive eyes. Grooming demands are fairly light, though owners should expect moderate shedding and moderate drooling.
At home, the Spinone Italiano is gentle, patient and very affectionate with its family. It gets along well with other dogs and has a tolerant, easy-going manner around children and strangers. Most Spinoni are obedient and fairly easy to train, even if a stubborn streak shows up from time to time.
Day-to-day routines are straightforward to manage. Spinoni need moderate exercise and mental work to stay content, and they rarely bark, which helps them settle into a variety of living situations. They bring a steady, calm presence to the house without demanding constant entertainment.

general.name: Miniature American Shepherd
general.shortDescription: The Miniature American Shepherd is a compact, affectionate Herding dog with high energy.
general.longDescription:
Often described as a smaller Australian Shepherd, the Miniature American Shepherd stands around 15 inches tall, weighs about 30 pounds and lives roughly 13 years. Its medium-length, rough, wavy double coat comes in black, blue merle, red and red merle, often marked with flecks or marbling. Expect moderate shedding and regular brushing, though drooling is low.
Despite its compact size, this Herding dog brings real working drive to family life. It is faithful, playful and very affectionate with its people, and it gets along very well with children and other dogs. Because it adapts easily to different living environments, it can fit into a range of households, while still keeping a watchful eye on the home.
Keeping body and mind busy is the main commitment. Miniature American Shepherds have very high energy and strong herding drive, so they need plenty of daily exercise alongside regular mental work to stay happy. They are intelligent and very easy to train, which makes teaching new skills and routines straightforward for owners willing to put in the time.

general.name: Finnish Lapphund
general.shortDescription: The Finnish Lapphund is a friendly reindeer herder from the Arctic Circle with a double coat.
general.longDescription:
The Finnish Lapphund comes from Finland, where it worked as a reindeer herder in the Arctic Circle. This Herding dog stands about 20 inches tall, weighs around 45 pounds and lives for roughly 14 years. It has a muscular build that can move quickly from a trot into a full gallop. You'll spot the breed by its spitz-like face, thickly furred tail and weatherproof double coat, which is straight, rough and medium in length.
Known as Lappies, these dogs are very affectionate with their families and adapt well to most homes. They get on well with children, are friendly with strangers and are moderately sociable with other dogs. Centuries of dodging reindeer antlers gave them a strong startle reflex. They are vigilant and bark a lot, so they aren't a quiet breed.
Finnish Lapphunds learn quickly and are fairly easy to train. They have moderate needs for exercise, play and mental stimulation. Coat care takes less work than all that fur suggests, as occasional brushing is usually enough, though you should expect heavy shedding and a little drooling.

general.name: Norwegian Elkhound
general.shortDescription: The Norwegian Elkhound is a confident, active spitz Hound with a rough silver-grey double coat.
general.longDescription:
The Norwegian Elkhound is a sturdy, muscular spitz in the Hound group. Its history runs through Norse art and legend, including sailing with the Vikings. Adults stand about 20 inches at the shoulder, weigh around 50 pounds and typically live for 14 years. You'll recognise one by its erect ears, tightly curled tail and dense silver-grey double coat, which is straight, rough and medium in length.
At home, Elkhounds are very affectionate with their families, mixing a sensitive side with some independence. They have strong protective instincts and bark fairly often, which makes them reliable watchdogs. Once introduced, they are friendly with strangers, and they get on moderately well with children and other dogs.
These are active, playful dogs that need plenty of daily exercise and mental work, and many do well in agility and herding trials. They adapt easily and are fairly straightforward to train. Expect moderate shedding, low grooming needs and little drooling.

general.name: Toy Manchester Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Toy Manchester Terrier is a lively Companion dog with a smooth black-and-tan coat.
general.longDescription:
The Toy Manchester Terrier takes its name from Manchester, England, where the breed began. Weighing about 10 pounds and standing 10 inches tall, it is a small Companion dog with a typical lifespan of 15 years. Its build blends the sleek lines of a coursing hound with the keen instincts of a rat terrier. A long, wedge-shaped head and tan spots above the eyes give it a sharp, watchful look. The single coat is short, straight and smooth, coloured jet-black with mahogany tan markings.
Despite its small size, this breed has strong protective instincts and barks fairly often, so it makes an attentive watchdog. Toy Manchester Terriers are very affectionate with their families and usually do well with children. They are moderately sociable with other dogs and can be reserved around strangers. Their adaptable nature helps them settle into different homes.
For a 10-pound dog, this breed has plenty of energy. Toy Manchester Terriers are lively and playful, needing solid daily exercise and moderate mental stimulation. They are intelligent and fairly easy to train. Upkeep is straightforward: they don't drool, shed lightly and need infrequent grooming.

general.name: Silky Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Silky Terrier is a watchful, playful Companion dog from Sydney with a long glossy coat.
general.longDescription:
The Silky Terrier originated in Sydney, Australia, and belongs to the Companion group. Adults stand around 10 inches tall, weigh about 10 pounds and typically live for 15 years. Small as they are, these dogs are sturdy and nimble, pairing a terrier's tenacity with a companion's warmth.
Almond-shaped eyes and erect V-shaped ears give the breed a keen, alert expression. Its long, straight single coat is blue and tan, smooth to the touch and often compared to human hair for its glossy texture. Silky Terriers shed lightly and don't drool, though that long coat needs regular grooming.
At home, Silky Terriers form a strong bond with their families and are very affectionate, while keeping a streak of independence. They are playful, curious and quick on their feet. High adaptability also helps them settle easily into different living environments.
Strong protective instincts make the Silky Terrier a vigilant watchdog, and you should expect a fair amount of barking. Even with that alert nature, the breed is generally friendly towards strangers. It gets on moderately well with children and is moderately sociable with other dogs.
Silky Terriers have moderate needs for physical exercise and mental stimulation, so steady daily activity and playtime keep them occupied. They are fairly easy to train. If you don't mind regular brushing and a vocal watchdog, they are companionable little dogs.

general.name: Keeshond
general.shortDescription: The Keeshond is a friendly spitz from Holland with spectacle markings and a long double coat.
general.longDescription:
The Keeshond is a spitz in the Companion group that comes from Holland, where it lived on canal barges and became a symbol of Dutch patriotism. Adults stand about 18 inches tall, weigh around 40 pounds and typically live for 14 years.
Sharing ancient stock with Pomeranians and Samoyeds, Keeshonden have a square, sturdy build, pointed ears and a plumed tail carried high over the back. Their foxy face carries markings around the eyes known as spectacles, framed by a long, straight, rough double coat.
Sociability is a defining part of the breed. Keeshonden are very affectionate with their families, very playful and welcoming towards strangers. They also get on very well with children and other dogs.
That friendly nature sits alongside strong protective instincts. Keeshonden make vigilant watchdogs and bark fairly often, so they aren't the quietest housemates.
They are very adaptable and very easy to train. Even so, they are lively dogs that need plenty of daily exercise and mental stimulation.
That long double coat needs regular grooming to keep it in order, though Keeshonden shed only moderately. They drool very little, so brushing, exercise and training are the main parts of daily care.

general.name: Welsh Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Welsh Terrier is a friendly, lively terrier originally bred to hunt badgers and otters.
general.longDescription:
The Welsh Terrier is a compact, rugged dog standing 15 inches tall and weighing about 20 pounds. Most live to around 14 years. It has a rough black-and-tan wire double coat of medium length and a noticeable beard. Bred to confront badgers and otters, this terrier stays alert and lively, though it tends to be calmer than many other terrier breeds.
With its own family, the breed is very affectionate and gets along well with children. Welsh Terriers are playful and warm towards strangers, while their sociability with other dogs is moderate. Because they adapt well, they suit both city and country homes.
They have strong protective instincts and bark fairly often, so expect an alert, vocal housemate. Daily exercise needs are high, and they need regular mental stimulation alongside physical activity to stay settled. Because they are intelligent and eager to learn, training is usually straightforward.
Shedding and drooling are both low, which helps keep the house clean. Even so, that rough wire double coat calls for moderate, regular grooming to stay in good condition.

general.name: Leonberger
general.shortDescription: Bred in Germany as a guardian, the Leonberger pairs giant size with a loving, patient temperament.
general.longDescription:
Originating in Germany, the Leonberger is a very large guardian dog standing 30 inches at the shoulder and weighing around 130 pounds. For all its bulk, it moves with an easy, elastic gait. Its long, rough, wavy double coat is waterproof, and males grow a lion-like mane around the neck and chest. One hard reality of the breed is a short lifespan of roughly 7 years.
Leonbergers are loving, happy and patient. They stay closely attached to their families and get along very well with children. Strangers usually get a warm welcome too, while sociability with other dogs is moderate. Even with that friendly streak, they keep strong protective instincts and sound judgement as watchdogs.
They adapt well when given ample room to move. Playfulness, barking and exercise needs are moderate, though these intelligent dogs want plenty of attention and regular mental stimulation. Training is usually easy.
Coat care takes real work, because that dense double coat sheds heavily and needs frequent brushing. Expect moderate drooling as well.

general.name: Affenpinscher
general.shortDescription: Nicknamed the monkey dog, the Affenpinscher packs bold confidence and playful antics into 9 pounds.
general.longDescription:
Often called the monkey dog for its distinctive face, the Affenpinscher is a small companion breed standing 10 inches tall and weighing around 9 pounds. Its rough, fairly short wire single coat looks shaggy and comes in several colours. Most live to around 14 years.
Affenpinschers are brave, loyal and curious, with plenty of confidence for such a small dog. Their amusing habits keep owners entertained, and they are especially warm towards strangers. At home they are affectionate without being clingy, and they generally get along with children and other dogs. They settle well into different households, though their wilful, sometimes domineering streak means training takes steady patience.
Day to day, this is a fairly balanced dog to live with. It enjoys regular play, walks and mental engagement without demanding endless exercise, and it will alert you to visitors without barking constantly. That rough wire coat sheds a fair amount and needs regular grooming to keep its tidy, shaggy shape, though Affenpinschers do not drool.

general.name: Coton de Tulear
general.shortDescription: Quiet, playful and fond of clowning around, the Coton de Tulear loves staying close to its family.
general.longDescription:
Known as the Royal Dog of Madagascar, the Coton de Tulear is a small, sturdy companion dog standing 10 inches tall and weighing about 10 pounds. Its long, wavy, silky white double coat feels soft like cotton, and the breed lives a long time at around 17 years. Cotons have a playful, lighthearted streak and are known for clownish tricks like walking on their hind legs.
This is a happy, very affectionate dog that forms tight bonds with its owners and likes staying close to the family. It gets along very well with children, strangers and other dogs. Cotons are quiet, rarely barking, with moderate protective instincts. They adjust well to different living arrangements, and their intelligence makes training fairly easy.
Exercise and mental stimulation needs are moderate, so keeping one occupied is manageable. Shedding is low and the breed does not drool. The main upkeep is coat care, because that long, wavy double coat needs frequent grooming to stay tidy.

general.name: Beauceron
general.shortDescription: Built for herding and guarding, the Beauceron is a faithful, muscular dog best suited to experienced owners.
general.longDescription:
The Beauceron is a large, muscular herding dog standing about 25 inches tall and weighing around 90 pounds. It combines a rugged, graceful build with a long, chiselled head and dark brown eyes that give it a frank, confident expression. Its short, smooth, straight double coat is black with squirrel-red markings, especially on the feet, which earned the breed the French nickname Bas-Rouge, meaning red stockings. Typical lifespan is around 12 years.
Faithful, loving and obedient, the Beauceron is an intelligent, level-headed watchdog with strong protective instincts. With proper socialisation, it settles into family life well, sharing steady affection with its household and getting along reasonably with children and other dogs. Around strangers, though, it stays naturally reserved and cautious.
This breed is not suited to novice owners. Beaucerons can be dominant, so they need an experienced hand and consistent, confident training to bring out their obedient side. Their biggest daily demand is physical activity, because they have very high exercise needs and plenty of energy to burn. They also appreciate regular mental work and will bark when something warrants their attention.
Even with a short, smooth coat, Beaucerons shed heavily, so expect plenty of loose hair around the house. Moderate, regular grooming helps keep the double coat tidy. They do not drool, which helps keep things cleaner indoors.

general.name: Irish Red and White Setter
general.shortDescription: The Irish Red and White Setter is a lively, friendly bird dog that needs plenty of exercise.
general.longDescription:
Red patches on a white background make the Irish Red and White Setter easy to spot in the field, which is exactly what hunters wanted from this Sporting breed. It has a wavy, silky double coat that doesn't shed much and only needs occasional brushing. Standing 25 inches tall and weighing 45 pounds, it is shorter and stockier than the Irish Setter, with a solid build and a steady stance on point.
Away from work, this is a brave, reliable dog that fits easily into family life. It is very affectionate at home, gets on well with children, strangers and other dogs, and adapts to new routines. It is lively and alert without turning into a constant barker, and it typically lives for 13 years.
Daily exercise is the main commitment. This breed has very high energy and needs plenty of time outdoors, along with regular mental work. It picks up new commands quickly and is easy to train, so channelling that energy is straightforward if you have the time to get outside.

general.name: Black and Tan Coonhound
general.shortDescription: The Black and Tan Coonhound is a relaxed hound bred to track raccoons.
general.longDescription:
Bred to track raccoons at night, the Black and Tan Coonhound follows a trail with a sharp nose and long, velvety ears. This large, athletic Hound stands 25 inches tall, weighs 90 pounds and typically lives for 10 years. Its short, smooth black coat has rich tan markings, including small tan spots above the eyes called pumpkin seeds.
Indoors, this is a relaxed, brave dog that bonds closely with its family and happily spends hours on the sofa. It gets on very well with children and other dogs, settles into home life easily and takes a measured approach to strangers. With an easygoing streak and little guarding instinct, it isn't much of a watchdog. Plan for noise, though: it has a loud, mournful bay and often uses it when left alone.
Steady daily walks and regular mental work keep it happy, and training takes some patience. Grooming is light, though you'll notice some shedding and drool. Outdoors, its strong prey drive takes over once it catches a scent, so a sturdy lead and a secure fence are essential.

general.name: Catahoula Leopard Dog
general.shortDescription: The Catahoula Leopard Dog is an independent, faithful working breed that comes from Louisiana.
general.longDescription:
Named after the Choctaw word for sacred lake, the Catahoula Leopard Dog comes from Louisiana. It belongs to the Working group and stands out for its short, smooth coat, which appears in a wide range of colours and patterns, often paired with bright eyes.
This is a large, muscular dog at 25 inches tall and 75 pounds, built with the agility to work all day. Over the years it has handled herding, guarding, hunting and stock work.
Intelligent and observant, a Catahoula likes to think for itself. It picks up training fairly easily, but its independent streak still calls for firm guidance and early socialisation.
Strong protective instincts make it a vigilant watchdog that can be territorial and will stand up for itself if mistreated. Even so, it is a very quiet dog that rarely barks.
Once it settles into its place in the household, it is faithful, gentle and affectionate with its own family. It adjusts reasonably well to new routines and takes a measured, steady line with children, strangers and other dogs.
Expect very high daily exercise needs and plenty of mental work to match. It is serious on the job and playful at home once tired out. Coat care is light despite regular shedding, and the breed typically lives for 12 years.

general.name: Miniature Bull Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Miniature Bull Terrier is a compact, playful terrier with a loud voice.
general.longDescription:
With its egg-shaped head and mischievous streak, the Miniature Bull Terrier earned its nickname as the Clown Princes of Dogdom. Standing 12 inches tall and weighing 25 pounds, it packs the muscular build and fearless attitude of the standard Bull Terrier into a small frame, with a typical lifespan of 12 years.
This Terrier is happy, playful and very affectionate with its own family, settling smoothly into most household routines. It is more selective with children, strangers and other dogs, and its protective instincts run high for such a small dog.
Upkeep on the short, smooth single coat could hardly be simpler, with minimal brushing and little shedding. Energy is another matter: this breed needs plenty of daily exercise and engaging mental games to stay out of trouble.
Because it is lively and fearless, early socialisation and steady training are important, and teaching new habits takes some persistence. Plan on a vocal companion as well, since Miniature Bull Terriers bark often and make sure you hear them.

general.name: Bouvier des Flandres
general.shortDescription: The Bouvier des Flandres is a brave, independent herding dog originally bred for farm work.
general.longDescription:
Originally bred for farm work, the Bouvier des Flandres is a large, sturdy Herding dog recognisable by its rough, wavy, weatherproof double coat, beard and moustache. Built to handle a range of heavy tasks and still keen on dog sports like herding trials, it stands 25 inches tall, weighs 90 pounds and typically lives for 10 years.
Brave and independent, it takes naturally to watchdog and guardian duties thanks to its strong protective instincts. At home, it is loving yet steady rather than effusive with family, children, strangers and other dogs. It adjusts reasonably well to daily routines, has a measured playful side and stays alert without barking constantly.
Plan on plenty of daily exercise and space to move, along with regular mental tasks to keep it occupied. Although it can show a stubborn streak, it is intelligent and picks up training fairly easily when you use consistent, positive methods. The biggest ongoing chore is coat care: that rough, wavy coat sheds regularly and needs frequent grooming to stay in good order.

general.name: Spanish Water Dog
general.shortDescription: The Spanish Water Dog is a lively, intelligent herding dog from Spain with a curly, rough coat.
general.longDescription:
In its native Spain, the Spanish Water Dog worked as both a herder and a waterfowl retriever, and it still carries that energy today. It stands about 18 inches tall, weighs around 40 pounds and lives for roughly 13 years. Its medium-length single coat is curly, rough and woolly, and it comes in black, brown, beige, white or particolour. Shedding is very low, and drooling is low too.
At home, this happy, lively dog is very affectionate with its family. It is playful and gets on well with children, while staying moderately sociable around other dogs and strangers. It can also act as an alert watchdog, with moderate protective instincts and a moderate amount of barking. Adaptability is moderate as well.
Keeping a Spanish Water Dog busy takes real time. It is intelligent and fairly easy to train, which helps because it needs plenty of daily exercise and a very high amount of mental stimulation. Even though it barely sheds, that curly coat still needs frequent grooming to stay tidy. This Herding breed suits active owners who have room in their week for regular training, outdoor activity and coat care.

general.name: Kuvasz
general.shortDescription: The Kuvasz is a large, faithful Hungarian working dog with a white coat and strong protective instincts.
general.longDescription:
The Kuvasz, pronounced KOO-vahz (plural Kuvaszok, KOO-vah-sock), is a large Working breed from Hungary. Historically, these dogs guarded flocks and kept company with kings. A full-grown Kuvasz stands around 30 inches tall, weighs about 95 pounds and has a lifespan of 10 years. It wears a straight, rough, medium-length double coat in snow-white, with a well-proportioned head.
Despite its size, the Kuvasz is quick and nimble on its feet. It is a brave, faithful guardian with very strong protective instincts, always alert to a threat. Towards its own family it is deeply loving and very affectionate.
Sociability with children, strangers and other dogs is moderate, and so are playfulness and barking. It adapts well to different environments and is easy to train, though its size and vigilance mean owners still need to take its guarding instincts seriously.
Day-to-day care is fairly straightforward for a dog this size. Exercise and mental stimulation needs are moderate, drooling is low and that white double coat needs only occasional grooming, even though it sheds a moderate amount.

general.name: Australian Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Australian Terrier is a brave, lively small terrier with a rough coat.
general.longDescription:
The Australian Terrier is a small, sturdy dog standing about 10 inches tall and weighing roughly 18 pounds, with a lifespan of around 13 years. It has a slightly long torso, dark eyes and a straight, medium-length rough double coat in blue-and-tan, solid red or sandy. A soft, silky topknot sits on the head, while the rougher coat around the neck and forequarters gives extra protection.
For a Terrier, it is notably good with children and affectionate with its family. It is brave and alert, with strong protective instincts for its size, which makes it a capable watchdog. Barking is moderate, and it is moderately sociable with both strangers and other dogs.
That lively terrier streak shows up fast, and it often chases small critters with real determination. It learns quickly, trains fairly easily and does well in performance events. Playfulness, exercise needs and mental stimulation needs are all moderate, and the breed adapts well to different living setups.
Upkeep is one of the easiest parts of owning an Australian Terrier. It barely sheds, it doesn't drool and its rough double coat needs only occasional grooming to stay tidy.

general.name: Japanese Chin
general.shortDescription: The Japanese Chin is a small, dignified companion dog with a silky coat and quiet, cat-like habits.
general.longDescription:
Standing about 10 inches tall and weighing 9 pounds, the Japanese Chin is a small Companion dog with a lifespan of 10 years. A large head, short muzzle and round dark eyes often give it a surprised look. Its straight, silky single coat forms a mane around the neck and shoulders, a plumed tail over the back and decorative pants on the hind legs.
This dignified lapdog has several cat-like habits: it is fastidious, graceful and generally quiet, with little barking. It is very affectionate with its family and very sociable with other dogs, while staying moderately friendly with children and strangers. Protective instincts are moderate too.
The Japanese Chin adapts well to different homes and divides its day easily between playtime and resting. Exercise, mental stimulation and training difficulty are all moderate. It doesn't drool, and despite the silky look, grooming is infrequent, though you can still expect a moderate amount of shedding.

general.name: Redbone Coonhound
general.shortDescription: The Redbone Coonhound is a friendly, relaxed hound with a smooth, short red single coat.
general.longDescription:
The Redbone Coonhound is relaxed and even-tempered indoors, then turns into an eager hunter outside. Standing around 25 inches tall and weighing about 60 pounds, this Hound has a lifespan of 14 years. It has well-defined muscles under a short, smooth, straight single coat in red, paired with long ears and brown eyes.
Around the house, it is a friendly, obedient dog that is very affectionate with its family. It gets on very well with children and other dogs, while staying moderately friendly with strangers. It adapts well to different homes and happily switches between hunting or swimming and lounging. Expect plenty of noise, because this hound barks often.
Exercise needs, playfulness and training difficulty are all moderate, but mental stimulation needs are high, so it does best with regular work for its brain. Coat care is simple, because the short, smooth coat needs little grooming, though shedding and drooling are both moderate.

general.name: American Hairless Terrier
general.shortDescription: A lively, curious terrier from Louisiana, the American Hairless Terrier comes hairless or coated.
general.longDescription:
Despite its name, the American Hairless Terrier comes in both hairless and coated varieties. Hairless dogs have warm, smooth skin and may grow whiskers and eyebrows, while coated ones carry a short, shiny coat. Both types have round, expressive eyes, V-shaped ears and a broad, wedge-shaped head. Adults stand about 15 inches tall and weigh around 20 pounds.
The breed comes from Louisiana and belongs to the Terrier group. It has a long lifespan of about 15 years.
At home, these terriers are very affectionate with their families and do well with children. They are curious, lively and alert to whatever is going on nearby. They also adapt easily to different homes and routines, so they settle into most households without much trouble.
Training tends to be straightforward, as this is an easy breed to teach. Day-to-day upkeep is light too: they don't drool, they barely shed and they rarely need grooming.
The hairless variety does need special attention outdoors, though. Without a coat to shield their smooth skin, hairless dogs need protection from both sunburn and cold weather.

general.name: Australian Kelpie
general.shortDescription: Bred for Australia's open country, the Australian Kelpie is an alert, faithful sheepdog.
general.longDescription:
An Australian Kelpie is happiest when it has a real job to do. This Herding breed has huge reserves of energy and demands plenty of daily physical exercise along with regular mental work. Intelligent and fairly easy to train, Kelpies suit active households that can keep both their bodies and minds busy.
The breed grew out of Collie-type dogs brought from Scotland and developed to cope with the harsh, dry conditions of Australia's wide open spaces. Built for agility and endurance, it has a strong instinct for working sheep, whether out in open fields or inside enclosed yards.
A typical Kelpie stands about 20 inches tall, weighs around 45 pounds and lives roughly 12 years. Its lithe frame carries a short, smooth, straight double coat that rarely needs grooming. You won't deal with drooling, though you should expect a steady amount of shedding from that coat.
Away from work, Kelpies are faithful to their people, even if they aren't overly affectionate. They stay vigilant and protective of their families, keeping a close watch on what happens around them. For such an alert dog, though, the breed is noticeably quiet and rarely barks.

general.name: Dogo Argentino
general.shortDescription: The Dogo Argentino is a powerful, all-white working dog with strong protective instincts and deep loyalty.
general.longDescription:
Originally developed for pack hunting big game such as wild boar and puma, the Dogo Argentino brings serious power to the Working group. Adults stand around 25 inches tall, weigh about 90 pounds and live roughly 12 years. The build reflects strength and athleticism, with a strong head set on a thick neck, a well-proportioned body, muscular limbs and an alert, intelligent expression. Its short, smooth, straight coat is all white, occasionally marked with a small dark patch near one eye.
Around its own family, this brave, lively dog is deeply affectionate, faithful and playful. At the same time, it has very strong protective instincts and keeps a close watch over the people and home it belongs to. Even with that vigilant guardian streak, the Dogo Argentino adapts well to different environments and is generally friendly towards strangers.
Keeping a Dogo Argentino happy takes daily commitment. It needs plenty of vigorous physical exercise alongside regular mental stimulation to stay occupied, though training itself is straightforward because the breed learns quickly. Routine grooming takes very little time with a short single coat, even if you should expect heavy shedding.

general.name: Scottish Deerhound
general.shortDescription: The Scottish Deerhound is a tall, loving hound with a rough wire coat and quiet manners.
general.longDescription:
For a dog standing about 30 inches tall and weighing roughly 90 pounds, the Scottish Deerhound has remarkably gentle manners. Polite, dignified and deeply loving with its own family, it is also very sociable around other dogs. At home it stays quiet, rarely barking, and despite its imposing size it doesn't drool at all.
Known as the "Royal Dog of Scotland", this Hound breed was originally developed to stalk and hunt giant wild red deer, work that called for real strength and endurance. Built on the tall, lean template of the ancient Greyhound, it has a long, tapered head carried on a graceful neck. Its rough wire double coat is often dark blue-grey, a colour long favoured for the breed.
Looking after that coat takes very little work, because the Deerhound rarely needs grooming. One drawback to weigh up before bringing one home is its relatively short lifespan of about 10 years, which gives you fewer years together than many other breeds. For households with the space for a 90-pound hound, though, its quiet ways and deep devotion to its family make it a warm, dignified housemate.

general.name: Tibetan Spaniel
general.shortDescription: The Tibetan Spaniel is a small, confident companion with a silky coat, originally bred to watch monastery walls.
general.longDescription:
On the walls of Tibetan monasteries, the Tibetan Spaniel originally worked as a sentinel. Rather than descending from Western spaniels, this Companion breed traces its ancestry to ancient breeds such as Pekes, Pugs and Lhasas. That watchful history still shows today, giving the dog strong protective instincts despite its small size.
Often nicknamed Tibbies, adults stand about 10 inches tall, weigh around 12 pounds and move with agile purpose. They have blunt muzzles, large expressive eyes and a plumed tail curving over the back. Their straight, silky double coat comes in many colours and forms a "lion's mane" around the neck, yet it needs only light grooming and the breed rarely drools.
At home, the Tibetan Spaniel is happy, confident and intelligent, forming a close bond with its family. It is great with children, playful and generally friendly towards strangers. Because it adapts well to different homes and routines, it settles into a wide range of households. With a long lifespan of about 14 years, owners can expect many years with one.

general.name: Toy Fox Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Toy Fox Terrier is a friendly companion with a terrier's playful energy and sharp watchdog instincts.
general.longDescription:
At 10 inches tall and 7 pounds, the Toy Fox Terrier fits easily on a lap and loves being close to its family. Its straight, smooth coat is short and satin-like, with no undercoat, so grooming takes little time. Beneath that small frame sits real terrier grit. These dogs are spirited and agile, with a tenacious, comical streak that keeps life entertaining.
Around people, Toy Fox Terriers are very affectionate with their own household and just as friendly with strangers. That warmth doesn't stop them acting as watchful guards. They stay alert to anything new around the home and bark often to let you know about it. They adapt easily to different living situations, as long as they get plenty of companionship.
Despite their small size, Toy Fox Terriers need plenty of daily exercise and mental stimulation to keep their clever minds busy. Training is very easy, because they are intelligent and pick up new things quickly. They have a lifespan of 15 years, giving owners a long stretch with a bright, vocal dog that wants to be right in the middle of family life.

general.name: Brussels Griffon
general.shortDescription: The Brussels Griffon is a curious, faithful little companion with an expressive, almost human-like face.
general.longDescription:
The first thing you notice about a Brussels Griffon is its face: large eyes, a bearded muzzle and a funny, self-important attitude. This Companion dog stands 9 inches tall, weighs 9 pounds and has a lifespan of 14 years. Its double coat comes in a smooth type like a Pug's or a rough, wiry type like a Schnauzer's, in red, black-and-reddish-brown (belge), black and tan or black.
Devoted and curious, a Brussels Griffon wants to be right beside its favourite person. These dogs don't cope well with loneliness and stick close around the house. They are affectionate with family, friendly with strangers and eager to play. They adapt well to different homes, though you can expect regular barking when something catches their interest.
Smart and straightforward to train, these alert dogs do best when they get plenty of daily interaction. Because they are small and sensitive, rough play with children isn't a good match, so they tend to suit adult households best.

general.name: Rat Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Rat Terrier is a playful, friendly dog built for active families.
general.longDescription:
Teddy Roosevelt named the Rat Terrier after its roots as a skilled pest hunter. That working background shows in a neat, hardy frame built to move cleanly and keep going all day. A typical dog stands 14 inches tall and weighs 18 pounds, with miniature (10 to 13 inches) and standard (over 13 to 18 inches) sizes. Its short, straight single coat has a smooth sheen, comes in pied patterns and needs little grooming.
Expect plenty of energy and a sharp, curious mind that needs daily work to stay busy. Active games and time outside suit a Rat Terrier well. Training is very easy, because these dogs learn fast and enjoy working with their owners.
This Terrier is very affectionate and playful, getting on warmly with children and strangers as well as its own family. It stays protective of the household and adapts easily to different homes. With a lifespan of 15 years, it makes a loyal, spirited pet for families who match its pace.

general.name: Schipperke
general.shortDescription: The Schipperke is a confident, curious companion from Belgium, bred as a watchdog.
general.longDescription:
In Belgium, people call the Schipperke the 'little captain', a fitting nickname for a confident dog that likes to keep tabs on everything around it. Bred to guard and catch rats, it packs strong jaws, a solid neck and a well-muscled front end into a small frame standing 12 inches tall and weighing 13 pounds. It hunts vermin almost like a cat.
A fox-like head and a bold outline make the breed easy to spot. Its short, straight, rough black double coat grows thickest over the neck, shoulders and legs, giving this small dog real presence. Even with all that fur, grooming stays light. This Companion breed is built tough, with a lifespan of 15 years.
At home, a Schipperke is very affectionate and loyal, settling comfortably into many kinds of households. It has a cheeky, playful side alongside the curiosity that keeps it checking out every corner of the house, and training is fairly straightforward. True to its watchdog roots, it stays highly alert and protective, barking often whenever something new turns up.

general.name: Curly-Coated Retriever
general.shortDescription: The Curly-Coated Retriever is a dignified, independent gundog with a tight curly coat and deep family loyalty.
general.longDescription:
Small, firm curls in black or liver form the Curly-Coated Retriever's short, rough double coat, keeping out water and standing up to thorns. Paired with a wedge-shaped head, that coat sets this versatile Sporting gundog apart from other retrievers. Adults stand 25 inches tall and weigh 80 pounds, combining strength and endurance with an easy grace.
In character, this is a confident, dignified dog that thinks for itself. It is intelligent and independent, yet still straightforward to train for owners who enjoy working with a retriever that has a mind of its own.
Indoors, the Curly-Coated Retriever is gentle and very affectionate with its family, including children, and it has a lively sense of fun. Around strangers it stays more reserved than Labradors and Golden Retrievers, which makes it a watchful, protective guard. It adapts easily to different households.
Built for hard work outside, this dog needs a lot of daily activity and quickly gets bored if it isn't kept moving. Coat care is very simple for such a big breed: it rarely needs grooming, sheds very little and barely drools. Its lifespan is 10 years, on the shorter side among dog breeds.

general.name: Kerry Blue Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Kerry Blue Terrier is a vigilant, intelligent terrier from Ireland with a wavy, rough coat.
general.longDescription:
Bred in County Kerry, Ireland, the Kerry Blue Terrier handled all kinds of farm work before becoming a family companion and watchdog. It stands 20 inches tall, weighs 35 pounds and has a muscular, well-developed body. Its single coat is wavy and rough, in shades from deep slate to light blue-grey. A beard and dark, expressive eyes give its terrier head plenty of character.
At home, this intelligent terrier is very affectionate with its family and gets along well with children. Strong protective instincts and frequent barking make it a sharp watchdog that notices visitors quickly. Around other dogs it is less comfortable, as it is not naturally sociable with them. It doesn't drool much either.
Living with a Kerry Blue Terrier takes real time and energy. It needs regular daily exercise and plenty of mental stimulation to stay content, and training goes best with steady patience. Even though it sheds very little, its coat still needs consistent grooming to keep its texture and appearance. With a lifespan of 14 years, it is a long-term companion for an active household.

general.name: Norfolk Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Norfolk Terrier is a brave, playful little terrier with folded ears and an active streak.
general.longDescription:
You can tell a Norfolk Terrier from its close relative, the Norwich Terrier, by its folded ears rather than erect, pointed ones. At 10 inches tall and 12 pounds, it has a toy-sized frame, but its temperament is pure terrier. It is brave, confident and eager to hunt rodents if it gets the chance.
Its short, rough, straight wire double coat is hard and sturdy, ready for outdoor outings. Coat care stays simple because it needs little grooming, and it doesn't drool. With a lifespan of 15 years, it is a long-lived companion.
Around people, Norfolk Terriers are very warm. They bond closely with their families, do very well with children and welcome strangers easily. They still make alert watchdogs, though, with strong protective instincts and a habit of barking when something catches their eye.
These dogs adapt easily to different settings and travel well. They are playful and need plenty of exercise and mental stimulation every day, so active homes suit them best. Quiet days on the sofa won't be enough for a breed this energetic.

general.name: Pyrenean Mastiff
general.shortDescription: The Pyrenean Mastiff is a calm, brave 155-pound guardian bred to protect Spanish mountain livestock.
general.longDescription:
For centuries in the Pyrenees Mountains of Spain, the Pyrenean Mastiff protected livestock from wolves, bears and thieves. It is a giant dog, standing 30 inches tall and weighing 155 pounds, with a straight, rough double coat. Brave and dignified, it keeps a calm manner even when on watch.
Those guarding instincts remain very strong. This breed stays alert to anything out of place and barks often to warn its household. With its own family, though, it is loving and gentle. It does well with children, gets along easily with other dogs and has a low prey drive that lets it live peacefully beside other animals.
Day to day, a Pyrenean Mastiff doesn't need much exercise or mental stimulation, which suits a quieter home. Its independent streak makes training a challenge. You should also expect heavy drooling and plenty of shedding. Its lifespan is 10 years, which is shorter than many breeds.

general.name: English Toy Spaniel
general.shortDescription: The English Toy Spaniel is a quiet, affectionate 10-pound companion in four silky coat colours.
general.longDescription:
Often called the ETS, the English Toy Spaniel was bred to keep kings company and still likes staying close to its favoured people. It is happy, intelligent and very affectionate at home. Families with children or other dogs are a strong match, because English Toy Spaniels are very friendly with both. They enjoy cuddling on the couch, and they also show a curious, exuberant side when exploring their surroundings or playing games.
At 10 inches tall and 10 pounds, this is a small companion dog with a large domed head, dark expressive eyes and long, lush ears. Its straight, silky double coat comes in four named colour varieties: Blenheim (red and white), King Charles (black and tan), Prince Charles (white, black and tan) and Ruby (solid red). The coat needs regular grooming to stay in good shape.
Around the house, this spaniel is easy to live with. It adapts well to different households, barks very little and doesn't drool much. One practical point to know before bringing one home is its lifespan of 10 years, which is shorter than many other breeds.

general.name: Dandie Dinmont Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Dandie Dinmont Terrier is an independent, dignified terrier with a baritone bark.
general.longDescription:
Short legs and a long, low body give the Dandie Dinmont Terrier a distinctive shape. It stands 10 inches tall and weighs 20 pounds, with the sturdy build of a terrier bred for extermination work on farms. Its large head is covered in silky white hair, with round expressive eyes and long feathered ears. The wavy, rough double coat comes in two colours, pepper or mustard.
Away from the farm, Dandies suit city living too and keep a calmer demeanour than many other small dogs. They are dignified, brave and independent, with bright, intelligent expressions. At home they are affectionate with their families, and they are friendly towards strangers too. Strong protective instincts still make them reliable watchdogs, especially with that deep baritone bark.
Despite its independent streak, a Dandie Dinmont Terrier is relatively easy to train and responds best to positive, motivational methods. It doesn't drool and sheds very little, so there isn't much mess to clean up around the house. Its lifespan is 14 years, which is longer than many breeds.

general.name: Clumber Spaniel
general.shortDescription: The Clumber Spaniel is a quiet, affectionate Sporting dog built for thick cover.
general.longDescription:
At home, the Clumber Spaniel is polite, gentle and amusing, with a relaxed manner that makes it an easy housemate. Outdoors, that unhurried side gives way to a relentless nose. Historically favoured by kings as a hunting companion, it flushes game and moves freely through thick cover, and it also enjoys swimming and fetching.
Built long and low with heavy bones and a massive head, this Sporting dog stands 20 inches tall and weighs 70 pounds. Its dense coat is wavy, silky and mainly white, with sparse lemon or orange markings. You won't spend much time on grooming, because its coat needs little upkeep, though heavy drooling is part of life with the breed. It has an expected lifespan of 10 years.
Clumber Spaniels are affectionate with their families and friendly towards strangers, so visitors usually get a warm reception. They rarely bark and adapt well to different living arrangements. Smart and eager to please, they take well to training.

general.name: Volpino Italiano
general.shortDescription: Standing 11 inches tall, the Volpino Italiano bonds closely with family while staying cautious around strangers.
general.longDescription:
Italian breeders saved the Volpino Italiano from near extinction in the 1960s after interest in the breed faded. Its old Italian lineage also helped shape the toy-sized American Eskimo Dog. This small Companion breed stands 11 inches tall, weighs 12 pounds and typically lives around 14 years.
The Volpino Italiano is lively and demands plenty of mental stimulation. It enjoys running and agility training, then gladly curls up on a lap once playtime is over. That warmth belongs almost entirely to its own household. It is deeply affectionate and faithful with family, but strongly reserved around strangers. It also dislikes upheaval and doesn't adapt easily to new environments or sudden shifts in routine.
Care around the house is straightforward. Even though its straight, rough coat is long, it sheds lightly and rarely needs grooming. This breed doesn't drool and seldom barks. Give it a predictable home and regular brainwork, and the Volpino Italiano is a devoted, engaging housemate.

general.name: Komondor
general.shortDescription: Long white cords cover the Komondor, a brave Hungarian Working dog bred to guard flocks.
general.longDescription:
A Komondor treats protecting its household as a full-time job. Bred in Hungary to guard flocks, this brave, dignified Working dog stays highly alert to its surroundings and deeply faithful to its people. Its vigilance shapes daily life, so it fits best with owners who understand guardian breeds.
At 25 inches tall and 90 pounds, the Komondor has a deep chest and a muscular build. Even at that size, it stays agile and light-footed, moving across open ground with long, easy strides. Its expected lifespan is around 10 years.
Its coat is made of long, rough white cords that resemble dreadlocks and grow from head to tail. Although the Komondor barely sheds and drools little, that corded coat demands frequent grooming, so upkeep takes real commitment.
Within the family, Komondorok are faithful and deeply affectionate. They aren't especially sociable with other dogs, which is worth planning for on walks and visits. Despite an independent, strong-willed streak, they respond well to training and suit owners ready for a serious guardian dog.

general.name: American Leopard Hound
general.shortDescription: The American Leopard Hound tracks game for miles, pairing high stamina with a loud voice.
general.longDescription:
Built for hard work in extreme weather, the American Leopard Hound is a U.S. tree dog that hunts game ranging from raccoon to bear and cougar. It is intelligent, lively and capable of following prey for miles. With high exercise needs and a constant appetite for mental stimulation, this Hound fits best with active owners or dedicated hunters.
Standing 25 inches tall and weighing 55 pounds, it has a long expected lifespan of 14 years. Its short, smooth, straight coat comes in Solid, Leopard and Brindle patterns across 9 official colours. Coat care takes almost no effort, because it rarely needs grooming and doesn't drool.
This breed gets on very well with children and other dogs, and it adapts easily to new routines and environments. Around unfamiliar people, however, it stays very cautious and strongly protective, particularly where children are concerned.
Expect plenty of noise, because the American Leopard Hound barks frequently. That voice is worth weighing if you share walls or live close to neighbours. For active families or hunters who can supply daily exercise and mental work, it is a tough, adaptable partner.

general.name: Lapponian Herder
general.shortDescription: Give a Lapponian Herder daily exercise and mental work, and you get a devoted, vocal Herding partner.
general.longDescription:
At 20 inches tall and 70 pounds, the Lapponian Herder wears a short, straight, rough double coat that needs little grooming. Its colours include grey-brown and black with lighter undercoats, often paired with white or tan markings. It doesn't drool much and typically lives around 12 years.
This Herding breed brings high energy and a strong work ethic. Beyond herding, it takes on a range of tasks and dog sports, including companion events. Because it needs plenty of daily exercise and regular mental challenges, it does best when given steady jobs to focus on.
Smart and eager to please, the Lapponian Herder responds well to training even with its independent streak. Early socialisation is important because of its herding mentality. Expect a vocal housemate, too, since this breed barks frequently and often uses its voice while working.
Once its physical and mental needs are met, the Lapponian Herder adapts well to different living arrangements. It stays alert and protective while forming deeply affectionate bonds with its family. For active owners who enjoy training and don't mind a noisy companion, this friendly, lively dog makes an engaging partner.

general.name: Lancashire Heeler
general.shortDescription: The Lancashire Heeler is a small, affectionate herding dog used for cattle work, rabbiting and ratting.
general.longDescription:
Used for herding cattle as well as rabbiting and ratting, the Lancashire Heeler packs a lot of working drive into a small frame. This sturdy dog from the Herding group stands about 10 inches tall and weighs 13 pounds, pairing herding energy with terrier instincts.
The Lancashire Heeler has a short, straight, smooth double coat that holds up well in bad weather. Colours are usually black and tan or liver and tan. It needs very little grooming and barely drools, though you can expect moderate shedding.
At home, it is very affectionate and gets along well with children, other dogs and most strangers. One quirk is the Heeler Smile, an expression of contentment that looks like a human grin. With a lifespan of about 14 years, it stays with a family for a long stretch.
You'll need to keep this dog busy. It has high exercise needs and wants plenty of mental work, along with a playful streak. Because it is intelligent and fairly easy to train, daily walks and regular training sessions suit it well.
Lancashire Heelers adapt well to different homes, though they aren't quiet dogs. They bark fairly often and stay moderately alert to what happens around the house, so anyone with close neighbours should expect a vocal dog that lets you know when someone is at the door.

general.name: Plott Hound
general.shortDescription: The Plott Hound is North Carolina's state dog, a vigilant brindle scenthound built for hunting.
general.longDescription:
North Carolina's state dog, the Plott Hound is a fearless scenthound from the Hound group with a streamlined, light-footed build and a long tail. It stands around 20 inches tall, weighs about 50 pounds and has a typical lifespan of 13 years.
Its smooth, straight single coat is short and comes in brindle colours, ranging from black flecked with gold to bright oranges and russets. A black nose, lips and eye rims set off its confident, inquisitive expression. Grooming takes very little work, shedding is light and drooling stays low.
At home, the Plott Hound settles into a gentle, loyal and very affectionate companion. It gets along very well with other dogs and is friendly towards strangers. It is generally fine around children, and while it enjoys a game, its playfulness sits in the middle.
This is an active dog that needs plenty of daily exercise alongside moderate mental stimulation. It adapts well to different homes and is fairly easy to train thanks to its intelligence. Plott Hounds are vigilant watchdogs and frequent barkers, so you should expect a dog that alerts you loudly to anything unusual.

general.name: German Spitz
general.shortDescription: The German Spitz is a lively, intelligent companion dog with a thick ruff and loud bark.
general.longDescription:
A foxy head, small pointed ears, a full neck ruff and a bushy tail carried over the back give the German Spitz a distinctive look. This lively, faithful dog from the Companion group stands about 15 inches tall and weighs 30 pounds, wearing a long, straight, rough double coat with a thick undercoat.
Although faithful to its owner, this breed is independent and reserved rather than cuddly. It is very wary of strangers and doesn't have much of a hunting instinct. Moderately alert and very noisy, the German Spitz barks a lot, so you'll hear about most things moving outside.
A German Spitz is intelligent and very easy to train, which helps because it needs a lot of daily mental work. It is playful and gets by on moderate exercise rather than endless runs. Its adaptability sits in the middle, so a steady routine suits it best.
With good training and socialisation, it can live comfortably with children and get on fairly well with other dogs. The thick coat sheds a fair amount and needs regular brushing to keep it tidy, though the breed barely drools. It is a long-lived dog, with a typical lifespan of 15 years.

general.name: Alaskan Klee Kai
general.shortDescription: The Alaskan Klee Kai is a small, vigilant companion dog of Arctic heritage.
general.longDescription:
With its wedge-shaped head, upright triangular ears and symmetrical contrasting coat markings in three colour varieties, the Alaskan Klee Kai wears its Arctic heritage clearly. This well-proportioned dog from the Companion group stands 15 inches tall, weighs 15 pounds and moves with a smooth, agile gait.
This breed is faithful to its household and moderately affectionate, though it is very reserved with strangers and unfamiliar situations. It stays watchful around the home without being overly protective. Around other dogs it is very sociable, and it gets along decently with children.
Day to day, the Alaskan Klee Kai has balanced needs. It wants moderate exercise, playtime and mental work, and it barks only a moderate amount. Although intelligent, training takes steady effort, and it adapts at a measured pace.
Its straight, rough, medium-length double coat sheds a fair amount and needs regular brushing, though this breed doesn't drool. With a typical lifespan of 15 years, an Alaskan Klee Kai suits owners who appreciate a faithful dog that takes time to warm up to new people.

general.name: Bluetick Coonhound
general.shortDescription: The Bluetick Coonhound is a hardworking nocturnal hunting hound with a mottled glossy coat.
general.longDescription:
The Bluetick Coonhound is a nocturnal hunter that tracks quarry with high prey drive, persistence and bold focus. It is easy to spot by its droopy ears and glossy, black-and-blue mottled coat. A compact, agile member of the Hound group, it stands around 25 inches tall, weighs about 60 pounds and has a typical lifespan of 12 years.
Coon hunters value its melodious baying, though frequent barking and baying can be hard on suburban neighbours. At home, a Bluetick Coonhound is faithful and moderately affectionate. It is only moderately playful and has low protective instincts, so it isn't much of a guard dog. It is very sociable with other dogs and usually gets on fine with children and strangers.
This intelligent hound is fairly easy to train and adapts moderately well to different homes and routines. Because it is built to work, it needs plenty of daily exercise and steady mental stimulation to prevent boredom and unwanted behaviour. Its short, straight, smooth single coat sheds a moderate amount and needs only light grooming. Drooling stays low, so basic upkeep takes little effort.

general.name: Portuguese Podengo Pequeno
general.shortDescription: The Portuguese Podengo Pequeno is a small, lively hound bred to hunt rabbits.
general.longDescription:
The Portuguese Podengo Pequeno is a small hound and one of Portugal's three Podengo breeds, originally bred to hunt rabbits. Standing 10 inches tall and weighing 10 pounds, it is quick and athletic with a lifespan of 14 years. It has a wedge-shaped head, almond-shaped eyes and upright, pointed ears that give it a curious look.
Its short single coat is smooth or wiry and sheds a moderate amount, though it only needs occasional grooming. It doesn't drool. Because it is a lively, active hound, it needs plenty of daily exercise and mental stimulation to stay occupied. Training is moderately challenging, so regular practice helps.
At home, the Portuguese Podengo Pequeno is happy, playful and very affectionate with its family. It gets on very well with children and other dogs, and it adapts well to most living situations. With strangers it is moderately friendly, and both its barking and its protective instincts are moderate. It is a companionable dog that enjoys spending time outdoors with its people.

general.name: Stumpy
general.shortDescription: The Stumpy is a lively, vigilant herding dog with a naturally bobbed tail and high energy.
general.longDescription:
The Stumpy is a sturdy, athletic herding dog born with a naturally bobbed tail. People often mistake it for an Australian Cattle Dog with a docked tail, though it is a separate breed. It stands 20 inches tall, weighs 40 pounds and has a lifespan of 14 years.
This is a lively, hardworking dog with very high needs for both physical exercise and mental work. Daily walks alone won't be enough, so it needs active time outdoors and regular tasks to keep its mind busy. It is obedient, though training is moderately challenging and works best with steady, structured sessions.
The Stumpy is reserved, even with its own family, and isn't a particularly affectionate dog. It is cautious around strangers and doesn't generally get along with other dogs, while its tolerance for children is moderate. It is vigilant and moderately protective, yet it rarely barks.
Its short, rough, straight double coat sheds a moderate amount and takes regular brushing to maintain. It doesn't drool. Playfulness and adaptability are both moderate, so the Stumpy suits an active household that can meet its high energy needs and is comfortable with a reserved dog.

general.name: Skye Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Skye Terrier is a brave, relaxed terrier from Scotland with a long, low build.
general.longDescription:
Originally bred as an exterminator on Scotland's Isle of Skye, the Skye Terrier has a long, low, level profile. It is muscular and substantial, standing 10 inches tall and weighing 40 pounds, with short legs, a deep chest and a body twice as long as its height. Its lifespan is 13 years.
Its long, straight, rough double coat lies flat and hangs over its eyes, framed by either large, feathered upright ears or drop ears that lie flat. It sheds a fair amount and needs regular brushing to keep the coat tidy, though it doesn't drool. Daily walks, a bit of mental work and steady, patient training are usually enough to keep it happy without demanding hours of activity.
At home, the Skye Terrier is brave, intelligent and relaxed, and it is very affectionate with its own family. It gets along reasonably well with strangers, children and other dogs, though it isn't overly outgoing. It barks now and then, keeps a watchful eye on the house, and enjoys a game without being constantly on the go. Because its energy is balanced, it settles into both active and quieter households.

general.name: Teddy Roosevelt Terrier
general.shortDescription: The Teddy Roosevelt Terrier is a happy, adaptable small terrier bred to hunt vermin.
general.longDescription:
The Teddy Roosevelt Terrier is a small, sturdy terrier originally bred to hunt squirrels and vermin. It stands 10 inches tall, weighs 15 pounds and has a lifespan of 15 years. Intelligent, happy and very adaptable, it adjusts easily to life in a flat or on a farm.
At home, it bonds closely with its family and is very affectionate. It gets on very well with children and other dogs, and it does well with cats when raised alongside them. Around strangers, however, it is reserved and cautious. Its protective instincts and barking are both moderate.
Its hunting background gives it boldness and solid endurance for outdoor tasks, and it keeps a prey drive without becoming obsessive. Even so, it doesn't need endless exercise or constant entertainment. Daily walks paired with agility, obedience or a game in the garden keep its mind and body busy, and it learns well with steady training.
Coat care is straightforward. The Teddy Roosevelt Terrier has a short, smooth, straight single coat that rarely needs grooming. It still sheds a moderate amount, so an occasional brush helps, and it doesn't drool.
Because it is so adaptable and has manageable daily needs, the Teddy Roosevelt Terrier suits many different homes. It is eager to join in whatever its owners are doing, from structured training to relaxing with the family. Prospective owners just need to bear in mind its caution around unfamiliar people.

general.name: Tosa
general.shortDescription: The Tosa is a large, brave working dog with strong protective instincts.
general.longDescription:
The Tosa, also known as the Tosa Ken or Japanese Mastiff, is a heavy working dog standing 23 inches tall and weighing 150 pounds. Originally bred for fighting, it is now kept as a watchdog. It matures slowly, often not reaching its prime until around 4 years of age, and has a lifespan of 10 years.
With its own family, the Tosa is very affectionate, patient and tolerant, rarely showing aggression towards humans. It is brave, vigilant and strongly protective, with a territorial streak that leaves it aloof with strangers and wary of other dogs. It isn't overly vocal or boisterous, gets on reasonably well with children, and is best suited to experienced owners.
Its short, smooth, straight double coat comes in fawn, red, apricot, black and brindle. It needs very little grooming and sheds lightly, though it can drool a fair bit. It adjusts reasonably well to different routines and doesn't demand extreme exercise, but it needs regular mental work and steady, consistent training alongside its daily walks.

general.name: Azawakh
general.shortDescription: The Azawakh is a lean West African sighthound bred to chase gazelle.
general.longDescription:
The Azawakh is a sighthound from West Africa, native to Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger. Standing around 25 inches tall and weighing about 45 pounds, it has a deep chest, a narrow head and a lean frame where bone and muscle show beneath its short, smooth single coat. Colours include red, fawn, brindle, parti-colour, blue, black and brown, often with white markings.
Bred to hunt gazelle across the Sahara, the Azawakh is tough, fast and keen-eyed. In the United States it now works in lure coursing and lives as a guardian and companion. It bonds faithfully with its own household and rarely barks or drools, though it remains guarded around strangers.
That fine coat sheds lightly and needs only occasional grooming. Moderate daily exercise and mental work suit the breed, and it adapts reasonably well to new routines. Azawakhs are moderately protective and get along fairly well with children and other dogs, while their independent nature makes training challenging. Most live around 14 years.

general.name: Puggle
general.shortDescription: The Puggle is a playful, sociable Pug and Beagle cross with a smooth coat and lively curiosity.
general.longDescription:
Bred from the Pug and the Beagle, the Puggle stands about 14 inches tall and weighs 20 pounds. It has a wrinkled face, expressive eyes and a short, smooth single coat in several colours.
Puggles are affectionate, playful and great with children and other dogs, as well as friendly with strangers. They inherit Beagle curiosity and adapt easily to new homes, though moderate barking means early training helps.
Grooming is light, yet the short coat sheds heavily. Puggles need plenty of daily exercise and mental work. Training takes moderate effort, and most live around 14 years.

general.name: Chiweenie
general.shortDescription: The Chiweenie is a lively, vocal cross of Chihuahua and Dachshund that bonds closely with its owners.
general.longDescription:
The Chiweenie crosses the Chihuahua with the Dachshund. Standing about 7 inches tall and weighing 13 pounds, it has the Dachshund's long body and a straight, smooth single coat.
Devoted to its family, this lively lap dog has a playful, sometimes feisty attitude. It gets along well with other dogs and adapts easily to flat living, though it is protective and less suited to young children.
Plan for frequent barking and high daily exercise needs despite its small size. Shedding and grooming stay light, training takes moderate effort and gentle socialisation helps around strangers. Most live about 15 years.

general.name: Labradoodle
general.shortDescription: A Labrador Retriever and Poodle cross, the Labradoodle is lively, friendly and trainable.
general.longDescription:
A cross between the Labrador Retriever and Poodle, the Labradoodle stands around 20 inches tall and weighs 63 pounds. It has a medium-length, straight, smooth double coat in several colours.
Gentle and very sociable, Labradoodles work well as family pets and therapy dogs. They are great with children, friendly with strangers and easily adaptable, though fairly vocal and protective.
Shedding is moderate and brushing should be regular. These dogs need heavy daily exercise and lots of mental work, so active homes suit them best. Easy to train, they typically live around 14 years.

general.name: Goldendoodle
general.shortDescription: The Goldendoodle is a friendly, clever Golden Retriever and Poodle cross that learns fast.
general.longDescription:
Golden Retriever and Poodle parents give the Goldendoodle a long, wavy, silky double coat in several colours. Most stand about 20 inches tall and weigh 60 pounds.
Faithful, playful and sociable, Goldendoodles get on very well with children, strangers and other dogs. They adapt easily to most homes, bark moderately and do well in obedience training and therapy work.
Moderate shedding and regular brushing come with that long coat. Goldendoodles are very easy to train, but they need plenty of outdoor exercise and high daily mental stimulation to stay happy. Most live around 13 years.

general.name: Cockapoo
general.shortDescription: The Cockapoo crosses a Cocker Spaniel and Poodle into a friendly, active family dog.
general.longDescription:
The Cockapoo crosses a Cocker Spaniel and a Poodle into a cheerful, loving Sporting dog. It welcomes children, strangers and other dogs, suiting families, singles and older owners.
At 14 inches tall and 19 pounds, it lives about 14 years. Its long, wavy, silky double coat comes in varied colours and sheds lightly, though it needs frequent grooming.
Cockapoos are intelligent and straightforward to train, with high energy for daily walks and mental games. They settle easily into most homes, though you can expect a fair amount of barking.

general.name: Maltipoo
general.shortDescription: The Maltipoo is a small Maltese and Poodle cross with a loving nature and plenty of energy.
general.longDescription:
A Companion cross of Maltese and Poodle, the Maltipoo is a small, sturdy dog at 11 inches tall and 10 pounds. It settles easily into a flat or a house, and it bonds closely with its family.
Happy and eager to please, it picks up training quickly and needs plenty of daily exercise and mental activity. It is warm with children and visitors, more selective with other dogs and quick to bark when alert.
Expect a lifespan of about 15 years. Its long, straight, silky coat sheds very little, though frequent grooming is still needed to keep it tidy.

general.name: Pomsky
general.shortDescription: The Pomsky is a curious, noisy Pomeranian and Siberian Husky cross with high energy and a double coat.
general.longDescription:
Combining the Pomeranian and Siberian Husky, the Pomsky often shows Husky markings on a fairly long, rough double coat in many colours. Eyes can be brown, blue or one of each. Most measure 14 inches tall and 28 pounds, though size varies with the parents.
Expect a loud, lively Companion dog. Pomskies bark a lot, and their curious, brave nature calls for plenty of exercise and mental work. Training takes steady effort, whereas their moderate shedding and grooming are straightforward to keep up with.
They bond closely with their families, adapt well to most homes and get on with children, strangers and other dogs. Their lifespan is around 14 years.

general.name: Yorkipoo
general.shortDescription: Bred from the Yorkshire Terrier and Poodle, the Yorkipoo is a lively, adaptable dog with heavy grooming needs.
general.longDescription:
The Yorkipoo stands just 11 inches tall and weighs 10 pounds, yet this Yorkshire Terrier and Poodle cross demands a lot of upkeep. Its long, straight, silky coat sheds very little, but it requires very frequent brushing and trimming to prevent tangles.
Playful and curious, it needs lots of mental stimulation alongside plenty of daily exercise. Because this lively Companion dog is quick to learn and eager to please, training goes smoothly.
Yorkipoos adapt easily to flats or houses and live around 14 years. They adore family, children and strangers, stay a bit reserved with other dogs and are vocal when on watch.

general.name: Schnoodle
general.shortDescription: Friendly and very easy to train, the Schnoodle is a playful, vocal Terrier cross of Schnauzer and Poodle.
general.longDescription:
Bred from the Schnauzer and Poodle, the Schnoodle is an intelligent, obedient Terrier that takes well to obedience and agility work. Very easy to train and full of play, it suits active homes able to meet its high need for exercise and mental challenges.
Friendly and affectionate, it adapts smoothly to almost any home, suiting families, singles or older owners. It is great with children and welcoming to strangers, though less keen on other dogs. Be ready for noise, because this alert dog barks a lot.
The Schnoodle measures 13 inches tall, weighs 14 pounds and lives about 15 years. Its rough, wiry double coat sheds lightly, but it still needs frequent grooming to stay in good condition.

general.name: Cavapoo
general.shortDescription: The Cavapoo crosses a Cavalier King Charles Spaniel with a Poodle, making a small, outgoing companion suited to family life.
general.longDescription:
Cavapoos want company and warm quickly to children, strangers and other dogs. They live comfortably with families, singles and older owners, adapting well to different homes, though they tend to bark a fair amount.
Bred from the Cavalier King Charles Spaniel and Poodle, this Companion dog stands 13 inches tall, weighs 14 pounds and has a lifespan of 15 years. Its long, wavy coat feels silky and comes in various colours. Shedding and drooling both stay low.
Cavapoos are eager to please and easy to train. For such a small dog, they need plenty of exercise and mental activity, and they enjoy regular walks and games like fetch.

general.name: Morkie
general.shortDescription: Small enough for flat living, the Morkie blends the Maltese and Yorkshire Terrier into a bold, affectionate companion.
general.longDescription:
At 8 inches tall and 7 pounds, the Morkie is a tiny Companion dog with a lifespan of 14 years. Its straight, silky coat grows very long in various colours. It barely sheds or drools, but needs frequent grooming.
A mix of Maltese and Yorkshire Terrier, the Morkie is happy and bold, and it forms strong bonds with its family. Morkies get on well with children and strangers, yet stay sharply alert and quite vocal.
They settle easily into flats or smaller homes. Despite their size, they have plenty of energy and need regular playtime, short walks and mental stimulation each day.

general.name: Aussiedoodle
