general.shortDescription: Aussiedoodles pair the Australian Shepherd with the Poodle, producing an athletic, fast-learning herding dog for active households.
general.longDescription:
Aussiedoodles are hardworking dogs that need a great deal of daily exercise and mental stimulation. Very easy to train and keen to learn, they do well in obedience, agility and herding, suiting active families or individuals.
This Herding cross of Australian Shepherd and Poodle stands 18 inches tall, weighs 55 pounds and lives around 15 years. Its long, wavy double coat has a rough texture in varied colours and patterns. Shedding stays low and drooling is not an issue.
At home, they are playful, affectionate and especially good with children. They are friendly towards strangers and adapt well to new routines, while staying watchful and prone to barking.

general.name: Chorkie
general.shortDescription: Bold and very vocal, the Chorkie pairs the Chihuahua and Yorkshire Terrier into a tiny, watchful companion dog.
general.longDescription:
Chorkies pack a big-dog attitude into a small, delicate frame. Deeply affectionate and strongly protective, they make alert watchdogs and bark a lot, so noise is something to expect. They bond closely with their owners and are friendly towards strangers.
This Companion dog brings together the bold Chihuahua and playful Yorkshire Terrier. It stands 8 inches tall, weighs 6 pounds and has a lifespan of 14 years. Its long, straight single coat feels smooth and sheds lightly, with almost no drooling.
Chorkies are very adaptable and suit flat living well, provided they have a loving home. Lively and playful, they still need plenty of daily activity and mental stimulation through short walks and interactive play.

general.name: Pitsky
general.shortDescription: A Pit Bull and Siberian Husky mix, the Pitsky is a muscular, friendly dog with plenty of energy.
general.longDescription:
Confident and deeply affectionate, Pitskies bond closely with their families and greet strangers warmly. They are playful, adaptable and generally good with children and other dogs, especially with proper socialisation. Expect a fair bit of barking, though.
Active homes suit this breed best. Pitskies have high energy and need plenty of daily exercise and mental stimulation. Intelligent and eager to please, they do well with consistent training.
A Terrier cross of Pit Bull and Siberian Husky, the Pitsky is muscular and often shows Husky eyes and coat markings. It stands 19 inches tall, weighs 55 pounds and lives around 14 years. Its short, straight single coat feels smooth and needs little grooming, and it is not a drooler.

general.name: Goldador
general.shortDescription: Bred from the Golden Retriever and Labrador Retriever, the Goldador is an energetic Sporting dog that trains easily.
general.longDescription:
The Goldador crosses the Golden Retriever and Labrador Retriever in the Sporting group. Intelligent and easy to train, these dogs regularly work in service, therapy and search and rescue.
At home, a Goldador is faithful, playful and quick to settle into family routines. They are warm with children, welcoming to strangers and happy around other dogs, without barking much. Sturdy and athletic, most reach 25 inches tall and weigh around 68 pounds, carrying a wavy, silky double coat in yellow, gold or black.
With a lifespan of around 11 years, they need plenty of daily exercise and mental work, so hiking, swimming and fetch suit them well. Grooming stays light, though that double coat sheds heavily.

general.name: Bernedoodle
general.shortDescription: Friendly and playful, the Bernedoodle crosses the Bernese Mountain Dog and Poodle and needs daily exercise and frequent grooming.
general.longDescription:
Bred from the Bernese Mountain Dog and Poodle, the Bernedoodle is a Working dog that likes being part of daily family life. Affectionate and playful, they take easily to children and greet strangers warmly, while staying relaxed indoors.
They are brave and watchful, and they bark fairly often. Most are sociable with other dogs and adapt well to change. Training is straightforward, so they do well in obedience and agility when given daily exercise and mental work.
At 20 inches tall and 73 pounds, the Bernedoodle carries a long, straight, rough double coat. You can expect a lifespan of around 12 years. The coat sheds moderately and needs frequent grooming, though drooling stays low.

general.name: Shorkie
general.shortDescription: At 10 pounds, the Shorkie is a loving Shih Tzu and Yorkshire Terrier cross that needs constant grooming.
general.longDescription:
The Shorkie is a Companion cross of the Shih Tzu and Yorkshire Terrier, standing just 9 inches tall and weighing 10 pounds. Its long, straight, silky double coat often mixes colours from both parents. Shedding is very low and drooling isn't an issue, but the coat needs very frequent grooming to prevent tangles.
They settle easily into flats and bond closely with singles, seniors or families. Happy and playful, Shorkies enjoy company from children, visitors and other dogs. For such a small breed, they are alert and bark fairly often.
Most live around 14 years, and despite their size they need daily exercise, interactive play and mental work. They are clever but can turn stubborn, so consistent training matters.

general.name: Boxador
general.shortDescription: The Boxador, a Working cross of Boxer and Labrador Retriever, is a playful dog with very high energy.
general.longDescription:
Exercise is the main commitment with a Boxador. This Working cross of Boxer and Labrador Retriever brings very high energy and strong mental needs, so daily running, hiking or long games of fetch suit them best. Strong and athletic, they grow to around 25 inches tall and 68 pounds.
At home, Boxadors are lively, playful and deeply affectionate. They adapt well to family life, do well with children and greet new people warmly, while getting along with other dogs. Alert and protective, they also make capable watchdogs.
They are intelligent and eager to please, picking up new tricks readily. Their short, straight, smooth single coat needs little grooming, though expect moderate shedding and drooling. Boxadors typically live about 11 years.

general.name: Bullmatian
general.shortDescription: A Bulldog and Dalmatian cross, the Bullmatian is a muscular, affectionate dog with high energy and heavy shedding.
general.longDescription:
The Bullmatian brings together the sturdy Bulldog and the Dalmatian in the Companion group. Muscular at 18 inches tall and 53 pounds, they have a short, straight, smooth single coat that often shows Dalmatian spots.
Affectionate, playful and relaxed with their family, Bullmatians are also brave and protective. They warm to strangers easily, though early socialisation helps around children and other dogs. High energy and strong mental needs mean they want daily exercise and space to run.
Most live around 11 years, pick up training readily and adapt well to household routines. Even with a short coat, expect heavy shedding and moderate grooming.

general.name: Doxiepoo
general.shortDescription: The Doxiepoo is a small, lively Dachshund and Poodle cross with plenty of affection and a loud bark.
general.longDescription:
The Doxiepoo crosses a Dachshund with a Poodle and sits in the Hound group. Averaging 10 inches tall and 17 pounds, it has a long, smooth coat and lives around 15 years.
Frequent barking is part of living with a Doxiepoo, because it stays very alert. It learns quickly, though a Dachshund stubborn streak calls for steady consistency. It is playful, deeply affectionate with its family, warm with strangers and good with children and other dogs.
Shedding stays light, and moderate brushing keeps the straight single coat tidy. Flats and larger homes both suit the Doxiepoo well, as long as it gets plenty of daily exercise and mental work.

general.name: Corgipoo
general.shortDescription: A small, loving Corgi and Poodle cross, the Corgipoo needs regular exercise and plenty of daily mental work.
general.longDescription:
A small Herding dog bred from the Corgi and Poodle, the Corgipoo averages 12 inches tall and 22 pounds. Many inherit the Corgi's long body under a rough, medium-length double coat. It lives around 14 years and doesn't drool.
Vigilant and quick to learn, the Corgipoo takes well to obedience and agility work, though those watchful instincts also mean fairly frequent barking. It bonds closely with its family, plays hard, greets strangers warmly and gets on well with children and other dogs.
High mental stimulation needs and active daily exercise are the main commitment. Once those are met, it settles into most homes. Expect moderate shedding and steady brushing to keep tangles out of its straight coat.

general.name: Sheepadoodle
general.shortDescription: The Sheepadoodle is a loving Old English Sheepdog and Poodle cross with high watchfulness and a long, wavy coat.
general.longDescription:
Standing about 18 inches tall and weighing 68 pounds, the Sheepadoodle is a medium Herding dog bred from the Old English Sheepdog and Poodle. Its long, wavy double coat has a rough texture. It drools lightly and lives about 13 years.
Strong protective instincts keep this breed alert and fairly vocal, and it is only moderately sociable with other dogs. With people it is very affectionate, playful, great with children and friendly towards most strangers. Because it learns quickly, training and new tricks usually go smoothly.
Hiking, fetch and lots of daily mental work suit this active breed well, and with that routine it settles easily into most homes. Shedding stays low, though that long coat needs frequent grooming to prevent tangles.

general.name: Cheagle
general.shortDescription: Lively and loud, the Cheagle crosses a Chihuahua with a Beagle and brings plenty of daily energy.
general.longDescription:
Part Chihuahua and part Beagle, the Cheagle is a Companion dog averaging 11 inches tall and 15 pounds. Its short, smooth coat often blends the colouring of both parent breeds. It lives around 14 years and doesn't drool.
Curious like a Beagle and bold like a Chihuahua, it bonds closely with its family and gets on well with other dogs. Because it can be cautious around children and strangers, early socialisation helps alongside patient training to manage frequent barking.
Active homes suit this energetic cross best, giving it plenty of daily exercise and mental work. It adjusts well to different spaces. Shedding is moderate, though the straight single coat needs little grooming.

general.name: Springador
general.shortDescription: A friendly Springer Spaniel and Labrador Retriever cross, the Springador trains easily and has high daily exercise needs.
general.longDescription:
In the Sporting group, the Springador pairs the Springer Spaniel with the Labrador Retriever in a sturdy, medium build of 23 inches and 58 pounds. It has a short, silky double coat in various colours and lives about 13 years.
Friendly and happy, it greets strangers warmly, loves other dogs and gets on well with children. Watchfulness and barking stay moderate. Very easy to train, it takes readily to obedience work and outdoor activities like hiking, swimming or fetch.
Expect heavy shedding and moderate drooling, though the wavy coat needs little grooming. Give it plenty of vigorous daily exercise and steady mental work, and it adapts easily to most homes.

general.name: Shihpoo
general.shortDescription: The Shihpoo is a small Shih Tzu and Poodle cross that loves family company and needs regular exercise.
general.longDescription:
The Shihpoo crosses a Shih Tzu with a Poodle in a small Companion dog of 12 inches and 13 pounds. Its long, straight double coat feels silky and sheds very little, though it needs frequent grooming.
Shihpoos are happy, affectionate dogs that adapt easily to families, singles and older owners. They get on well with children, other dogs and strangers, though they bark often.
For a small dog, they need plenty of daily exercise, interactive play and mental activity. Training is fairly straightforward if you start early, and they live about 15 years.

general.name: Bordoodle
general.shortDescription: The Bordoodle is an active Border Collie and Poodle cross that learns fast and needs plenty of exercise and work.
general.longDescription:
A Herding group cross of Border Collie and Poodle, the Bordoodle is a lively, intelligent dog that needs daily work. It has high needs for exercise and mental stimulation, and does well in obedience, agility and other dog sports. Easy to train and quick to learn, it suits active, experienced owners with time for regular tasks.
At 18 inches tall and 50 pounds, this medium dog lives about 15 years. Its fairly long, wavy double coat feels rough, sheds lightly and needs frequent grooming to stop tangles.
Bordoodles are playful, loving dogs that bond closely with their families and welcome strangers warmly. They adapt easily, do well with children and are moderately sociable with other dogs. They stay alert and bark often.

general.name: Cockalier
general.shortDescription: The Cockalier crosses the Cocker Spaniel and Cavalier King Charles Spaniel into an affectionate, sociable dog that needs plenty of exercise.
general.longDescription:
Cockaliers combine the Cocker Spaniel and Cavalier King Charles Spaniel into a happy, loving Sporting dog that suits families, singles and older owners. They get on very well with children and other dogs, greet strangers warmly and settle into flats or larger houses.
They are small-to-medium dogs of about 14 inches and 20 pounds, living around 13 years. Their fairly long, wavy double coat is silky and comes in several colours, with moderate shedding and regular grooming.
Give a Cockalier plenty of daily exercise, plus some playtime and mental work. This intelligent cross is fairly easy to train and enjoys a moderately playful routine at home.

general.name: Cavachon
general.shortDescription: Bred from the Cavalier King Charles Spaniel and Bichon Frise, the Cavachon is a small, friendly companion with a silky coat.
general.longDescription:
Bred from the Cavalier King Charles Spaniel and Bichon Frise, the Cavachon is a Companion dog that loves being around people. It greets children, strangers and other dogs warmly, and adapts well to families, singles and older owners. It has a dignified side alongside a playful streak.
Despite weighing 15 pounds and standing 12 inches tall, the Cavachon needs plenty of daily exercise and playtime, plus moderate mental activity. Training is fairly easy.
Its fairly long single coat is wavy and silky. Shedding stays light, though the coat needs frequent grooming to stay in good shape. Cavachons live about 15 years.
